question: What Electoral Division in Victoria contained a suburb of Melbourne with a population of 25,147 at the 2016 Census?
context:
[d09p000] South Yarra, Victoria
[d09s000] South Yarra is an inner suburb of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, 4 km south-east of Melbourne's Central Business District, located within the Cities of Melbourne and Stonnington local government areas. South Yarra recorded a population of 25,147 at the 2016 Census.

[d03p000] Fitzroy, Victoria
[d03s000] Fitzroy is an inner-city suburb of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, 3 km north-east of Melbourne's Central Business District in the local government area of the City of Yarra.
[d03s001] At the 2016 Census, Fitzroy had a population of 10,445.
[d03s002] Planned as Melbourne's first suburb, it was later also one of the city's first areas to gain municipal status.

[d06p000] Division of Maribyrnong
[d06s000] The Division of Maribyrnong is an Australian Electoral Division in the state of Victoria.
[d06s001] It is located in the inner north-western suburbs of Melbourne.
[d06s002] It covers the suburbs of Aberfeldie, Airport West, Avondale Heights, Braybrook, Essendon, Kealba, Keilor East, Maribyrnong, Moonee Ponds, Niddrie, St. Albans and Sunshine North.

[d07p000] Division of McMillan
[d07s000] The Division of McMillan is an Australian Electoral Division in the state of Victoria.
[d07s001] It is located in the western part of the Gippsland region, which extends for the length of Victoria's eastern Bass Strait coastline.
[d07s002] It includes the outer south-eastern Melbourne suburb of Pakenham, and also includes the towns of Warragul, Moe, Wonthaggi, Leongatha and Foster.

[d02p000] Division of Hotham
[d02s000] The Division of Hotham is an Australian Electoral Division in Victoria.
[d02s001] The division was created in 1969 and is named for Sir Charles Hotham, Governor of Victoria 1854–55.
[d02s002] It is located in the south-eastern suburbs of Melbourne.

[d01p000] Division of Kooyong
[d01s000] The Division of Kooyong is an Australian Electoral Division in the state of Victoria.
[d01s001] The Division was proclaimed in 1900, and was one of the original 75 divisions to be contested at the first Federal election.
[d01s002] It covers an area of approximately 52 km2 in the inner-east suburbs of Melbourne.

[d08p003] Division of Fawkner
[d08s003] It was located in the inner southern suburbs of Melbourne, including at various times Prahran, South Yarra, St Kilda and Toorak.
[d08s004] It was usually a safe conservative seat, but was occasionally won by the Australian Labor Party.

[d06p003] Division of Maribyrnong
[d06s003] Due to redistributions, the division has been slowly moving west.
[d06s004] It originally covered the suburbs of Footscray and North Melbourne.
[d06s005] According to the 2011 census, Maribyrnong has the highest proportion of Catholics in any Commonwealth Electoral Division in Australia with 41.6% of the population.

[d02p003] Division of Hotham
[d02s003] Hotham covers an area of approximately 72 square kilometres from Oakleigh in the north to Dingley Village in the south.
[d02s004] The division includes the suburbs of Bentleigh East, Clarinda, Dingley Village, Heatherton and Moorabbin in their entirety, and parts of Clayton, Cheltenham, Hughesdale, Murrumbeena, Noble Park, Oakleigh, and Springvale.
[d02s005] Hotham is the only electorate in Victoria which does not have either a waterway or a body of water forming any part of its boundary.

[d03p003] Fitzroy, Victoria
[d03s003] It occupies Melbourne's smallest and most densely populated suburban area, just 100 ha.

question: Which opera has more acts, Parsifal or Manon by Massenet?
context:
[d07p000] Manon
[d07s000] Manon (] ) is an "opéra comique" in five acts by Jules Massenet to a French libretto by Henri Meilhac and Philippe Gille, based on the 1731 novel "L’histoire du chevalier des Grieux et de Manon Lescaut" by the Abbé Prévost.
[d07s001] It was first performed at the Opéra-Comique in Paris on 19 January 1884, with sets designed by Eugène Carpezat (Act I), Auguste-Alfred Rubé and Philippe Chaperon (Acts II and III), and Jean-Baptiste Lavastre (Act IV).

[d01p000] Manon Lescaut (Puccini)
[d01s000] Manon Lescaut is an opera in four acts by Giacomo Puccini, composed between 1890 and 1893.
[d01s001] The story is based on the 1731 novel "L'histoire du chevalier des Grieux et de Manon Lescaut" by the Abbé Prévost and should not be confused with "Manon", an 1884 opera by Jules Massenet based on the same novel.

[d02p000] Manon (disambiguation)
[d02s000] Manon is an opera by Jules Massenet, adapted from Abbé Prévost's novel "Manon Lescaut".

[d06p000] Manon Lescaut (Auber)
[d06s000] Manon Lescaut is an opera or opéra comique in 3 acts by Daniel Auber to a libretto by Eugène Scribe, and, like Puccini's "Manon Lescaut" and Massenet's "Manon", is based on the Abbé Prévost's novel "Manon Lescaut".
[d06s001] Auber's version is nowadays the least-performed of the three.

[d00p000] Parsifal
[d00s000] Parsifal (WWV 111) is an opera in three acts by German composer Richard Wagner.
[d00s001] It is loosely based on "Parzival" by Wolfram von Eschenbach, a 13th-century epic poem of the Arthurian knight Parzival (Percival) and his quest for the Holy Grail (12th century).

[d09p000] L'histoire de Manon
[d09s000] L'histoire de Manon, generally referred to as "Manon", is a ballet choreographed by Kenneth MacMillan to music by Jules Massenet and based on the 1731 novel "Manon Lescaut" by Abbé Prévost.
[d09s001] The ballet was first performed by The Royal Ballet in London in 1974 with Antoinette Sibley and Anthony Dowell in the leading roles.
[d09s002] It continues to be performed and recognised internationally.

[d03p000] Boulevard Solitude
[d03s000] Boulevard Solitude is a "Lyrisches Drama " (lyric drama) or opera in one act by Hans Werner Henze to a German libretto by Grete Weil after the play by Walter Jockisch, in its turn a modern retelling of François Prévost's "Manon Lescaut".
[d03s001] The piece is a reworking of the Manon Lescaut story, already adapted operatically by Auber, Massenet and Puccini, and here relocated to Paris after the Second World War where, as is noted in Grove, the focus of the story moves away from Manon and towards Armand des Grieux.
[d03s002] It became Henze’s first fully-fledged opera.

[d05p000] Massenet Festival
[d05s000] Massenet Festival ("Festival Massenet") is a biennale festival of music by French composer, Jules Massenet held in Saint-Étienne, France, close to the area where the composer was born.
[d05s001] The first Massenet Festival took place in November 1990 when the opera "Cléopâtre" and the oratorio "La Vierge" were presented.
[d05s002] In recent years, performances have been given in the Grand Théâtre Massenet, one of the theatres of the Opéra Théâtre de Saint-Etienne, and formerly known as L'Esplanade.

[d04p003] Renée Fleming
[d04s003] She also speaks fluent German and French, along with limited Italian.
[d04s004] Her signature roles include Countess Almaviva in Mozart's "Le nozze di Figaro", Desdemona in Verdi's "Otello", Violetta in Verdi's "La traviata", the title role in Dvořák's "Rusalka", the title role in Massenet's "Manon", the title role in Massenet's "Thaïs", the title role in Richard Strauss's "Arabella", the Marschallin in "Der Rosenkavalier", and the Countess in "Capriccio".

[d08p003] Jean-Claude Auvray
[d08s003] Among his 150 and more productions are "Tancredi" (Rossini), "La Gioconda" (Ponchielli), "Tristan und Isolde" (Wagner), "Manon" (Massenet), "Peter Grimes" (Britten), "Fidelio" (Beethoven), "Otello, "Aida" (Verdi), "La bohème" and "Gianni Schicchi" (Puccini).
[d08s004] Between 1996 and 2006 he directed plays at the Israeli Opera.

question: What is the genus and species of the bear in which the Florida black bear is a subspecies of?
context:
[d04p000] Florida black bear
[d04s000] The Florida black bear ("Ursus americanus floridanus") is a subspecies of the American black bear that has historically ranged throughout most of Florida and southern portions of Alabama, Georgia, and Mississippi.
[d04s001] The large black-furred bears live mainly in forested areas and have seen recent habitat reduction throughout the state.

[d02p000] Ursus americanus carlottae
[d02s000] The Haida Gwaii black bear ("Ursus americanus carlottae") is a morphologically distinct subspecies of the American black bear.
[d02s001] The most significant morphological differences are its large size, massive cranium, and large molars.
[d02s002] This subspecies is endemic to the Haida Gwaii (Queen Charlotte Islands) and is considered a "keystone species" because of the bears transportation of salmon remains into surrounding forests of Haida Gwaii.

[d08p000] Newfoundland black bear
[d08s000] The Newfoundland black bear ("Ursus americanus hamiltoni") is a morphologically distinct subspecies of the American black bear which is endemic to the island of Newfoundland in Atlantic Canada.
[d08s001] The Newfoundland black bear is generally larger than its mainland relatives, ranging in size from 90 to and averaging 135 kg .
[d08s002] It also has one of the longest hibernation periods of any bear in North America.

[d06p000] American black bear
[d06s000] The American black bear ("Ursus americanus") is a medium-sized bear native to North America.

[d01p000] Cinnamon bear
[d01s000] The cinnamon bear ("Ursus americanus cinnamomum") is both a color phase and subspecies of the American black bear, native to central and western areas of the United States and Canada.
[d01s001] Established populations are found in Colorado, New Mexico, Utah, Idaho, Montana, Washington, Manitoba Minnesota, Wisconsin, Wyoming, California, Alberta, and British Columbia.
[d01s002] They also have been seen in Pennsylvania and New York.

[d05p000] Japanese black bear
[d05s000] The Japanese black bear ("Ursus thibetanus japonicus") is a subspecies of the Asian black bear that lives on three main islands of Japan: Honshu, Shikoku and Kyushu.
[d05s001] There are said to be 10,000 black bears on Japan.
[d05s002] The population of black bears on Shikoku and Kyushu may be endangered or extinct.

[d09p000] Kermode bear
[d09s000] The Kermode bear ("Ursus americanus kermodei"), also known as the "spirit bear" (particularly in British Columbia), is a rare subspecies of the American black bear living in the Central and North Coast regions of British Columbia, Canada.
[d09s001] It is the official provincial mammal of British Columbia.
[d09s002] It is noted for about one-tenth of its population having white or cream-coloured coats like polar bears.

[d07p000] Baluchistan bear
[d07s000] The Baluchistan bear, also called the Pakistan black bear ("Ursus thibetanus gedrosianus") is a subspecies of the Asian black bear found in the Baluchistan Mountains of southern Pakistan and Iran.
[d07s001] It has an unusually thin coat for an Asian black bear, but this is because it is found in a warmer climate than most of the other subspecies, which are found in the much colder Himalayan Mountains.
[d07s002] It is also more frugivorous than the other subspecies, and it loves to eat figs and bananas.

[d03p000] Ussuri black bear
[d03s000] The Ussuri black bear ("Ursus thibetanus ussuricus"), also known as the Manchurian black bear, is a large subspecies of the Asian black bear native to the Far East, including the Korean Peninsula.

[d09p003] Kermode bear
[d09s003] This colour is due to a double recessive gene unique in the subspecies.
[d09s004] They are not albinos and not any more related to polar bears or the "blonde" brown bears of Alaska's "ABC Islands" than other members of their species.
[d09s005] Sometimes, a mother black bear can have a white cub.

context:
[d04p000] Battle of Stones River
[d04s000] The Battle of Stones River or Second Battle of Murfreesboro, was fought from December 31, 1862, to January 2, 1863, in Middle Tennessee, as the culmination of the Stones River Campaign in the Western Theater of the American Civil War.
[d04s001] Of the major battles of the Civil War, Stones River had the highest percentage of casualties on both sides.
[d04s002] Although the battle itself was inconclusive, the Union Army's repulse of two Confederate attacks and the subsequent Confederate withdrawal were a much-needed boost to Union morale after the defeat at the Battle of Fredericksburg, and it dashed Confederate aspirations for control of Middle Tennessee.

[d06p000] Battle of the Ch'ongch'on River
[d06s000] The Battle of the Ch'ongch'on River, also known as the Battle of the Ch'ongch'on () or the Second Phase Campaign Western Sector (), was a decisive battle in the Korean War, and it took place from November 25 to December 2, 1950, along the Ch'ongch'on River Valley in the northwestern part of North Korea.
[d06s001] In response to the successful Chinese First Phase Campaign against the United Nations forces, General Douglas MacArthur launched the Home-by-Christmas Offensive to evict the Chinese forces from Korea and to end the war.
[d06s002] Anticipating this reaction, the Chinese People's Volunteer Army Commander Peng Dehuai planned a counteroffensive, dubbed the "Second Phase Campaign", against the advancing UN forces.

[d01p003] Battle of Berestechko
[d01s003] The Polish camp was on the river opposite Berestechko and faced south, towards the Cossack army about two kilometers away, whose right flank was against the River Pliashivka (Pliashova) and the Tatar army on their left flank.
[d01s004] It was probably the largest European land battle of the 17th century.

question: What where both Hawker Hurricane and No. 1455 Flight apart of?
context:
[d05p000] No. 1455 Flight RAF
[d05s000] No. 1455 (Fighter) Flight was formed at RAF Tangmere, West Sussex on 7 July 1941, equipped with Turbinlite Douglas Boston and Douglas Havoc aircraft.
[d05s001] On operations they co-operated with the Hawker Hurricanes of 1 Squadron and 3 Squadron.
[d05s002] The flight was replaced with 534 Squadron on 2 September 1942.

[d08p000] Hawker Hurricane
[d08s000] The Hawker Hurricane is a British single-seat fighter aircraft of the 1930s–1940s that was designed and predominantly built by Hawker Aircraft Ltd for the Royal Air Force (RAF).
[d08s001] Although overshadowed by the Supermarine Spitfire, the aircraft became renowned during the Battle of Britain, accounting for 60 percent of the RAF air victories in the battle, and served in all the major theatres of the Second World War.

[d02p000] Hawker Typhoon
[d02s000] The Hawker Typhoon (Tiffy in RAF slang), is a British single-seat fighter-bomber, produced by Hawker Aircraft.
[d02s001] It was intended to be a medium–high altitude interceptor, as a replacement for the Hawker Hurricane but several design problems were encountered and it never completely satisfied this requirement.

[d06p000] Hawker Tornado
[d06s000] The Hawker Tornado was a British single-seat fighter aircraft design of World War II for the Royal Air Force as a replacement for the Hawker Hurricane.
[d06s001] The planned production of Tornados was cancelled after the engine it was designed to use—the Rolls-Royce Vulture—proved unreliable in service.
[d06s002] A parallel airframe with the Napier Sabre continued into production as the Hawker Typhoon.

[d04p000] No. 1300 Flight RAF
[d04s000] No. 1300 (Meteorological) Flight was formed on 31 July 1943 at RAF Alipore, West Bengal, British India, by re-designating No. 1 Meteorological Flight RAF.
[d04s001] The flight, strength of which had been reduced to three Hawker Hurricane Mk.IIs by this time, was disbanded on 30 May 1946 at RAF Kallang, Malaya, as No. 1300 (Meteorological THUM) Flight, THUM standing for Temperature and Humidity.

[d01p000] Flying Legend Hawker Hurricane Replica
[d01s000] The Flying Legend Hawker Hurricane Replica is an Italian light-sport aircraft, designed and produced by Flying Legend of Caltagirone and introduced at the AERO Friedrichshafen show in 2011.
[d01s001] The aircraft, a 72% scale replica of the British Hawker Hurricane Second World War fighter, is supplied as a kit for amateur construction or as a complete ready-to-fly-aircraft.

[d07p000] Sindlinger Hawker Hurricane
[d07s000] The Sindlinger HH-1 Hawker Hurricane is a ⅝ scale homebuilt design based on the Hawker Hurricane.
[d07s001] Designed by Fred Sindlinger for amateur construction, the prototype was built between 1969 and 1972.

[d09p000] Battle of Britain Memorial Flight
[d09s000] The Battle of Britain Memorial Flight (BBMF) is a Royal Air Force flight which provides an aerial display group usually comprising an Avro Lancaster, a Supermarine Spitfire and a Hawker Hurricane.
[d09s001] The aircraft are regularly seen at events commemorating the Second World War and upon British State occasions, notably Trooping the Colour, celebrating Queen Elizabeth II's 80th birthday in 2006, as well as the wedding of Prince William, Duke of Cambridge and Catherine Middleton in 2011 and at air displays throughout the United Kingdom and Europe.

[d03p003] Hawker Hurricane in Yugoslav service
[d03s003] When the country was drawn into World War II by the German-led Axis invasion of April 1941, a total of 41 Hurricane Mk I's were in service as fighters.
[d03s004] They achieved some successes against "Luftwaffe" aircraft, but all Yugoslav Hurricanes were destroyed or captured during the 11-day invasion.

[d03p000] Hawker Hurricane in Yugoslav service
[d03s000] The Royal Yugoslav Air Force (VVKJ) operated the British Hawker Hurricane Mk I fighter aircraft from 1938 to 1941.
[d03s001] Between 1938 and 1940, the VVKJ obtained 24 Hurricane Mk I's from early production batches, marking the first foreign sale of the aircraft.
[d03s002] Twenty additional aircraft were built by Zmaj under licence in Yugoslavia.

question: Which opera has more acts, Parsifal or Manon by Massenet?
context:
[d00p000] Parsifal
[d00s000] Parsifal (WWV 111) is an opera in three acts by German composer Richard Wagner.
[d00s001] It is loosely based on "Parzival" by Wolfram von Eschenbach, a 13th-century epic poem of the Arthurian knight Parzival (Percival) and his quest for the Holy Grail (12th century).

[d06p000] Manon Lescaut (Auber)
[d06s000] Manon Lescaut is an opera or opéra comique in 3 acts by Daniel Auber to a libretto by Eugène Scribe, and, like Puccini's "Manon Lescaut" and Massenet's "Manon", is based on the Abbé Prévost's novel "Manon Lescaut".
[d06s001] Auber's version is nowadays the least-performed of the three.

[d08p003] Jean-Claude Auvray
[d08s003] Among his 150 and more productions are "Tancredi" (Rossini), "La Gioconda" (Ponchielli), "Tristan und Isolde" (Wagner), "Manon" (Massenet), "Peter Grimes" (Britten), "Fidelio" (Beethoven), "Otello, "Aida" (Verdi), "La bohème" and "Gianni Schicchi" (Puccini).
[d08s004] Between 1996 and 2006 he directed plays at the Israeli Opera.

[d04p000] Renée Fleming
[d04s000] Renée Fleming (born February 14, 1959) is an American opera singer and soprano whose repertoire encompasses Richard Strauss, Mozart, Handel, bel canto, lieder, French opera and chansons, jazz and indie rock.
[d04s001] Fleming has a full lyric soprano voice.
[d04s002] She has performed coloratura, lyric, and lighter spinto soprano operatic roles in Italian, German, French, Czech, and Russian, aside from her native English.

[d01p000] Manon Lescaut (Puccini)
[d01s000] Manon Lescaut is an opera in four acts by Giacomo Puccini, composed between 1890 and 1893.
[d01s001] The story is based on the 1731 novel "L'histoire du chevalier des Grieux et de Manon Lescaut" by the Abbé Prévost and should not be confused with "Manon", an 1884 opera by Jules Massenet based on the same novel.

[d03p000] Boulevard Solitude
[d03s000] Boulevard Solitude is a "Lyrisches Drama " (lyric drama) or opera in one act by Hans Werner Henze to a German libretto by Grete Weil after the play by Walter Jockisch, in its turn a modern retelling of François Prévost's "Manon Lescaut".
[d03s001] The piece is a reworking of the Manon Lescaut story, already adapted operatically by Auber, Massenet and Puccini, and here relocated to Paris after the Second World War where, as is noted in Grove, the focus of the story moves away from Manon and towards Armand des Grieux.
[d03s002] It became Henze’s first fully-fledged opera.

[d07p000] Manon
[d07s000] Manon (] ) is an "opéra comique" in five acts by Jules Massenet to a French libretto by Henri Meilhac and Philippe Gille, based on the 1731 novel "L’histoire du chevalier des Grieux et de Manon Lescaut" by the Abbé Prévost.
[d07s001] It was first performed at the Opéra-Comique in Paris on 19 January 1884, with sets designed by Eugène Carpezat (Act I), Auguste-Alfred Rubé and Philippe Chaperon (Acts II and III), and Jean-Baptiste Lavastre (Act IV).

[d02p000] Manon (disambiguation)

question: In what order does Three Colours: Blue appear in the Three Colours trilogy?
context:
[d04p000] Three Colours: Blue
[d04s000] Three Colours: Blue (French: Trois couleurs : Bleu ) is a 1993 French drama film directed and co-written by Polish filmmaker Krzysztof Kieślowski.
[d04s001] "Blue" is the first of three films that comprise the "Three Colours" trilogy, themed on the French Revolutionary ideals of liberty, equality, and fraternity; it is followed by "" and "".
[d04s002] According to Kieślowski, the subject of the film is liberty, specifically emotional liberty, rather than its social or political meaning.

[d06p000] Three Colours trilogy
[d06s000] The "Three Colours" trilogy (Polish: "Trzy kolory" , French: "Trois couleurs" ) is a three-part film series directed by Krzysztof Kieślowski.
[d06s001] Two of the films were made in French and one primarily in Polish: "" (1993), "" (1994), and "" (1994).
[d06s002] All three were co-written by Kieślowski and Krzysztof Piesiewicz (with story consultants Agnieszka Holland and Sławomir Idziak) and have musical scores by Zbigniew Preisner.

[d00p000] Three Colours: White
[d00s000] Three Colours: White (French: Trois couleurs : Blanc ) is a 1994 French-Polish comedy-drama film co-written, produced, and directed by Krzysztof Kieślowski.
[d00s001] "White" is the second in "The Three Colors Trilogy", themed on the French Revolutionary ideals, following "" and preceding "".
[d00s002] The film was selected as the Polish entry for the Best Foreign Language Film at the 67th Academy Awards, but was not accepted as a nominee.

[d05p003] Blue
[d05s003] In painting and traditional colour theory, blue is one of the three primary colours of pigments, along with red and yellow, which can be mixed to form a wide gamut of colours.
[d05s004] Red and blue mixed together form violet, blue and yellow together form green.
[d05s005] Blue is also a primary colour in the RGB colour model, used to create all the colours on the screen of a television or computer monitor.

[d05p000] Blue
[d05s000] Blue is the colour between violet and green on the spectrum of visible light.
[d05s001] Human eyes perceive blue when observing light with a wavelength between 450 and 495 nanometres. Blues with a higher frequency and thus a shorter wavelength appear more violet, while those with a lower frequency and a longer wavelength gradually appear more green.
[d05s002] Pure blue, in the middle, has a wavelength of 470 nanometres.

[d08p000] Pan-African colours
[d08s000] The term Pan-African colours refers to two different sets of three colours: red, gold (not yellow), and green (inspired by the flag of Ethiopia), and red, black, and green.
[d08s001] They are used in flags and other emblems of various countries and territories in Africa and the Americas to represent Pan-Africanist ideology.
[d08s002] The Rastafarian movement and many Pan-African organisations also often employ the colours for their activities.

[d09p000] Requiem for my friend (Preisner)
[d09s000] Requiem for my friend is a major and the first non-film musical work composed by Zbigniew Preisner.
[d09s001] The composition was meant to honour the composer's late friend, the director Krzysztof Kieślowski, with whom he collaborated while working on a number of films, including the famous "Three Colours" trilogy.
[d09s002] The album was released in 1998 although some parts of the work must have been ready upon Kieślowski's passing as Preisner asserted in an interview that "the Requiem had accompanied Krzysztof in his last journey".

[d01p003] Be All That You Can't Be
[d01s003] The vinyl is available in three colours: Blue, orange and white (Hot Topic Exclusive).
[d01s004] Each colour is limited to 500.
[d01s005] The music video for the song was released through Absolute Punk on 6 August 2009.

[d07p000] City of Sydney flag
[d07s000] The City of Sydney flag is made up of a horizontal triband of three colours – white, gold and blue.
[d07s001] It was designed in 1908.
[d07s002] The top third of the flag features three designs.

[d03p003] Hokusai Manga
[d03s003] Block-printed in three colours (black, gray and pale flesh), the Manga comprise literally thousands of images in 15 volumes, the first published in 1814, when the artist was 55.
[d03s004] The final three volumes were published posthumously, two of them assembled by their publisher from previously unpublished material.
[d03s005] The final volume was made up of previously published works, some not even by Hokusai, and is not considered authentic by art historians.

question: What broadcasting company did both Andrew Collins and Stuart Maconie of Collins and Maconie's Hit Parade both work together from 1194 to 1197?
context:
[d00p000] Collins and Maconie's Hit Parade
[d00s000] Collins and Maconie's Hit Parade was a radio programme that aired from May 1994 to June 1997.
[d00s001] There were 74 hour-long episodes and it was broadcast on BBC Radio 1.
[d00s002] It starred Andrew Collins and Stuart Maconie.

[d04p000] Stuart Maconie
[d04s000] Stuart Maconie (born 13 August 1960) is an English radio DJ and television presenter, writer, journalist, and critic working in the field of pop music and popular culture.
[d04s001] He is currently a presenter on BBC Radio 6 Music, where he hosts an afternoon show five times a week (Monday–Friday, 1pm–4pm), alongside Mark Radcliffe, called "Radcliffe & Maconie", which broadcasts from the BBC's MediaCityUK in Salford, Greater Manchester.
[d04s002] The pair had previously presented an evening show on BBC Radio 2.

[d07p000] Radcliffe & Maconie
[d07s000] Radcliffe & Maconie is a weekday radio programme that is broadcast on BBC Radio 6 Music in the United Kingdom.
[d07s001] It runs from 1 pm–4 pm on Monday to Friday, and is presented by Mark Radcliffe and Stuart Maconie.
[d07s002] The show originally ran on BBC Radio 2 from 16 April 2007 until 23 March 2011, where it was known as "The Radcliffe and Maconie Show".

[d08p000] Hit parade
[d08s000] A hit parade is a ranked list of the most popular recordings at a given point in time, usually determined by sales and/or airplay.
[d08s001] The term originated in the 1930s; "Billboard" magazine published its first music hit parade on January 4, 1936.
[d08s002] It has also been used by broadcast programs which featured hit (sheet music and record) tunes such as "Your Hit Parade", which aired on radio and television in the United States from 1935 through the 1950s.

[d01p000] Sons Ltd
[d01s000] The Soul of North Staffs Recording & Publishing or Sons is an independent record label based in Stoke-on-Trent.
[d01s001] The company was formed in 2004 by Neil Graham, Seb Clarke, Al Padmore, James Wakefield and Tangwyn Davies.
[d01s002] The label consists solely of bands native to the North Staffordshire area and has become a noted figure both locally and nationally, having recently received attention from Steve Lamacq and Huw Stephens (6music, BBC Radio 1) as well as Mark Radcliffe and Stuart Maconie (BBC Radio 2) SONS has earned comparisons to Factory Records for its DIY ethic and its unique 'SONS sound'.

[d09p000] Hit Parade 1
[d09s000] In 1992, The Wedding Present decided to release a limited edition single every month, each featuring an original track on the A side and a cover on the B side.
[d09s001] The tracks were compiled as two LPs called Hit Parade 1 and "Hit Parade 2" and re-released as a double CD in 2003 called "The Hit Parade".

[d06p000] Somebody's Gotta Go
[d06s000] "Somebody's Gotta Go" is a 1945 song by Cootie Williams and His Orchestra.
[d06s001] With vocals performed by Eddie Vinson, the single was Cootie Williams' most successful entry on the Harlem Hit Parade, hitting number one on the Harlem Hit Parade.
[d06s002] "Somebody's Gotta Go" was the final number one on The Harlem Hit Parade chart.

[d05p000] Hit Parade 2
[d05s000] Hit Parade 2 is a compilation album by The Wedding Present released in January 1993.
[d05s001] Having decided to release a limited edition single every month for all of 1992 (each featuring an original track on the A side and a cover version on the B side) the group subsequently compiled the songs as two LPs called Hit Parade 1 and Hit Parade 2.
[d05s002] In 2003, a double CD was issued called simply "The Hit Parade".

[d02p000] Dave Hill
[d02s000] David John "Dave" Hill (born 4 April 1946) is an English musician, who is the lead guitarist and backing vocalist in the English glam rock group, Slade.
[d02s001] Hill is known for his flamboyant stage clothes and hairstyle.

question: Which breed of dog was first recognized by their country's official kennel club, the American Hairless Terrier or the Saint-Usuge Spaniel?
context:
[d06p000] Saint-Usuge Spaniel
[d06s000] The Saint-Usuge Spaniel (or Épagneul de Saint-Usuge) is a breed of Spaniel originating in the Bresse region of France.
[d06s001] The breed has origins dating back to at least the 16th century, but was nearly extinct by the end of World War II.
[d06s002] Through the efforts of Father Robert Billard, the breed was resurrected during the second half of the 20th century; its national breed club was founded in 1990.

[d01p000] American Russell Terrier Club
[d01s000] The American Russell Terrier Club (formerly named the English Jack Russell Terrier Club), founded by JoAnn Stoll in 1995, was the first registry in the United States to maintain the Russell Terrier as a separate breed from the Parson Russell Terrier.
[d01s001] The American Jack Russell Terrier Club is affiliated with both the United Kennel Club and the American Kennel Club.
[d01s002] The purpose of the early founders was to establish a registry for the perpetuation and development of the Russell Terrier as a pure strain of working Jack Russell Terrier keeping their blood and type pure within the registry to works towards Kennel Club recognition as an official breed in the US.

[d06p003] Saint-Usuge Spaniel
[d06s003] The breed was recognised by the Société Centrale Canine (French Kennel Club) in 2003.

[d00p000] American Hairless Terrier
[d00s000] The American Hairless Terrier is a rare breed of dog that was derived as a variant of Rat Terrier.
[d00s001] As of January 1, 2004, the United Kennel Club deemed the AHT a separate terrier breed, granting it full UKC recognition.
[d00s002] An intelligent, social and energetic working breed, the American Hairless Terrier is often listed as a potential good breed choice for allergy sufferers.

[d04p000] Terrier Group
[d04s000] Terrier Group is the name of a breed Group of dogs, used by kennel clubs to classify a defined collection of dog breeds.
[d04s001] In general, a "Terrier Group" includes one particular type of dog, the Terrier, although other types may be included in a kennel club's "Terrier Group".
[d04s002] Most major English-language kennel clubs include a "Terrier Group" although different kennel clubs may not include the same breeds in their "Terrier Group".

[d01p003] American Russell Terrier Club
[d01s003] On January 1, 2001, the United Kennel Club recognized the Russell Terrier as an official breed, designating only the stock from the American Russell Terrier Club as Foundation stock for the UKC Russell Terrier.
[d01s004] In 2004 the American Russell Terrier Club submitted an official request to include the American Russell Terrier Club stock into the AKC FSS Program to work towards becoming an official breed under the perimeters.
[d01s005] On December 8, 2004, the AKC officially accepted the Russell Terrier.

[d03p000] Shikoku (dog)
[d03s000] The Shikoku (四国犬 , Shikoku-ken , alternative names: Kochi-ken, Mikawa Inu, Japanese Wolfdog) is a native, primitive Japanese breed of dog from Shikoku island that is similar to a Shiba Inu.
[d03s001] The Shikoku was recently added as recognized breed of the American Kennel Club as an AKC FSS standard [ Foundation Stock Service ], it is recognized by the Japan Kennel Club, an organization recognized by AKC as an official foreign registry (AKC recognizes the Shiba Inu, however).
[d03s002] The Shikoku is also in the Canadian Kennel Club Hound group and the United Kennel Club, awaiting full recognition.

[d02p000] Rare breed (dog)
[d02s000] Rare breed (dog) is any breed of dog that is small in number and is used to refer to both old established breeds such as the Stabyhoun and Glen of Imaal Terrier or newer creations.
[d02s001] Since dogs have greater genetic variability than other domesticated animals the number of possible breeds is vast with new crosses constantly occurring, from these both selected and random crosses may come new breeds should offspring reliably breed true to type.
[d02s002] New breeds from the wild such as the Carolina Dog are quite rare compared to attempts at breed creation from man as found in the American Hairless Terrier which sought to exploit a mutation.

[d07p000] Toy Manchester Terrier
[d07s000] The Toy Manchester Terrier is a breed of dog, categorized as a terrier.
[d07s001] The breed was bred down in size in North America from the Manchester Terrier, and is placed in the Toy Group by the American Kennel Club and the Canadian Kennel Club (the Manchester Terrier is placed in the Terrier Group.)
[d07s002] Neither the Fédération Cynologique Internationale nor The Kennel Club recognize a Toy variety of the Manchester Terrier.

[d09p006] English Springer Spaniel
[d09s006] The smaller "cockers" hunted woodcock while the larger littermates were used to flush, or "spring," game.
[d09s007] In 1902, The Kennel Club recognized the English Springer Spaniel as a distinct breed.
[d09s008] They are used as sniffer dogs on a widespread basis.

question: Who lived longer Ellen Glasgow or N. Scott Momaday ?
context:
[d05p000] Ellen Glasgow
[d05s000] Ellen Anderson Gholson Glasgow (April 22, 1873 – November 21, 1945) was an American novelist who portrayed the changing world of the contemporary South.

[d02p000] N. Scott Momaday
[d02s000] Navarre Scott Momaday (born February 27, 1934) — known as N. Scott Momaday — is a Kiowa novelist, short story writer, essayist, and poet.
[d02s001] His novel "House Made of Dawn" was awarded the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 1969, and is considered the first major work of the Native American Renaissance.
[d02s002] His follow-up work "The Way to Rainy Mountain" blended folklore with memoir.

[d04p000] Ellen Glasgow House
[d04s000] The Ellen Glasgow House, also known as the Branch-Glascow House, is a historic house at 1 West Main Street in Richmond, Virginia.
[d04s001] Built in 1841, it is nationally significant as the home of writer Ellen Glasgow (1873-1945) from 1887 until her death.
[d04s002] It was declared a National Historic Landmark in 1971.

[d01p000] The Way to Rainy Mountain
[d01s000] The Way to Rainy Mountain (1969) is a book by Pulitzer Prize winning author N. Scott Momaday.
[d01s001] It is about the journey of Momaday's Kiowa ancestors from their ancient beginnings in the Montana area to their final war and surrender to the United States Cavalry at Fort Sill, and subsequent resettlement near Rainy Mountain, Oklahoma.

[d06p000] The Shadowy Third and Other Stories
[d06s000] The Shadowy Third and Other Stories is a 1923 short story collection by Ellen Glasgow.
[d06s001] Glasgow published only this one short story collection during her lifetime, which included seven stories.
[d06s002] While Glasgow's novels receive more critical attention, scholarship on her stories continues into the twenty-first century.

[d03p000] House Made of Dawn
[d03s000] House Made of Dawn is a 1968 novel by N. Scott Momaday, widely credited as leading the way for the breakthrough of Native American literature into the mainstream.
[d03s001] It was awarded the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 1969, and has also been noted for its significance in Native American Anthropology.

[d07p000] Virginia (novel)
[d07s000] Virginia (1913) is a novel by Ellen Glasgow about a wife and mother who in vain seeks happiness by serving her family.
[d07s001] This novel, her eleventh, marked a clear departure from Glasgow's previous work—she had written a series of bestsellers before publishing "Virginia"—in that it attacked, in a subtle yet unmistakable way, the very layer of society that constituted her readership.
[d07s002] Also, as its heroine, though virtuous and god-fearing, is denied the happiness she is craving, its plot did not live up to readers' expectations as far as poetic justice is concerned and was bound to upset some of them.

[d00p000] Ari Berk
[d00s000] Ari Berk is an American writer, folklorist, artist, and scholar of literature, iconography, and comparative myth.
[d00s001] Berk holds degrees in Ancient History (B.A.), American Indian Studies (M.A.), and Comparative Literature and Culture (Ph.D.) from Humboldt State University and University of Arizona respectively.
[d00s002] His dissertation was directed by Pulitzer Prize winner N. Scott Momaday and Berk was appointed to the committee that developed the first American Indian Studies doctoral program in the United States.

[d09p000] Native American Renaissance
[d09s000] The Native American Renaissance is a term originally coined by critic Kenneth Lincoln in the 1983 book "Native American Renaissance" to categorise the significant increase in production of literary works by Native Americans in the United States in the late 1960s and onwards.
[d09s001] A. Robert Lee and Alan Velie note that the book's title "quickly gained currency as a term to describe the efflorescence on literary works that followed the publication of N. Scott Momaday's "House Made of Dawn" in 1968".
[d09s002] Momaday's novel garnered critical acclaim, including the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 1969.

[d02p003] N. Scott Momaday
[d02s003] Momaday received the National Medal of Arts in 2007 for his work's celebration and preservation of indigenous oral and art tradition.
[d02s004] He holds twenty honorary degrees from colleges and universities, and is a fellow of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences.

[d04s000] The Florida black bear ("Ursus americanus floridanus") is a subspecies of the American black bear that has historically ranged throughout most of Florida and southern portions of Alabama, Georgia, and Mississippi.
[d04s001] The large black-furred bears live mainly in forested areas and have seen recent habitat reduction throughout the state.

[d05p003] Japanese black bear
[d05s003] There is a high price on bear parts in the black market, which threatens all bear populations in Japan.
[d05s004] This particular species of bear are typically smaller with males only reaching 60-120 Kg and females only weighing about 40-100 Kg.
[d05s005] Their body length is about 120–140 cm long.

[d07p000] Baluchistan bear
[d07s000] The Baluchistan bear, also called the Pakistan black bear ("Ursus thibetanus gedrosianus") is a subspecies of the Asian black bear found in the Baluchistan Mountains of southern Pakistan and Iran.
[d07s001] It has an unusually thin coat for an Asian black bear, but this is because it is found in a warmer climate than most of the other subspecies, which are found in the much colder Himalayan Mountains.
[d07s002] It is also more frugivorous than the other subspecies, and it loves to eat figs and bananas.

[d08p000] Newfoundland black bear
[d08s000] The Newfoundland black bear ("Ursus americanus hamiltoni") is a morphologically distinct subspecies of the American black bear which is endemic to the island of Newfoundland in Atlantic Canada.
[d08s001] The Newfoundland black bear is generally larger than its mainland relatives, ranging in size from 90 to and averaging 135 kg .
[d08s002] It also has one of the longest hibernation periods of any bear in North America.

[d09p003] Kermode bear
[d09s003] This colour is due to a double recessive gene unique in the subspecies.
[d09s004] They are not albinos and not any more related to polar bears or the "blonde" brown bears of Alaska's "ABC Islands" than other members of their species.
[d09s005] Sometimes, a mother black bear can have a white cub.

[d02p000] Ursus americanus carlottae
[d02s000] The Haida Gwaii black bear ("Ursus americanus carlottae") is a morphologically distinct subspecies of the American black bear.
[d02s001] The most significant morphological differences are its large size, massive cranium, and large molars.
[d02s002] This subspecies is endemic to the Haida Gwaii (Queen Charlotte Islands) and is considered a "keystone species" because of the bears transportation of salmon remains into surrounding forests of Haida Gwaii.

[d01p000] Cinnamon bear
[d01s000] The cinnamon bear ("Ursus americanus cinnamomum") is both a color phase and subspecies of the American black bear, native to central and western areas of the United States and Canada.
[d01s001] Established populations are found in Colorado, New Mexico, Utah, Idaho, Montana, Washington, Manitoba Minnesota, Wisconsin, Wyoming, California, Alberta, and British Columbia.
[d01s002] They also have been seen in Pennsylvania and New York.

[d00p000] Black Bear Creek
[d00s000] Black Bear Creek is a 116 mi creek in northern Oklahoma.
[d00s001] Black Bear Creek drains an area of 538 sqmi in Garfield County, Noble County and Pawnee County, Oklahoma.
[d00s002] It takes on a red color from the red clay of this area.

[d09p000] Kermode bear
[d09s000] The Kermode bear ("Ursus americanus kermodei"), also known as the "spirit bear" (particularly in British Columbia), is a rare subspecies of the American black bear living in the Central and North Coast regions of British Columbia, Canada.
[d09s001] It is the official provincial mammal of British Columbia.
[d09s002] It is noted for about one-tenth of its population having white or cream-coloured coats like polar bears.

[d01p003] Cinnamon bear
[d01s003] The most striking difference between a cinnamon bear and any other black bear is its brown or red-brown fur, reminiscent of cinnamon.
[d01s004] The subspecies was given the designation because the lighter color phase is more common there than in other areas.

question: Glaramara is a fell in the English Lake District in Cumbria that stretches from Stonethwaite which is a part of a valley and civil parrish in what Borough?
context:
[d06p000] Glaramara
[d06s000] Glaramara is a fell in the English Lake District in Cumbria.
[d06s001] It is a substantial fell that is part of a long ridge that stretches for over six kilometres from Stonethwaite in Borrowdale up to the important mountain pass of Esk Hause.
[d06s002] The summit of Glaramara at 783 m (2,569 ft) is the central point of this ridge, which separates the valleys of Langstrath and Grains Gill.

[d04p000] Stonethwaite
[d04s000] Stonethwaite is a small village in the Lake District in the English county of Cumbria.
[d04s001] Historically part of Cumberland, it is situated in the valley of the Stonethwaite Beck, a side valley of Borrowdale, and within the Lake District National Park.
[d04s002] It is on the Cumbria Way long distance footpath.

[d01p000] Borrowdale
[d01s000] Borrowdale is a valley and civil parish in the English Lake District in the Borough of Allerdale in Cumbria, England.

[d09p000] Eagle Crag
[d09s000] Eagle Crag is a fell in the Lake District in Cumbria, England, it is situated near the village of Stonethwaite where the valleys of Langstrath and Greenup join.
[d09s001] Impressive walls of crag look down upon Stonethwaite, making Eagle Crag the most arresting sight from that settlement.
[d09s002] It can be climbed direct by the average walker, picking a route between the rock faces.

[d03p000] Great Crag
[d03s000] Great Crag is a fell in the English Lake District, located near the hamlets of Rosthwaite and Stonethwaite in Borrowdale.

[d08p000] Bowfell
[d08s000] Bowfell (named "Bow Fell" on Ordnance Survey maps) is a pyramid-shaped mountain lying at the heart of the English Lake District, in the Southern Fells area.
[d08s001] It is the sixth-highest mountain in the Lake District and one of the most popular of the Lake District fells for walkers.
[d08s002] It is listed in Alfred Wainwright's 'best half dozen' Lake District fells.

[d00p000] Ritson's Force
[d00s000] Ritson's Force is a set of waterfalls in the valley of Mosedale in the English Lake District.
[d00s001] It is also the river that leads past the Wasdale Head Inn and the Great Gable Brewing Company.
[d00s002] The hills nearby include Sca Fell and Scafell Pike, England's two highest mountains, and Great Gable, home to British climbing.

[d02p000] Blindcrake
[d02s000] Blindcrake is a village and civil parish within the Isel Valley, in the Lake District National Park and in the Allerdale district of Cumbria, England.
[d02s001] According to the 2001 census it had a population of 287, increasing to 348 at the 2011 Census.
[d02s002] The parish includes Blindcrake village and the hamlets of Redmain, Isel and Sunderland, The whole parish lies within the Lake District National Park and, since 2001, Blindcrake village  is one of 23 designated conservation areas of the National Park Planning Authority.

[d05p000] Dock Tarn
[d05s000] Dock Tarn is a small tarn located within the Lake District National Park in Cumbria, England at grid reference [ NY273143] .
[d05s001] It is situated on moorland at 400 metres above sea level near the summit of Great Crag, midway between Watendlath, the Stonethwaite valley and Borrowdale.
[d05s002] It measures approximately 300 by 200 metres, and the shoreline is indented with rocky headlands and bays.

[d02p003] Blindcrake
[d02s003] This status is largely based on its mediaeval strip field pattern which is described as "undoubtedly the finest example of its type in the Lake District".
[d02s004] The parish boundary is approximately defined by the Lake District National Park boundary in the north and west, by a line 2 km to the west of the A591 in the east and by the River Derwent in the south.
[d02s005] It is one of the smallest parishes within the Allerdale district of Cumbria.

question: What is the genus and species of the bear in which the Florida black bear is a subspecies of?
context:
[d04p000] Florida black bear
[d04s000] The Florida black bear ("Ursus americanus floridanus") is a subspecies of the American black bear that has historically ranged throughout most of Florida and southern portions of Alabama, Georgia, and Mississippi.
[d04s001] The large black-furred bears live mainly in forested areas and have seen recent habitat reduction throughout the state.

[d05p003] Japanese black bear
[d05s003] There is a high price on bear parts in the black market, which threatens all bear populations in Japan.
[d05s004] This particular species of bear are typically smaller with males only reaching 60-120 Kg and females only weighing about 40-100 Kg.
[d05s005] Their body length is about 120–140 cm long.

[d07p000] Baluchistan bear
[d07s000] The Baluchistan bear, also called the Pakistan black bear ("Ursus thibetanus gedrosianus") is a subspecies of the Asian black bear found in the Baluchistan Mountains of southern Pakistan and Iran.
[d07s001] It has an unusually thin coat for an Asian black bear, but this is because it is found in a warmer climate than most of the other subspecies, which are found in the much colder Himalayan Mountains.
[d07s002] It is also more frugivorous than the other subspecies, and it loves to eat figs and bananas.

[d08p000] Newfoundland black bear
[d08s000] The Newfoundland black bear ("Ursus americanus hamiltoni") is a morphologically distinct subspecies of the American black bear which is endemic to the island of Newfoundland in Atlantic Canada.
[d08s001] The Newfoundland black bear is generally larger than its mainland relatives, ranging in size from 90 to and averaging 135 kg .
[d08s002] It also has one of the longest hibernation periods of any bear in North America.

[d09p003] Kermode bear
[d09s003] This colour is due to a double recessive gene unique in the subspecies.
[d09s004] They are not albinos and not any more related to polar bears or the "blonde" brown bears of Alaska's "ABC Islands" than other members of their species.
[d09s005] Sometimes, a mother black bear can have a white cub.

[d02p000] Ursus americanus carlottae
[d02s000] The Haida Gwaii black bear ("Ursus americanus carlottae") is a morphologically distinct subspecies of the American black bear.
[d02s001] The most significant morphological differences are its large size, massive cranium, and large molars.
[d02s002] This subspecies is endemic to the Haida Gwaii (Queen Charlotte Islands) and is considered a "keystone species" because of the bears transportation of salmon remains into surrounding forests of Haida Gwaii.

[d01p000] Cinnamon bear
[d01s000] The cinnamon bear ("Ursus americanus cinnamomum") is both a color phase and subspecies of the American black bear, native to central and western areas of the United States and Canada.
[d01s001] Established populations are found in Colorado, New Mexico, Utah, Idaho, Montana, Washington, Manitoba Minnesota, Wisconsin, Wyoming, California, Alberta, and British Columbia.
[d01s002] They also have been seen in Pennsylvania and New York.

[d09p000] Kermode bear
[d09s000] The Kermode bear ("Ursus americanus kermodei"), also known as the "spirit bear" (particularly in British Columbia), is a rare subspecies of the American black bear living in the Central and North Coast regions of British Columbia, Canada.
[d09s001] It is the official provincial mammal of British Columbia.
[d09s002] It is noted for about one-tenth of its population having white or cream-coloured coats like polar bears.

[d01p003] Cinnamon bear
[d01s003] The most striking difference between a cinnamon bear and any other black bear is its brown or red-brown fur, reminiscent of cinnamon.
[d01s004] The subspecies was given the designation because the lighter color phase is more common there than in other areas.

[d00p000] Black Bear Creek
[d00s000] Black Bear Creek is a 116 mi creek in northern Oklahoma.
[d00s001] Black Bear Creek drains an area of 538 sqmi in Garfield County, Noble County and Pawnee County, Oklahoma.
[d00s002] It takes on a red color from the red clay of this area.

context:
[d01p000] Fiat Chrysler Automobiles
[d01s000] Fiat Chrysler Automobiles N.V. (abbreviated as FCA) is an Italian-controlled multinational corporation incorporated in the Netherlands, and currently the world’s seventh-largest auto maker.
[d01s001] The group was established in late 2014 by merging Fiat S.p.A. into a new holding company, FCA (with headquarters in London) for tax purposes.
[d01s002] The holding company is listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Borsa Italiana in Milan.

[d05p000] Fiat S.p.A.
[d05s000] Fiat S.p.A., or "Fabbrica Italiana Automobili Torino" (Italian Automobile Factory of Turin), was an Italian holding company whose original and core activities were in the automotive industry, and that was succeeded by Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV (FCA).
[d05s001] The Fiat Group contained many brands such as Ferrari, Maserati, Fiat, Alfa Romeo, the Chrysler Group, and many more.
[d05s002] On 29 January 2014, it was announced that Fiat S.p.A. (the former owner of Fiat Group) was to be merged into a new Netherlands-based holding company Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV (FCA), took place before the end of 2014.

[d02p000] Fiat Industrial
[d02s000] Fiat Industrial S.p.A. was an Italian company into which Fiat S.p.A. (parent company of Fiat Group) demerged most of its activities not directly related to automobiles at the start of 2011.
[d02s001] Fiat Industrial served as a holding company for the activities of truck manufacturer Iveco; an 89.3% stake in the agricultural and construction equipment producer CNH Global; and FPT Industrial, which consists of the industrial and marine activities formerly part of Fiat Powertrain Technologies.
[d02s002] The company's Chairman was Sergio Marchionne, who also served as CEO of Fiat S.p.A. and Chairman/CEO of Chrysler Group LLC, now merged as Fiat Chrysler Automobiles.

[d07p000] Luca Cordero di Montezemolo
[d07s000] Luca Cordero di Montezemolo (] ; born 31 August 1947) is an Italian businessman, former Chairman of Ferrari, and formerly Chairman of Fiat S.p.A. and President of Confindustria and FIEG.
[d07s001] He comes from an aristocratic family from the region of Piedmont in Italy.
[d07s002] He graduated with a degree in law from La Sapienza University in 1971.

context:
[d09p000] Mr. Nice Guy (1997 film)
[d09s000] Mr. Nice Guy (一個好人, LSHK "Jat1 go3 hou2 jan4") is a 1997 Hong Kong action film directed by Sammo Hung, who makes a cameo as an unfortunate cyclist.
[d09s001] The film stars Jackie Chan and Richard Norton.
[d09s002] The film was released in the Hong Kong on January 31, 1997.

[d07p003] Baadshah (1999 film)
[d07s003] Shahrukh Khan earned a Filmfare Award nomination for Best Performance in a Comic Role.
[d07s004] It is inspired from films such as "Nick of Time", "Rush Hour", "If Looks Could Kill", "Mr Nice Guy", "The Mask".

[d00p000] Rob-B-Hood
[d00s000] Rob-B-Hood (, also known as Robin-B-Hood, literally: Baby Project) is a 2006 Hong Kong action comedy film written, produced and directed by Benny Chan, and starring Jackie Chan, Louis Koo, Yuen Biao and Michael Hui.
[d00s001] The film was produced with a budget of HK$130 million (US$16.8 million) and filmed between December 2005 and January 2006.
[d00s002] "Rob-B-Hood" is the first film in over 30 years in which Jackie Chan plays an anti-hero.

[d06p000] City Hunter (film)
[d06s000] City Hunter (; "Sing si lip yan") is a 1993 Hong Kong action comedy film written and directed by Wong Jing, starring Jackie Chan, Joey Wong, Kumiko Goto and Chingmy Yau.
[d06s001] The film is based on the Japanese manga of the same name.
[d06s002] The film was released in the Hong Kong on 14 January 1993 along with Stephen Chow's "Fight Back to School III".

[d03p000] Project A Part II
[d03s000] Project A Part II (; aka Jackie Chan’s Project A II) is a 1987 Hong Kong action film written and directed by Jackie Chan, who also starred in the lead role.
[d03s001] It is the sequel to the 1983 film "Project A".
[d03s002] Jackie Chan plays "Sergeant Dragon Ma" once again, Sammo Hung and Yuen Biao, stars from the original film, are absent.

[d08p000] Jackie Chan Hill
[d08s000] Jackie Chan Hill or Jackie Chan Village (Indonesian: "Kampung Jackie Chan"; formally: "The Friendship Village of Indonesia-China") is a neighbourhood in Banda Aceh, Indonesia.
[d08s001] It is named for Chinese actor Jackie Chan who, with other Hong Kong actors, helped fund the building of the community and purchase of the hill.
[d08s002] Jackie Chan also campaigned with the Hong Kong Red Cross to raise additional relief funds that went to reconstruction of the site.

[d01s000] Who Am I?
[d01s001] (, also known as Jackie Chan's Who Am I?)

[d04p000] Police Story 4: First Strike
[d04s000] Police Story 4: First Strike (, often released as Jackie Chan's First Strike) is a 1996 Hong Kong action film written and directed by Stanley Tong, starring Jackie Chan, Jackson Lou, Wu Chen-chun and Bill Tung.
[d04s001] The film was released in Hong Kong on 10 February 1996.

[d02p000] Police Story 3: Super Cop
[d02s000] Police Story 3: Super Cop (), also known as Super Cop in North America, is a 1992 Hong Kong action comedy film starring Jackie Chan and Michelle Yeoh.

[d02s002] It is the first in the "Police Story" series not to be directed by Jackie, with Stanley Tong taking over the helm.

question: Was the 2007 documentary 'Zoo' more successful than the 1998 documentary 'Divine Trash'?
context:
[d09p000] Divine Trash [d09s000] Divine Trash is a 1998 documentary film directed by Steve Yeager about the life and work of John Waters. [d01p000] Zoo (2007 film) [d01s000] Zoo is a 2007 American documentary film based on the life and death of Kenneth Pinyan, an American man who died of peritonitis due to perforation of the colon after engaging in an unusual tryst involving receptive anal sex with a horse. context:

[d05p000] Ulrich Walter
[d05s000] Prof. Dr. Ulrich Hans Walter (born February 9, 1954) is a German physicist/engineer and a former DFVLR astronaut.

[d02p003] Martial Henri Valin
[d02s003] He commanded the Free French Air Forces from July 1941 to June 1944, and was then Chief of General Staff of the French Air Army from October 1944 until 1946.
[d02s004] He participated in both World Wars and the Rif War.

[d04p000] Jean-Paul Paloméros
[d04s000] Jean-Paul Paloméros (born 13 August 1953 in Paris) is a retired general of the French Air Force and served as Supreme Allied Commander Transformation, a senior military post in NATO.
[d04s001] Paloméros previously served as Chief of Staff of the French Air Force from 2009 to 2012.

[d01p003] Jean-Philippe Douin
[d01s003] For most of his flying career, Douin piloted the Dassault Mirage III and the Dassault Mirage 5, commanding a squadron, wing and fighter group, before becoming the French Air Attache to Pakistan and Chile.
[d01s004] After entering the General Ranks he served variously as a doctrinal specialist in the Air Force Staff & Training Command, the chief of Aerial Intelligence for a Fighter Division, and Commander of a Fighter Division.

[d02p000] Martial Henri Valin
[d02s000] Martial Henri Valin (14 May 1898 in Limoges – 19 September 1980 in Neuilly-sur-Seine) was a French Air Force general.
[d02s001] He initially served as a cavalryman in the First World War.
[d02s002] After nine years cavalry service in the "chasseurs d'Afrique", dragoons, spahis, and hussars, he eventually volunteered for the French Army's aviation branch, the "aéronautique militaire", in 1926.

[d01p000] Jean-Philippe Douin
[d01s000] Jean-Philippe Douin (8 April 1940 – 19 January 2016) was a French Air Force general.
[d01s001] He was the Chief of Staff of the French Air Force from 1994 to 1995 and Chief of the Defence Staff from 1995 to 1998.
[d01s002] There was some controversy surrounding his appointment since, as a Conscript between 1958 and 1959, he had served in a French Marine Light Cavalry/Light Armored Reconnaissance Regiment (Régiment d'infanterie-chars de marine) in Algeria that was accused of committing war crimes during the Algerian War; later, as a young Air Force Lieutenant and Dassault Mirage III fighter pilot in 1961, his unit had taken part in the Algiers Putsch under the command of Air Vice Marashal Jouhaud.

[d08p003] French Air Force
[d08s003] The French Air Force has 241 combat aircraft in service, with the majority being 133 Dassault Mirage 2000 and 108 Dassault Rafale.
[d08s004] As of early 2017, the French Air Force employs a total of 41,160 regular personnel.
[d08s005] The reserve element of the air force consisted of 5,187 personnel of the Operational Reserve.

[d08p000] French Air Force
[d08s000] The French Air Force (French: "Armée de l'air" ] , literally "air army") is the air force of the French Armed Forces.
[d08s001] It was formed in 1909 as the "Service Aéronautique", a service arm of the French Army, then was made an independent military arm in 1934.
[d08s002] The number of aircraft in service with the French Air Force varies depending on source, however sources from the French Ministry of Defence give a figure of 658 aircraft in 2014.

[d03p000] Fusiliers Commandos de l'Air
[d03s000] The Fusiliers Commandos de l'Air (French for "Fusilier commandos of the Air (force)") of France's Armée de l'Air (French Air Force) are equivalent to the United Kingdom's RAF Regiment, Germany's Objektschutzregiment der Luftwaffe or the United States Air Force's United States Air Force Security Forces.
[d03s001] They are airmen armed and trained as infantry, who provide ground defense of air bases and secure forward base areas.
[d03s002] They also participate in forward air control, combat search and rescue missions, and as air assault infantry.

[d05s000] Errors of impunity is a term used in Brian Forst's book "Errors of Justice" and in Robert Bohm's introduction to a special edition of "The Journal of Criminal Justice" on miscarriages of justice.
[d05s001] They are defined as lapses that result in criminals either remaining at large or receiving sanctions that are below a socially optimal level.
[d05s002] If convicting an innocent person, called a miscarriage of justice, is a Type I error for falsely identifying culpability (a "false positive"), then an error of impunity would be a Type II error of failing to find a culpable person guilty (a "false negative").

[d02s000] A description error or selection error is an error, or more specifically a human error, that occurs when a person performs the correct action on the wrong object due to insufficient specification of an action which would have led to a desired result.
[d02s001] This commonly happens when similar actions lead to different results.
[d02s002] A typical example is a panel with rows of identical switches, where it is easy to carry out a correct action (flip a switch) on a wrong switch due to their insufficient differentiation.

[d08s004] As of early 2017, the French Air Force employs a total of 41,160 regular personnel.
[d08s005] The reserve element of the air force consisted of 5,187 personnel of the Operational Reserve.

[d03p000] Fusiliers Commandos de l'Air
[d03s000] The Fusiliers Commandos de l'Air (French for "Fusilier commandos of the Air (force)") of France's Armée de l'Air (French Air Force) are equivalent to the United Kingdom's RAF Regiment, Germany's Objektschutzregiment der Luftwaffe or the United States Air Force's United States Air Force Security Forces.
[d03s001] They are airmen armed and trained as infantry, who provide ground defense of air bases and secure forward base areas.

[d02p000] Martial Henri Valin
[d02s000] Martial Henri Valin (14 May 1898 in Limoges – 19 September 1980 in Neuilly-sur-Seine) was a French Air Force general.
[d02s001] He initially served as a cavalryman in the First World War.
[d02s002] After nine years cavalry service in the "chasseurs d'Afrique", dragoons, spahis, and hussars, he eventually volunteered for the French Army's aviation branch, the "aéronautique militaire", in 1926.

[d01p000] Jean-Philippe Douin
[d01s000] Jean-Philippe Douin (8 April 1940 – 19 January 2016) was a French Air Force general.
[d01s001] He was the Chief of Staff of the French Air Force from 1994 to 1995 and Chief of the Defence Staff from 1995 to 1998.
[d01s002] There was some controversy surrounding his appointment since, as a Conscript between 1958 and 1959, he had served in a French Marine Light Cavalry/Light Armored Reconnaissance Regiment (Régiment d'infanterie-chars de marine) in Algeria that was accused of committing war crimes during the Algerian War; later, as a young Air Force Lieutenant and Dassault Mirage III fighter pilot in 1961, his unit had taken part in the Algiers Putsch under the command of Air Vice Marashal Jouhaud.

[d08p000] French Air Force
[d08s000] The French Air Force (French: "Armée de l'air" ] , literally "air army") is the air force of the French Armed Forces.
[d08s001] It was formed in 1909 as the "Service Aéronautique", a service arm of the French Army, then was made an independent military arm in 1934.
[d08s002] The number of aircraft in service with the French Air Force varies depending on source, however sources from the French Ministry of Defence give a figure of 658 aircraft in 2014.

question: What Dutch painter specialized in domestic interior scenes of middle class life and has a painting of a young woman dressed in a yellow shawl in the Louvre, Paris?
context:
[d01p000] The Lacemaker (Vermeer)

question: Who was a higher ranked tennis player: Paola Suárez or Michael Venus?
context:
[d00p000] Paola Suárez
[d00s000] Paola Suárez (born 23 June 1976) is a retired professional tennis player from Argentina.
[d00s001] She was one of the most prominent women's doubles players throughout the early and mid-2000s, winning eight Grand Slam titles, all of them with Virginia Ruano Pascual, and holding the No. 1 doubles ranking for 87 non-consecutive weeks.
[d00s002] She was also a singles semifinalist at the 2004 French Open.

[d04p000] Michael Venus (tennis)
[d04s000] Michael Venus (born 16 October 1987) is a New Zealand professional tennis player.
[d04s001] He reached a career high singles ranking of 274 in July 2011, but is much better known as a leading doubles player with a huge serve.
[d04s002] His highest ranking in this discipline is 12, gained in July 2017.

[d04p003] Michael Venus (tennis)
[d04s003] He won the final of the 2017 French Open partnering with American Ryan Harrison, and followed that with a runner-up finish in the 2017 US Open mixed doubles with Chan Hao-ching of Chinese Taipei as his partner.

[d03p000] Clarisa Fernández
[d03s000] Clarisa Fernández (born 28 August 1981) is a retired Argentine tennis player who is best known for her semi-final appearance at the 2002 French Open, the first Argentine since Sabatini in 1992 to reach that stage.
[d03s001] Fernández was ranked 87th in the world at the time of her shocking result.
[d03s002] She defeated, in order: (Q) Lubomira Bacheva, Jelena Kostanić, Kim Clijsters, (13) Elena Dementieva, Paola Suárez, before losing to second-seeded Venus Williams in straight sets.

[d01p000] 1999 Copa Colsanitas – Singles
[d01s000] The 1999 Copa Colsanitas – Singles was the singles event of the second edition of the Copa Colsanitas; a WTA Tier IV tournament and the most prestigious women's tennis tournament held in Colombia and Hispanic America.
[d01s001] Paola Suárez was the defending champion but lost in the semifinals to Christína Papadáki.

[d02p000] 1999 Egger Tennis Festival – Doubles
[d02s000] The 1999 Egger Tennis Festival – Singles was the singles event of the twenty-ninth edition of the Egger Tennis Festival; a WTA Tier IV tournament and the second most prestigious women's tennis tournament held in Austria.
[d02s001] Laura Montalvo and Paola Suárez were the defending champions, but they didn't compete together this year.
[d02s002] Montalvo played with Olga Lugina as the third seed, while Suárez teamed up with Virginia Ruano Pascual as the second seed.

[d08p000] 1999 Brasil Open – Doubles
[d08s000] The 1999 Brasil Open – Doubles was the tennis doubles event of the first edition of the most prestigious tournament in Brazil.
[d08s001] Argentinian team Laura Montalvo and Paola Suárez won the title, in what was the team's second title of the year, defeating Janette Husárová and Florencia Labat in the final.

[d06p000] 1999 Copa Colsanitas – Doubles
[d06s000] The 1999 Copa Colsanitas – Doubles was the doubles event of the second edition of the Copa Colsanitas; a WTA Tier IV tournament and the most prestigious women's tennis tournament held in Colombia and Hispanic America.
[d06s001] Janette Husárová and Paola Suárez were the defending champions but only Suárez competed that year with Laura Montalvo.

[d05p000] 1999 Italian Open – Women's Doubles
[d05s000] The 1999 Italian Open – Doubles was the doubles event of the fifty-fifth edition of the tennis tournament played at Rome, Italy, the most prestigious tennis tournament in Southern Europe.
[d05s001] It was the fifth WTA Tier I tournament of the year, and part of the European claycourt season.
[d05s002] Virginia Ruano Pascual and Paola Suárez were the defending champions, but lost to Martina Hingis and Anna Kournikova in the quarterfinals.

[d09p000] Patricia Tarabini
[d09s000] Patricia Tarabini (born 6 August 1968) is an Argentine former tennis player.
[d09s001] Tarabini represented her country and won the bronze Olympic medal at the 2004 Athens games, with Paola Suárez, where they lost 7–9 in the third set to eventual gold medalists from China, Sun Tiantian and Li Ting.
[d09s002] On May 9, 1988, Patricia reached her highest singles ranking; world number 29.

question: Which breed of dog was first recognized by their country's official kennel club, the American Hairless Terrier or the Saint-Usuge Spaniel?
context:
[d06p000] Saint-Usuge Spaniel
[d06s000] The Saint-Usuge Spaniel (or Épagneul de Saint-Usuge) is a breed of Spaniel originating in the Bresse region of France.
[d06s001] The breed has origins dating back to at least the 16th century, but was nearly extinct by the end of World War II.
[d06s002] Through the efforts of Father Robert Billard, the breed was resurrected during the second half of the 20th century; its national breed club was founded in 1990.

[d06p003] Saint-Usuge Spaniel
[d06s003] The breed was recognised by the Société Centrale Canine (French Kennel Club) in 2003.

[d00p000] American Hairless Terrier
[d00s000] The American Hairless Terrier is a rare breed of dog that was derived as a variant of Rat Terrier.
[d00s001] As of January 1, 2004, the United Kennel Club deemed the AHT a separate terrier breed, granting it full UKC recognition.
[d00s002] An intelligent, social and energetic working breed, the American Hairless Terrier is often listed as a potential good breed choice for allergy sufferers.

[d01p000] American Russell Terrier Club
[d01s000] The American Russell Terrier Club (formerly named the English Jack Russell Terrier Club), founded by JoAnn Stoll in 1995, was the first registry in the United States to maintain the Russell Terrier as a separate breed from the Parson Russell Terrier.
[d01s001] The American Jack Russell Terrier Club is affiliated with both the United Kennel Club and the American Kennel Club.
[d01s002] The purpose of the early founders was to establish a registry for the perpetuation and development of the Russell Terrier as a pure strain of working Jack Russell Terrier keeping their blood and type pure within the registry to works towards Kennel Club recognition as an official breed in the US.

[d01p003] American Russell Terrier Club
[d01s003] On January 1, 2001, the United Kennel Club recognized the Russell Terrier as an official breed, designating only the stock from the American Russell Terrier Club as Foundation stock for the UKC Russell Terrier.
[d01s004] In 2004 the American Russell Terrier Club submitted an official request to include the American Russell Terrier Club stock into the AKC FSS Program to work towards becoming an official breed under the perimeters.
[d01s005] On December 8, 2004, the AKC officially accepted the Russell Terrier.

[d09p006] English Springer Spaniel
[d09s006] The smaller "cockers" hunted woodcock while the larger littermates were used to flush, or "spring," game.
[d09s007] In 1902, The Kennel Club recognized the English Springer Spaniel as a distinct breed.
[d09s008] They are used as sniffer dogs on a widespread basis.

[d09p000] English Springer Spaniel
[d09s000] The English Springer Spaniel is a breed of gun dog in the Spaniel family traditionally used for flushing and retrieving game.
[d09s001] It is an affectionate, excitable breed with a typical lifespan of twelve to fourteen years.
[d09s002] They are very similar to the Welsh Springer Spaniel and are descended from the Norfolk or Shropshire Spaniels of the mid-19th century; the breed has diverged into separate show and working lines.

[d08p000] Welsh Springer Spaniel
[d08s000] The Welsh Springer Spaniel is a breed of dog and a member of the spaniel family.
[d08s001] Thought to be comparable to the old Land Spaniel, they are similar to the English Springer Spaniel and historically have been referred to as both the Welsh Spaniel and the Welsh Cocker Spaniel.
[d08s002] They were relatively unknown until a succession of victories in dog trials by the breed increased its popularity.

[d08p003] Welsh Springer Spaniel
[d08s003] Following recognition by The Kennel Club in 1902, the breed gained the modern name of Welsh Springer Spaniel.
[d08s004] The breed's coat only comes in a single colour combination of white with red markings, usually in a piebald pattern.
[d08s005] Loyal and affectionate, they can become very attached to family members and are wary of strangers.

[d04p000] Terrier Group
[d04s000] Terrier Group is the name of a breed Group of dogs, used by kennel clubs to classify a defined collection of dog breeds.
[d04s001] In general, a "Terrier Group" includes one particular type of dog, the Terrier, although other types may be included in a kennel club's "Terrier Group".
[d04s002] Most major English-language kennel clubs include a "Terrier Group" although different kennel clubs may not include the same breeds in their "Terrier Group".

[d03p000] Massive Attack
[d03s000] Massive Attack are an English trip hop group formed in 1988 in Bristol, consisting of Robert "3D" Del Naja, Grant "Daddy G" Marshall and formerly Andy "Mushroom" Vowles ("Mush").
[d03s001] Their debut album "Blue Lines" was released in 1991, with the single "Unfinished Sympathy" reaching the charts and later being voted the 63rd greatest song of all time in a poll by "NME".
[d03s002] 1998's "Mezzanine", containing "Teardrop", and 2003's "100th Window" charted in the UK at number one.

[d09p000] Massive Attack discography
[d09s000] The discography of British trip hop group Massive Attack consists of five studio albums, three compilation albums, five remix albums, one soundtrack album, five extended plays, eighteen singles and twenty-seven music videos.
[d09s001] The group were founded in 1988 by musicians Robert "3D" Del Naja, Grantley "Daddy G" Marshall, Andrew "Mushroom" Vowles and Adrian "Tricky" Thaws in Bristol, England.
[d09s002] Prior to the formation of Massive Attack, all three were members of British sound system The Wild Bunch.

[d07p003] Massive Attack (song)
[d07s003] The song was a distinct change in Minaj's previous work on mixtapes and features, thus receiving mixed to positive reviews from critics, commending lyrical content and distinctiveness, and critiquing that it did not fit her "Barbie" persona well.
[d07s004] An accompanying music video which features a helicopter chase, and militaristic jungle and desert scenes, was positively received.

[d04p000] Dodgy
[d04s000] Dodgy are an English power pop rock trio, that rose to prominence during the Britpop era of the 1990s.
[d04s001] They are best known for their hits "Staying Out for the Summer", "If You're Thinking of Me", and "Good Enough".
[d04s002] The last was their biggest hit reaching No. 4 in the UK Singles Chart.

[d08p000] Unfinished Sympathy
[d08s000] "Unfinished Sympathy" is a song by English trip hop group Massive Attack, released under the temporary group name of Massive.
[d08s001] It was written by the three band members Robert "3D" Del Naja, Andrew "Mushroom" Vowles and Grant "Daddy G" Marshall, the song's vocalist Shara Nelson and the group's co-producer Jonathan "Jonny Dollar" Sharp.
[d08s002] The song was released as the second single from the band's debut album "Blue Lines", on the band's Wild Bunch label distributed through Circa Records on 11 February 1991.

[d00p000] Protection (Massive Attack song)
[d00s000] "Protection" is a collaboration between Massive Attack and Everything But the Girl singer Tracey Thorn, that appeared on Massive Attack's second album "Protection" on CD and 12" in 1994 as a second single.
[d00s001] It reached number 14 on the UK Singles Chart, staying there for four weeks.
[d00s002] The song was also included on Everything But the Girl's compilations "The Best of" and "Like the Deserts Miss the Rain".

[d01p000] Four Walls / Paradise Circus
[d01s000] "Four Walls / Paradise Circus" is a collaboration between Massive Attack and Burial, which was first released as a limited vinyl edition on 17 October 2011, with pre-orders from 10 October 2011.
[d01s001] The single consists of Burial mixes of Massive Attack's previously unreleased track "Four Walls", and of "Paradise Circus", which was featured in their 2010 album "Heligoland".

[d01s000] Helen Elizabeth Hunt (born June 15, 1963) is an American actress, director, and screenwriter.
[d01s001] She starred in the sitcom "Mad About You" for seven years, and played single mother Carol Connelly in the 1997 romantic comedy film "As Good as It Gets", for which she won the Academy Award for Best Actress.
[d01s002] Some of her other notable films include "Twister" (1996), "Cast Away" (2000), "What Women Want" (2000), "Pay It Forward" (2000), and "The Sessions" (2012), the latter garnered her a second Academy Award nomination.

[d04p000] Dan Schneider (TV producer)
[d04s000] Dan Schneider (born January 14, 1966) is an American actor, television and film writer, and producer.
[d04s001] After appearing in mostly supporting roles in a number of 1980s and 1990s films and TV shows, Schneider devoted himself to behind-the-scenes work in production.
[d04s002] He is the co-president of television production company Schneider's Bakery.

[d02p000] Helen Hunt Falls
[d02s000] Helen Hunt Falls is a waterfall located on Cheyenne Creek in the North Cheyenne Cañon Park of Colorado Springs, Colorado.
[d02s001] The falls are named in honor of Helen Maria Hunt Jackson (October 15, 1830 – August 12, 1885), a United States poet and writer who became an activist on behalf of improved treatment of Native Americans by the U.S. government.
[d02s002] She died in San Francisco, California in 1885 and was later buried in Colorado Springs.

[d09s001] The film stars Helen Hunt, Luke Wilson, Brenton Thwaites and Leonor Varela.
[d09s002] The film had a limited release in theaters and was released on video on demand beginning on May 1, 2015 by Screen Media Films.

[d03s000] Schneider's Bakery, DANWARP Inc. is a television production company founded by Dan Schneider.
