question: What type of profession does Chris Jericho and Gary Barlow have in common?
context:
[d01p003] Gary Barlow
[d01s003] Barlow is one of Britain's most successful songwriters, having written fourteen number one singles and twenty-four top 10 hits.
[d01s004] He has had three number one singles, six top 10 singles and two number one albums as a solo artist, and has had seventeen top 5 hits, twelve number one singles and seven number one albums with Take That.
[d01s005] He is also a six-time recipient of the Ivor Novello Award and has sold over 50 million records worldwide.

[d04p000] Chris Jericho
[d04s000] Christopher Keith Irvine (born November 9, 1970), better known by the ring name Chris Jericho, is a Canadian-American professional wrestler, musician, media personality, actor, author, podcaster, and businessman signed to WWE on the SmackDown brand, where he is currently on a hiatus due to an expected tour with Fozzy.
[d04s001] He is known for his over-the-top, rockstar persona.

[d02p000] Gary Barlow: In Concert
[d02s000] Gary Barlow: In Concert was the first full solo tour that Gary Barlow had performed in over 13 years.
[d02s001] Leg 1 saw him performing songs from his "incredible music career spanning over 20 years" in front of a sell out audience, whilst also raising money for The Prince's Trust and The Foundation of Prince William and Prince Harry during two nights at the Royal Albert Hall.
[d02s002] It was announced on 15 October 2012 that Barlow would go on a full solo tour for his second leg of shows, lasting two months around the UK and Ireland.

[d06p006] List of songs recorded by Gary Barlow
[d06s006] Barlow worked with American songwriter Dianne Warren with whom he co-wrote the song "My Commitment" for the album.
[d06s007] Howard Perdew and Andy Spooner wrote "So Help Me Girl", a single for which Barlow recorded a Spanish language version titled "Ayúdame" (English: "Help Me").

[d05p000] Gary Barlow: On Her Majesty's Service
[d05s000] Gary Barlow: On Her Majesty's Service is a documentary featuring the process of Gary Barlow writing the Queen's Diamond Jubilee official single and travelling across The Commonwealth enlisting the help of singers and musicians to feature in the track.

[d03p000] Fozzy
[d03s000] Fozzy is an American heavy metal band formed in Atlanta, Georgia, in 1999 by lead singer Chris Jericho and guitarist Rich Ward.
[d03s001] The band is currently signed to Century Media Records and has released two studio albums through this label.
[d03s002] The band's current lineup consists of Chris Jericho, Rich Ward, Frank Fontsere, Billy Grey and Paul Di Leo.

[d07p000] Children in Need Rocks the Royal Albert Hall
[d07s000] Children in Need Rocks the Royal Albert Hall was a charity music concert held at the Royal Albert Hall in London, England on 12 November 2009.

question: What Dutch painter specialized in domestic interior scenes of middle class life and has a painting of a young woman dressed in a yellow shawl in the Louvre, Paris?
context:
[d01p000] The Lacemaker (Vermeer)
[d01s000] The Lacemaker is a painting by the Dutch artist Johannes Vermeer (1632–1675), completed around 1669–1670 and held in the Louvre, Paris.
[d01s001] The work shows a young woman dressed in a yellow shawl, holding up a pair of bobbins in her left hand as she carefully places a pin in the pillow on which she is making her bobbin lace.
[d01s002] At 24.5 cm x 21 cm (9.6 in x 8.3 in), the work is the smallest of Vermeer's paintings, but in many ways one of his most abstract and unusual.

[d06p000] Johannes Vermeer
[d06s000] Johannes, Jan or Johan Vermeer ( ; ] ; October 1632 – December 1675) was a Dutch painter who specialized in domestic interior scenes of middle-class life.
[d06s001] Vermeer was a moderately successful provincial genre painter in his lifetime.
[d06s002] He evidently was not wealthy, leaving his wife and children in debt at his death, perhaps because he produced relatively few paintings.

[d05p000] Young Woman in a Pearl Necklace (New York City)
[d05s000] Young Woman in a Pearl Necklace (after 1655) is an oil on canvas painting by an unknown painter, after a painting by the Dutch painter Willem Drost.
[d05s001] It is an example of Dutch Golden Age painting and is part of the collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

[d09p000] A Young Woman Reading (Vermeer imitator)
[d09s000] A Young Woman Reading (after 1670s) is an oil on canvas painting by an unknown painter in the manner of the Dutch painter Johannes Vermeer.
[d09s001] It is an example of Dutch Golden Age painting and is part of the collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

[d02p000] Pieter Janssens Elinga
[d02s000] Pieter Janssens Elinga (1623–1682) was a Dutch Golden Age painter, mainly of domestic interior scenes with a strong emphasis on the rectangular geometrical elements of windows, floor tiling paintings, and other elements, and a few genre figures.
[d02s001] He also painted still lifes.

[d07p000] Annunciation (Memling)
[d07s000] The Annunciation is an oil-on-oak panel painting attributed to the Early Netherlandish master Hans Memling.
[d07s001] Completed c. 1482, it was partially transferred to canvas in the 1920s and is today held in the Robert Lehman collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
[d07s002] It shows the Virgin in a domestic interior, two attendant angels, the archangel Gabriel dressed in rich ecclesiastical robes, and a hovering dove.

[d00p000] Co Breman
[d00s000] Ahazueros Jacobus Breman, known as Co (7 December 1865, Zwolle - 18 November 1938, Laren) was a Dutch painter.
[d00s001] He specialized in landscapes, farms and interior scenes, with figures, and was one of the first Pointillist painters in the Netherlands.

[d03p003] Alexis Leon Louis Valbrun
[d03s003] Some of his paintings are displayed at the Fondation Calvet in Avignon, the Palace of Versailles (Philip V of Spain) and the Chateau de Chantilly (Sophie Dawes, Baronne de Feucheres).
[d03s004] His historic painting "La mort de Saphire" (Fine Art Museum in Saint Lo) was exhibited at the Salon in 1843.
[d03s005] In 1846 he decorated the church Saint-Paul-Saint-Louis in Paris.

[d01p003] The Lacemaker (Vermeer)
[d01s003] The canvas used was cut from the same bolt as that used for "A Young Woman Seated at the Virginals", and both paintings seem to have had identical dimensions originally.

[d03p000] Alexis Leon Louis Valbrun
[d03s000] Alexis Leon Louis Valbrun (Paris, January 3, 1803 – Paris, 1852) was a prominent French painter specialized in portraits of the European aristocracy.
[d03s001] He studied under Nicolas Gosse and was a pupil of Antoine-Jean Gros.
[d03s002] He entered the École nationale supérieure des Beaux-Arts in Paris in 1817 and exhibited his work at the Salon (Paris) between 1831 and 1843.

question: What position does Kyle York hold at the internet performance management company Dyn?
context:
[d01p000] Kyle York (entrepreneur)
[d01s000] Kyle York (born November 26, 1982) is an Internet entrepreneur, startup advisor, angel investor, cloud and Infrastructure-as-a-Service expert and sought-after global public speaker on cloud migration, internet security and hybrid cloud strategy.
[d01s001] York is an executive at Dyn, currently serving as Chief Strategy Officer.
[d01s002] Dyn was acquired by Oracle on November 21, 2016.

[d07p000] Dyn (company)
[d07s000] Dyn, Inc. ( ) is an Internet performance management company, offering products to monitor, control, and optimize online infrastructure, and also domain registration services and email products.
[d07s001] The company was acquired by Oracle Corporation in 2016.

[d05p000] Verelo
[d05s000] Verelo, originally based in Toronto, Canada and acquired by infrastructure as a service company Dyn in January 2013, was a website monitoring service that tracks a website's uptime, downtime, and performance.
[d05s001] Verelo monitored websites from multiple locations globally so that it could distinguish actual downtime from routing and access problems.
[d05s002] Verelo argued that downtime can be costly and even take lives, and is now based in Manchester, New Hampshire.

[d04p000] Dynatrace
[d04s000] Dynatrace is an American application performance management (APM) software company with products aimed at the information technology departments and digital business owners of medium and large businesses.
[d04s001] The company's services include performance management software for programs running on-premises and in the cloud.
[d04s002] This software manages the availability and performance of software applications and the impact on user experience in the form of deep transaction tracing, synthetic monitoring, real user monitoring, and network monitoring.

[d08p000] IBM Application Performance Management
[d08s000] IBM Application Performance Management is an offering that enables IT operations and DevOps and personnel to detect, isolate and diagnose problems in their hybrid cloud development and production environments.
[d08s001] The solution is part of the IBM IT Service Management portfolio, which is a key component of IBM Cloud solutions.
[d08s002] The offering provides capabilities such as End User Management (EUM), Application Discovery, Application Diagnostics, Transaction profiling and IT Operations Analytics.

[d06p000] Cognos
[d06s000] Cognos (Cognos Incorporated) was an Ottawa, Ontario-based company making business intelligence (BI) and performance management (PM) software.
[d06s001] Founded in 1969, at its peak Cognos employed almost 3,500 people and served more than 23,000 customers in over 135 countries until being acquired by IBM on January 31, 2008.
[d06s002] While no longer an independent company, the Cognos name continues to be applied to IBM's line of business intelligence and performance management products.

[d00p000] Business performance management
[d00s000] Business performance management is a set of performance management and analytic processes that enables the management of an organization's performance to achieve one or more pre-selected goals.
[d00s001] Synonyms for "business performance management" include "corporate performance management (CPM)" and "enterprise performance management".

[d01p003] Kyle York (entrepreneur)
[d01s003] York also sits on the boards of Datanyze, CloudApp and 3rd Generation family business, YORK Athletics MFG.
[d01s004] where he is a co-founder.
[d01s005] York is also an active angel investor and advisor in dozens of fast growth Internet companies.

[d08p003] IBM Application Performance Management
[d08s003] IBM Application Performance Management solutions are available in both SaaS (software-as-a-service), hybrid and on-premises delivery models.
[d08s004] IBM Application Performance Management was a part of IBM Tivoli brand until 2013.

[d01p006] Kyle York (entrepreneur)
[d01s006] He has been part of eight successful exits as an investor and employee.
[d01s007] Companies he has invested in and worked as a go-to-market (GTM) leader have been acquired by Cisco, Cognizant, New Relic, Oracle and Sophos.

question: In what order does Three Colours: Blue appear in the Three Colours trilogy?
context:
[d05p000] Blue
[d05s000] Blue is the colour between violet and green on the spectrum of visible light.
[d05s001] Human eyes perceive blue when observing light with a wavelength between 450 and 495 nanometres. Blues with a higher frequency and thus a shorter wavelength appear more violet, while those with a lower frequency and a longer wavelength gradually appear more green.
[d05s002] Pure blue, in the middle, has a wavelength of 470 nanometres.

[d04p000] Three Colours: Blue
[d04s000] Three Colours: Blue (French: Trois couleurs : Bleu ) is a 1993 French drama film directed and co-written by Polish filmmaker Krzysztof Kieślowski.
[d04s001] "Blue" is the first of three films that comprise the "Three Colours" trilogy, themed on the French Revolutionary ideals of liberty, equality, and fraternity; it is followed by "" and "".
[d04s002] According to Kieślowski, the subject of the film is liberty, specifically emotional liberty, rather than its social or political meaning.

[d06p000] Three Colours trilogy
[d06s000] The "Three Colours" trilogy (Polish: "Trzy kolory" , French: "Trois couleurs" ) is a three-part film series directed by Krzysztof Kieślowski.
[d06s001] Two of the films were made in French and one primarily in Polish: "" (1993), "" (1994), and "" (1994).
[d06s002] All three were co-written by Kieślowski and Krzysztof Piesiewicz (with story consultants Agnieszka Holland and Sławomir Idziak) and have musical scores by Zbigniew Preisner.

[d03p000] Hokusai Manga
[d03s000] The Hokusai Manga (北斎漫画 , "Hokusai's Sketches") is a collection of sketches of various subjects by the Japanese artist Hokusai.
[d03s001] Subjects of the sketches include landscapes, flora and fauna, everyday life and the supernatural.
[d03s002] The word "manga" in the title does not refer to the contemporary story-telling "manga", as the sketches in the work are not connected to each other.

[d00p000] Three Colours: White
[d00s000] Three Colours: White (French: Trois couleurs : Blanc ) is a 1994 French-Polish comedy-drama film co-written, produced, and directed by Krzysztof Kieślowski.
[d00s001] "White" is the second in "The Three Colors Trilogy", themed on the French Revolutionary ideals, following "" and preceding "".
[d00s002] The film was selected as the Polish entry for the Best Foreign Language Film at the 67th Academy Awards, but was not accepted as a nominee.

[d07p000] City of Sydney flag
[d07s000] The City of Sydney flag is made up of a horizontal triband of three colours – white, gold and blue.
[d07s001] It was designed in 1908.
[d07s002] The top third of the flag features three designs.

[d01p003] Be All That You Can't Be
[d01s003] The vinyl is available in three colours: Blue, orange and white (Hot Topic Exclusive).
[d01s004] Each colour is limited to 500.
[d01s005] The music video for the song was released through Absolute Punk on 6 August 2009.

[d02p000] Colombia (cocktail)
[d02s000] The Colombia is a cocktail containing vodka and curaçao.
[d02s001] The layering effect takes advantage of the variation in density and temperature between the layers.
[d02s002] The drink appears as stacked horizontal layers of yellow, blue and red, which matches the three colours of the Colombian flag.

[d09p000] Requiem for my friend (Preisner)
[d09s000] Requiem for my friend is a major and the first non-film musical work composed by Zbigniew Preisner.
[d09s001] The composition was meant to honour the composer's late friend, the director Krzysztof Kieślowski, with whom he collaborated while working on a number of films, including the famous "Three Colours" trilogy.
[d09s002] The album was released in 1998 although some parts of the work must have been ready upon Kieślowski's passing as Preisner asserted in an interview that "the Requiem had accompanied Krzysztof in his last journey".

[d05p003] Blue
[d05s003] In painting and traditional colour theory, blue is one of the three primary colours of pigments, along with red and yellow, which can be mixed to form a wide gamut of colours.
[d05s004] Red and blue mixed together form violet, blue and yellow together form green.
[d05s005] Blue is also a primary colour in the RGB colour model, used to create all the colours on the screen of a television or computer monitor.

[d03p000] Atatürk Museum, Şişli

[d00p000] İzmir Atatürk Museum
[d00s000] The Izmir Atatürk Museum is a museum in İzmir, Turkey.
[d00s001] Founded by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, a Turkish army officer, revolutionary, and the first President of Turkey, the Izmir Atatürk Museum opened to the public on 11 September 1941, on the 19th anniversary of Atatürk’s arrival in Izmir.

Mustafa Kemal Atatürk (Anahtar)
Mustafa Kemal Atatürk is an outdoor bronze sculpture of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk by Nuray Anahtar, installed outside the Turkish Ambassador's Residence (1606 23rd Street NW), on the periphery of Sheridan Circle, in Embassy Row, Washington, D.C., United States. It was unveiled by the Atatürk Society of America (ASA) in November 2013. It is one of two statues in Washington, D.C. depicting Kemal Atatürk; the other is installed in front of the Embassy of Turkey, which is also located in Embassy Row.

question: Which breed of dog was first recognized by their country's official kennel club, the American Hairless Terrier or the Saint-Usuge Spaniel?
context:
[d06p000] Saint-Usuge Spaniel
[d06s000] The Saint-Usuge Spaniel (or Épagneul de Saint-Usuge) is a breed of Spaniel originating in the Bresse region of France.
[d06s001] The breed has origins dating back to at least the 16th century, but was nearly extinct by the end of World War II.
[d06s002] Through the efforts of Father Robert Billard, the breed was resurrected during the second half of the 20th century; its national breed club was founded in 1990.

[d00p000] American Hairless Terrier
[d00s000] The American Hairless Terrier is a rare breed of dog that was derived as a variant of Rat Terrier.
[d00s001] As of January 1, 2004, the United Kennel Club deemed the AHT a separate terrier breed, granting it full UKC recognition.
[d00s002] An intelligent, social and energetic working breed, the American Hairless Terrier is often listed as a potential good breed choice for allergy sufferers.

[d01p000] American Russell Terrier Club
[d01s000] The American Russell Terrier Club (formerly named the English Jack Russell Terrier Club), founded by JoAnn Stoll in 1995, was the first registry in the United States to maintain the Russell Terrier as a separate breed from the Parson Russell Terrier.
[d01s001] The American Jack Russell Terrier Club is affiliated with both the United Kennel Club and the American Kennel Club.
[d01s002] The purpose of the early founders was to establish a registry for the perpetuation and development of the Russell Terrier as a pure strain of working Jack Russell Terrier keeping their blood and type pure within the registry to works towards Kennel Club recognition as an official breed in the US.

[d09p006] English Springer Spaniel
[d09s006] The smaller "cockers" hunted woodcock while the larger littermates were used to flush, or "spring," game.
[d09s007] In 1902, The Kennel Club recognized the English Springer Spaniel as a distinct breed.
[d09s008] They are used as sniffer dogs on a widespread basis.

[d08p000] Welsh Springer Spaniel
[d08s000] The Welsh Springer Spaniel is a breed of dog and a member of the spaniel family.
[d08s001] Thought to be comparable to the old Land Spaniel, they are similar to the English Springer Spaniel and historically have been referred to as both the Welsh Spaniel and the Welsh Cocker Spaniel.
[d08s002] They were relatively unknown until a succession of victories in dog trials by the breed increased its popularity.

[d04p000] Terrier Group
[d04s000] Terrier Group is the name of a breed Group of dogs, used by kennel clubs to classify a defined collection of dog breeds.
[d04s001] In general, a "Terrier Group" includes one particular type of dog, the Terrier, although other types may be included in a kennel club's "Terrier Group".
[d04s002] Most major English-language kennel clubs include a "Terrier Group" although different kennel clubs may not include the same breeds in their "Terrier Group".

[d06p003] Saint-Usuge Spaniel
[d06s003] The breed was recognised by the Société Centrale Canine (French Kennel Club) in 2003.

[d01p003] American Russell Terrier Club
[d01s003] On January 1, 2001, the United Kennel Club recognized the Russell Terrier as an official breed, designating only the stock from the American Russell Terrier Club as Foundation stock for the UKC Russell Terrier.
[d01s004] In 2004 the American Russell Terrier Club submitted an official request to include the American Russell Terrier Club stock into the AKC FSS Program to work towards becoming an official breed under the perimeters.
[d01s005] On December 8, 2004, the AKC officially accepted the Russell Terrier.

[d09p000] English Springer Spaniel
[d09s000] The English Springer Spaniel is a breed of gun dog in the Spaniel family traditionally used for flushing and retrieving game.
[d09s001] It is an affectionate, excitable breed with a typical lifespan of twelve to fourteen years.
[d09s002] They are very similar to the Welsh Springer Spaniel and are descended from the Norfolk or Shropshire Spaniels of the mid-19th century; the breed has diverged into separate show and working lines.

[d08p003] Welsh Springer Spaniel
[d08s003] Following recognition by The Kennel Club in 1902, the breed gained the modern name of Welsh Springer Spaniel.
[d08s004] The breed's coat only comes in a single colour combination of white with red markings, usually in a piebald pattern.
[d08s005] Loyal and affectionate, they can become very attached to family members and are wary of strangers.

question: Were both the Battle of Stones River and the Battle of the Ch'ongch'on River fought in the 19th century?
context:
[d04p000] Battle of Stones River
[d04s000] The Battle of Stones River or Second Battle of Murfreesboro, was fought from December 31, 1862, to January 2, 1863, in Middle Tennessee, as the culmination of the Stones River Campaign in the Western Theater of the American Civil War.
[d04s001] Of the major battles of the Civil War, Stones River had the highest percentage of casualties on both sides.
[d04s002] Although the battle itself was inconclusive, the Union Army's repulse of two Confederate attacks and the subsequent Confederate withdrawal were a much-needed boost to Union morale after the defeat at the Battle of Fredericksburg, and it dashed Confederate aspirations for control of Middle Tennessee.

[d06p000] Battle of the Ch'ongch'on River
[d06s000] The Battle of the Ch'ongch'on River, also known as the Battle of the Ch'ongch'on () or the Second Phase Campaign Western Sector (), was a decisive battle in the Korean War, and it took place from November 25 to December 2, 1950, along the Ch'ongch'on River Valley in the northwestern part of North Korea.
[d06s001] In response to the successful Chinese First Phase Campaign against the United Nations forces, General Douglas MacArthur launched the Home-by-Christmas Offensive to evict the Chinese forces from Korea and to end the war.
[d06s002] Anticipating this reaction, the Chinese People's Volunteer Army Commander Peng Dehuai planned a counteroffensive, dubbed the "Second Phase Campaign", against the advancing UN forces.

[d05p000] Joseph L. Follett
[d05s000] Joseph Leonard Follett (February 16, 1843 – April 1, 1907) was an American soldier who fought in the American Civil War.
[d05s001] Follett received the country's highest award for bravery during combat, the Medal of Honor, for his action during the Battle of Island Number Ten in New Madrid, Missouri on 3 March 1862 and the Battle of Stones River in Tennessee on 31 December 1862.
[d05s002] He was honored with the award on 19 September 1890.

[d00p000] Battle of Glendale (Skye)
[d00s000] The Battle of Glendale was a battle fought on the Inner Hebridean island of Skye, between the MacDonalds of Sleat and the MacDonalds of Clanranald, against the MacLeods of Harris and Dunvegan and the MacLeods of Lewis.
[d00s001] According to MacLeod tradition preserved in the early 19th century, the battle was fought in about the year 1490; yet it has been recently suggested that the battle more likely took place sometime after 1513.
[d00s002] MacLeod tradition records that the battle was the 'most tremendous battle' that the clan ever fought—although the clan was victorious, it never fully recovered from its severe losses.

[d01p003] Battle of Berestechko
[d01s003] The Polish camp was on the river opposite Berestechko and faced south, towards the Cossack army about two kilometers away, whose right flank was against the River Pliashivka (Pliashova) and the Tatar army on their left flank.
[d01s004] It was probably the largest European land battle of the 17th century.

[d07p003] Savage's Station, Virginia
[d07s003] The house served as the nucleus of a large field hospital during and after the battle of Seven Pines and the Seven Days Battles.
[d07s004] The house also functioned as General George B. McClellan's headquarters during the battle of Savage's Station on June 29, 1862.
[d07s005] Although the house survived the battle in 1862, it was burned by Federal cavalry under General Philip H. Sheridan in 1864.

[d03p003] Umba River (Tanzania)
[d03s003] Just before the Umba flows into the Indian Ocean, it crosses the border to Kenya.
[d03s004] The mouth itself marks the most eastern point on the border between Tanzania and Kenya, which was largely made in a straight line to the northwest towards Lake Victoria in the 19th Century.
[d03s005] On the upper reaches of the river in the mid-1960s rich deposits of precious stones, including sapphires and Spessartine, were discovered.

[d08p003] Collins Ferry Historic District
[d08s003] The Collins Farm includes 19th century farm outbuildings, the family cemetery, a mill site along the river, and the site where stones for the mill's construction and grinding stones were quarried.
[d08s004] The Hubbard Farm is located south and east of the Collins Farm, and is accessed via a private drive that forms part of the historic road leading to Collins Ferry.
[d08s005] Hubbard Farm includes a Greek Revival farmhouse built in 1856, and also includes 19th century outbuildings, a family cemetery, and the remains of a slave quarters.

[d00p003] Battle of Glendale (Skye)
[d00s003] MacLeod tradition relates how the MacDonalds originally had the upper hand during the conflict, but when the MacLeod's sacred Fairy Flag was unfurled the MacLeods gained heart and won the battle.

[d01p000] Battle of Berestechko
[d01s000] The Battle of Berestechko (Polish: "Bitwa pod Beresteczkiem" ; Ukrainian: Берестецька битва, Битва під Берестечком ) was fought between the Ukrainian Cossacks, led by Hetman Bohdan Khmelnytsky, aided by their Crimean Tatar allies, and a Polish army under King John II Casimir.
[d01s001] It was a battle of a Cossack rebellion in Ukraine that took place in the years 1648–1657 after the expiration of a two-year truce.
[d01s002] Fought from 28 to 30 June 1651, the battle took place in the province of Volhynia, on the hilly plain south of the Styr River.

[d05p000] Fatma Lanouar
[d05s000] Fatma Lanouar (Arabic: فاطمة لأنور; born March 14, 1978) is a former female middle distance runner from Tunisia.
[d05s001] She is best known for twice (2001 and 2005) winning the gold medal at the Mediterranean Games in the women's 1500 metres.
[d05s002] Lanouar set her personal best (4:06.91) in the 1,500 metres in 2000.

[d09p000] Mediterranean Games
[d09s000] The Mediterranean Games are a multi-sport games held usually every four years, between nations around or very close to the Mediterranean Sea, where Europe, Africa, and Asia meet.
[d09s001] The games are under the auspices of the International Committee of Mediterranean Games (CIJM).

[d02p000] Olympic Games
[d02s000] The modern Olympic Games or Olympics (French: "Jeux olympiques" ) are leading international sporting events featuring summer and winter sports competitions in which thousands of athletes from around the world participate in a variety of competitions.
[d02s001] The Olympic Games are considered the world's foremost sports competition with more than 200 nations participating.
[d02s002] The Olympic Games are held every four years, with the Summer and Winter Games alternating by occurring every four years but two years apart.

[d00p000] European Masters Games
[d00s000] The European Masters Games (EMG) is a multi-sport event, consisting of summer sports, that is held every four years.
[d00s001] The age categories vary depending on the sport but the competition is generally for people 30–35 years or older.
[d00s002] The first games were held in 2008 in Malmö, Sweden.

[d04p000] Winter Olympic Games
[d04s000] The Olympic Winter Games (official name) (French: "Jeux olympiques d'hiver" ) is a major international sporting event held once every four years, for sports practised on snow and ice.
[d04s001] The first Winter Olympics, the 1924 Winter Olympics, was held in Chamonix, France.
[d04s002] The original five sports (broken into nine disciplines) were bobsleigh, curling, ice hockey, Nordic skiing (consisting of the disciplines military patrol, cross-country skiing, Nordic combined, and ski jumping), and skating (consisting of the disciplines figure skating and speed skating).

[d06p000] Women's Rugby World Cup
[d06s000] The Women's Rugby World Cup is the premier international competition in rugby union for women.
[d06s001] The tournament is organised by the sport's governing body, World Rugby.
[d06s002] The championships are currently held every four years; the event was most recently held in France in August 2014.

[d05p003] Fatma Lanouar
[d05s003] She was also the silver medallist at the 2001 Jeux de la Francophonie.

[d00p003] European Masters Games
[d00s003] The European Masters Games are held once every four year, while the last games were held in 2015 in Nice, France, the next games will be celebrated in Torino, Italy, in 2019.
[d00s004] The International Masters Games Association (IMGA), which is based in Lausanne, Switzerland, is the body responsible for the bidding and placing of the games.

[d04p003] Winter Olympic Games
[d04s003] The Games were held every four years from 1924 to 1936, interrupted in 1940 and 1944 by World War II, and resumed in 1948.
[d04s004] Until 1992 the Winter and Summer Olympic Games were held in the same years, but in accordance with a 1986 decision by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) to place the Summer and Winter Games on separate four-year cycles in alternating even-numbered years, the next Winter Olympics after 1992 was in 1994.

question: What position does Kyle York hold at the internet performance management company Dyn?
context:
[d01p000] Kyle York (entrepreneur)
[d01s000] Kyle York (born November 26, 1982) is an Internet entrepreneur, startup advisor, angel investor, cloud and Infrastructure-as-a-Service expert and sought-after global public speaker on cloud migration, internet security and hybrid cloud strategy.
[d01s001] York is an executive at Dyn, currently serving as Chief Strategy Officer.
[d01s002] Dyn was acquired by Oracle on November 21, 2016.

[d07p000] Dyn (company)
[d07s000] Dyn, Inc. ( ) is an Internet performance management company, offering products to monitor, control, and optimize online infrastructure, and also domain registration services and email products.
[d07s001] The company was acquired by Oracle Corporation in 2016.

[d01p003] Kyle York (entrepreneur)
[d01s003] York also sits on the boards of Datanyze, CloudApp and 3rd Generation family business, YORK Athletics MFG.
[d01s004] where he is a co-founder.
[d01s005] York is also an active angel investor and advisor in dozens of fast growth Internet companies.

[d04p000] Dynatrace
[d04s000] Dynatrace is an American application performance management (APM) software company with products aimed at the information technology departments and digital business owners of medium and large businesses.
[d04s001] The company's services include performance management software for programs running on-premises and in the cloud.
[d04s002] This software manages the availability and performance of software applications and the impact on user experience in the form of deep transaction tracing, synthetic monitoring, real user monitoring, and network monitoring.

[d01p006] Kyle York (entrepreneur)
[d01s006] He has been part of eight successful exits as an investor and employee.
[d01s007] Companies he has invested in and worked as a go-to-market (GTM) leader have been acquired by Cisco, Cognizant, New Relic, Oracle and Sophos.

[d05s001] They are defined as lapses that result in criminals either remaining at large or receiving sanctions that are below a socially optimal level.
[d05s002] If convicting an innocent person, called a miscarriage of justice, is a Type I error for falsely identifying culpability (a "false positive"), then an error of impunity would be a Type II error of failing to find a culpable person guilty (a "false negative").

[d02s001] This commonly happens when similar actions lead to different results.

[d02p000] Tappi Tíkarrass
[d02s000] Tappi Tíkarrass was an Icelandic punk band which added elements of funk, rock and jazz to their music, marking a difference from other traditional bands at that time.
[d02s001] The band is also considered the first serious music project of now renowned singer Björk Guðmundsdóttir.

[d09p000] Miranda (album)
[d09s000] Miranda is the only studio album by Icelandic punk band Tappi Tíkarrass.

[d04p000] Nýtt líf
[d04s000] Nýtt Líf (   , English: "New Life") is an Icelandic film directed by Þráinn Bertelsson and released in 1983.
[d04s001] The film is a comedy shot in the Westman Islands and stars Eggert Þorleifsson and Karl Ágúst Úlfsson, among others.
[d04s002] The music features several musicians including the band Tappi Tíkarrass (of which Björk was a member), which contributed the songs "Sperglar" and "Kukl" (a.k.a. "Seiður").

[d00p000] Bitið fast í vitið
[d00s000] Bitið fast í vitið (roughly "Bite Hard In Your Mind" in Icelandic) is the début EP of Icelander punk/pop group Tappi Tíkarrass .
[d00s001] It was released in late-1982 on the Spor label, within a year of the band's formation in September 1981 – led by vocalists Björk and Eyþór Arnalds .
[d00s002] This was the band's most punk-oriented release and contains five tracks, featuring one in English, "London".

[d03p003] INXS
[d03s003] For twenty years, INXS was fronted by Hutchence, whose "sultry good looks" and magnetic stage presence made him the focal point of the band.
[d03s004] Initially known for their new wave/pop style, the band later developed a harder pub rock style that included funk and dance elements.

[d07p000] Rave music
[d07s000] Rave music may either refer to the late 1980s/early 1990s genres of house, breakbeat, acid house, techno and hardcore techno, which were the first genres of music to be played at rave parties, or to any other genre of electronic dance music (EDM) that may be played at a rave.
[d07s001] The genre "rave", also known as hardcore by early ravers, first appeared amongst the UK "acid" movement during the late 1980s at warehouse parties and other underground venues, as well as on UK pirate radio stations.
[d07s002] The genre would develop into oldschool hardcore, which lead onto newer forms of rave music such as drum and bass and 2-step, as well as other hardcore techno genres, such as gabber, hardstyle and happy hardcore.

[d05p003] Disco polo
[d05s003] Disco polo have enjoyed a renaissance of popularity in late 2007.
[d05s004] Language Dictionary Polish Publishing PWN defines the genre as a Polish variant of disco music, with simple melodies.
[d05s005] It is derived from disco, Euro disco contemporary folk music influenced by Italo disco and Polish folk songs (specifically, the vulgarized subgenre of which is mostly played at weddings and feasts).

[d01p003] Steeltown (band)
[d01s003] The group members were Andy Richmond vocals, Peter Howard keyboards, Terry Gidman drums and Kate Richmond vocals and percussion and Reece Speceis Lead Guitar.
[d01s004] The band were formed from the remnant members of a Scottish group called the Technicians who migrated to Australia in the 80s and who also attained top 40 status with their music releases, Hot for Love, Clockwork Clown and Sodier of Fortune through record companies Powderworks, EMI and BMG, and were published by MMA which was owned by legendary rock outfit INXS.

[d08p000] Folk rock
[d08s000] Folk rock is a music genre combining elements of folk music and rock music.
[d08s001] In its earliest and narrowest sense, the term referred to a genre that arose in the United States and the United Kingdom around the mid-1960s.
[d08s002] The genre emerged from bands such as the Beatles, the Searchers, and the Animals in the UK, and Bob Dylan and the Byrds in the US, who played traditional folk music and songs with rock instrumentation.

[d06p003] Kidandali
[d06s003] The music itself is given this name because most times it is the kind of music played or performed at such local parties and functions.
[d06s004] Some other sources and commentators refer to the genre alternatively as "Band music" while others refer to it as "Afrobeat".

question: What was the company that was co-owned by the person who Abbe error was named after?
context:
[d09p000] Othello error
[d09s000] Othello error occurs when a suspicious observer discounts cues of truthfulness.
[d09s001] Essentially the Othello error occurs, Paul Ekman states, "when the lie catcher fails to consider that a truthful person who is under stress may appear to be lying" their non-verbal signals expressing their worry at the possibility of being disbelieved.
[d09s002] A lie-detector or polygraph may be deceived in the same way, by misinterpreting nervous signals from a truthful person.

[d03p003] Ernst Abbe
[d03s003] He was a co-owner of Carl Zeiss AG, a German manufacturer of research microscopes, astronomical telescopes, planetariums and other optical systems.

[d06p000] Ernst-Abbe-Sportfeld
[d06s000] Ernst Abbe Sportfield is a sports facility in Jena, Germany.
[d06s001] It was dedicated on August 24, 1924 and was named after entrepreneur Ernst Abbe 15 years later.
[d06s002] The facility is in southern Jena, directly on the Saale River.

[d07p000] Abbe error
[d07s000] Abbe error, named after Ernst Abbe, also called sine error, describes the magnification of angular error over distance.
[d07s001] For example, when one measures a point that is 1 meter away at 45 degrees, an angular error of 1 degree corresponds to a positional error of over 1.745 cm, equivalent to a distance-measurement error of 1.745%.

[d04p000] Van Abbemuseum

[d01p000] Fiat Chrysler Automobiles
[d01s000] Fiat Chrysler Automobiles N.V. (abbreviated as FCA) is an Italian-controlled multinational corporation incorporated in the Netherlands, and currently the world’s seventh-largest auto maker.
[d01s001] The group was established in late 2014 by merging Fiat S.p.A. into a new holding company, FCA (with headquarters in London) for tax purposes.
[d01s002] The holding company is listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Borsa Italiana in Milan.

[d05p000] Fiat S.p.A.
[d05s000] Fiat S.p.A., or "Fabbrica Italiana Automobili Torino" (Italian Automobile Factory of Turin), was an Italian holding company whose original and core activities were in the automotive industry, and that was succeeded by Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV (FCA).
[d05s001] The Fiat Group contained many brands such as Ferrari, Maserati, Fiat, Alfa Romeo, the Chrysler Group, and many more.
[d05s002] On 29 January 2014, it was announced that Fiat S.p.A. (the former owner of Fiat Group) was to be merged into a new Netherlands-based holding company Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV (FCA), took place before the end of 2014.

[d02p000] Fiat Industrial
[d02s000] Fiat Industrial S.p.A. was an Italian company into which Fiat S.p.A. (parent company of Fiat Group) demerged most of its activities not directly related to automobiles at the start of 2011.
[d02s001] Fiat Industrial served as a holding company for the activities of truck manufacturer Iveco; an 89.3% stake in the agricultural and construction equipment producer CNH Global; and FPT Industrial, which consists of the industrial and marine activities formerly part of Fiat Powertrain Technologies.
[d02s002] The company's Chairman was Sergio Marchionne, who also served as CEO of Fiat S.p.A. and Chairman/CEO of Chrysler Group LLC, now merged as Fiat Chrysler Automobiles.

[d07s000] Luca Cordero di Montezemolo (] ; born 31 August 1947) is an Italian businessman, former Chairman of Ferrari, and formerly Chairman of Fiat S.p.A. and President of Confindustria and FIEG.
[d07s001] He comes from an aristocratic family from the region of Piedmont in Italy.
[d07s002] He graduated with a degree in law from La Sapienza University in 1971.

[d06s000] Future Italy ("Italia Futura", IF) is an Italian liberal-centrist think tank, formed in 2009 by Luca Cordero di Montezemolo, chairman of Alitalia (since 2014) and former chairman of Ferrari (1991–2014), FIAT (2004–2010) and Confindustria (2004–2008).

[d09s000] Fiat Automobiles S.p.A. (FIAT, Italian: "Fabbrica Italiana Automobili Torino" , 'Italian Automobiles Factory, Turin' ) is the largest automobile manufacturer in Italy, a subsidiary of FCA Italy S.p.A., which is part of Fiat Chrysler Automobiles.
[d09s001] Fiat Automobiles S.p.A. was formed in January 2007 when Fiat reorganized its automobile business, and traces its history back to 1899 when the first Fiat automobile was produced.

[d04s001] The company was founded on 9 March 2010.
[d04s002] Fiat has agreed to invest an initial US$559 million in the venture.

[d06s000] David Edward Williams, OBE (born 20 August 1971), known professionally as David Walliams ( ), is an English comedian, actor, talent-show judge, author, presenter, and activist, known for his partnership with Matt Lucas on the BBC One sketch show "Little Britain."

[d01p000] Montel Williams
[d01s000] Montel Brian Anthony Williams (born July 3, 1956) is an American television personality, radio talk show host, and actor.
[d01s001] He is best known as host of the long-running "The Montel Williams Show", and more recently as a spokesman for the Partnership for Prescription Assistance (PPA), Williams is also active with the nonprofit MS Foundation, which he founded after being diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 1999.

[d04s000] Harold Ray Ragsdale (born January 24, 1939), known professionally as Ray Stevens, is an American country and pop singer-songwriter and comedian, known for his Grammy-winning recordings "Everything Is Beautiful" and "Misty", as well as comedic hits such as "Gitarzan" and "The Streak".

[d05s000] Salomon Brothers was a Wall Street investment bank, known as a bulge bracket company.
[d05s001] Founded in 1910 by three brothers (Arthur, Herbert and Percy) along with a clerk named Ben Levy, it remained a partnership until the early 1980s, when it was acquired by the commodity trading firm Phibro Corporation and became "Salomon Inc." Eventually, Salomon (NYSE:SB) was acquired by Travelers Group in 1998; and, following the latter's merger with Citicorp that same year, Salomon became part of Citigroup.
[d05s002] Although the Salomon name carried on as Salomon Smith Barney, which were the investment banking operations of Citigroup, the name was abandoned in October 2003 after a series of financial scandals that tarnished the bank's reputation.

[d09s000] Donald Clark Paup (April 2, 1939 – August 7, 2012) was an American badminton player who won national and international titles from the mid-1960s to the early 1980s.
[d09s001] Primarily a doubles specialist, he was known for his quick racket and tactical astuteness.
[d09s002] He was ranked first in the U.S. men's doubles for twelve consecutive seasons (1965–1976); all but the last of these in a partnership with fellow left-hander Jim Poole that was consistently competitive at the world class level.

[d03s001] Lysins are highly evolved enzymes that are able to target one of the five bonds in peptidoglycan (murein), the main component of bacterial cell walls, which allows the release of progeny virions from the lysed cell.
[d03s002] Cell-wall-containing Archaea are also lysed by specialized pseudomurein-cleaving lysins, while most archaeal viruses employ alternate mechanisms.

question: Were both the Battle of Stones River and the Battle of the Ch'ongch'on River fought in the 19th century?
context:
[d04p000] Battle of Stones River
[d04s000] The Battle of Stones River or Second Battle of Murfreesboro, was fought from December 31, 1862, to January 2, 1863, in Middle Tennessee, as the culmination of the Stones River Campaign in the Western Theater of the American Civil War.
[d04s001] Of the major battles of the Civil War, Stones River had the highest percentage of casualties on both sides.
[d04s002] Although the battle itself was inconclusive, the Union Army's repulse of two Confederate attacks and the subsequent Confederate withdrawal were a much-needed boost to Union morale after the defeat at the Battle of Fredericksburg, and it dashed Confederate aspirations for control of Middle Tennessee.

[d06p000] Battle of the Ch'ongch'on River
[d06s000] The Battle of the Ch'ongch'on River, also known as the Battle of the Ch'ongch'on () or the Second Phase Campaign Western Sector (), was a decisive battle in the Korean War, and it took place from November 25 to December 2, 1950, along the Ch'ongch'on River Valley in the northwestern part of North Korea.
[d06s001] In response to the successful Chinese First Phase Campaign against the United Nations forces, General Douglas MacArthur launched the Home-by-Christmas Offensive to evict the Chinese forces from Korea and to end the war.
[d06s002] Anticipating this reaction, the Chinese People's Volunteer Army Commander Peng Dehuai planned a counteroffensive, dubbed the "Second Phase Campaign", against the advancing UN forces.

[d01p003] Battle of Berestechko
[d01s003] The Polish camp was on the river opposite Berestechko and faced south, towards the Cossack army about two kilometers away, whose right flank was against the River Pliashivka (Pliashova) and the Tatar army on their left flank.
[d01s004] It was probably the largest European land battle of the 17th century.

question: Which opera has more acts, Parsifal or Manon by Massenet?
context:
[d07p000] Manon
[d07s000] Manon (] ) is an "opéra comique" in five acts by Jules Massenet to a French libretto by Henri Meilhac and Philippe Gille, based on the 1731 novel "L’histoire du chevalier des Grieux et de Manon Lescaut" by the Abbé Prévost.
[d07s001] It was first performed at the Opéra-Comique in Paris on 19 January 1884, with sets designed by Eugène Carpezat (Act I), Auguste-Alfred Rubé and Philippe Chaperon (Acts II and III), and Jean-Baptiste Lavastre (Act IV).

[d01p000] Manon Lescaut (Puccini)
[d01s000] Manon Lescaut is an opera in four acts by Giacomo Puccini, composed between 1890 and 1893.
[d01s001] The story is based on the 1731 novel "L'histoire du chevalier des Grieux et de Manon Lescaut" by the Abbé Prévost and should not be confused with "Manon", an 1884 opera by Jules Massenet based on the same novel.

[d02p000] Manon (disambiguation)
[d02s000] Manon is an opera by Jules Massenet, adapted from Abbé Prévost's novel "Manon Lescaut".

[d06p000] Manon Lescaut (Auber)
[d06s000] Manon Lescaut is an opera or opéra comique in 3 acts by Daniel Auber to a libretto by Eugène Scribe, and, like Puccini's "Manon Lescaut" and Massenet's "Manon", is based on the Abbé Prévost's novel "Manon Lescaut".
[d06s001] Auber's version is nowadays the least-performed of the three.

[d00p000] Parsifal
[d00s000] Parsifal (WWV 111) is an opera in three acts by German composer Richard Wagner.
[d00s001] It is loosely based on "Parzival" by Wolfram von Eschenbach, a 13th-century epic poem of the Arthurian knight Parzival (Percival) and his quest for the Holy Grail (12th century).

[d09p000] L'histoire de Manon
[d09s000] L'histoire de Manon, generally referred to as "Manon", is a ballet choreographed by Kenneth MacMillan to music by Jules Massenet and based on the 1731 novel "Manon Lescaut" by Abbé Prévost.
[d09s001] The ballet was first performed by The Royal Ballet in London in 1974 with Antoinette Sibley and Anthony Dowell in the leading roles.
[d09s002] It continues to be performed and recognised internationally.

[d03p000] Boulevard Solitude
[d03s000] Boulevard Solitude is a "Lyrisches Drama " (lyric drama) or opera in one act by Hans Werner Henze to a German libretto by Grete Weil after the play by Walter Jockisch, in its turn a modern retelling of François Prévost's "Manon Lescaut".
[d03s001] The piece is a reworking of the Manon Lescaut story, already adapted operatically by Auber, Massenet and Puccini, and here relocated to Paris after the Second World War where, as is noted in Grove, the focus of the story moves away from Manon and towards Armand des Grieux.
[d03s002] It became Henze’s first fully-fledged opera.

[d05p000] Massenet Festival
[d05s000] Massenet Festival ("Festival Massenet") is a biennale festival of music by French composer, Jules Massenet held in Saint-Étienne, France, close to the area where the composer was born.
[d05s001] The first Massenet Festival took place in November 1990 when the opera "Cléopâtre" and the oratorio "La Vierge" were presented.
[d05s002] In recent years, performances have been given in the Grand Théâtre Massenet, one of the theatres of the Opéra Théâtre de Saint-Etienne, and formerly known as L'Esplanade.

[d04p003] Renée Fleming
[d04s003] She also speaks fluent German and French, along with limited Italian.
[d04s004] Her signature roles include Countess Almaviva in Mozart's "Le nozze di Figaro", Desdemona in Verdi's "Otello", Violetta in Verdi's "La traviata", the title role in Dvořák's "Rusalka", the title role in Massenet's "Manon", the title role in Massenet's "Thaïs", the title role in Richard Strauss's "Arabella", the Marschallin in "Der Rosenkavalier", and the Countess in "Capriccio".

[d08p003] Jean-Claude Auvray
[d08s003] Among his 150 and more productions are "Tancredi" (Rossini), "La Gioconda" (Ponchielli), "Tristan und Isolde" (Wagner), "Manon" (Massenet), "Peter Grimes" (Britten), "Fidelio" (Beethoven), "Otello, "Aida" (Verdi), "La bohème" and "Gianni Schicchi" (Puccini).
[d08s004] Between 1996 and 2006 he directed plays at the Israeli Opera.

[d02s000] The Wolf Prize in Mathematics is awarded almost annually by the Wolf Foundation in Israel.

[d02s000] Mixed spice, also called pudding spice, is a British blend of sweet spices, similar to the pumpkin pie spice used in the United States.
[d02s001] Cinnamon is the dominant flavour, with nutmeg and allspice.
[d02s002] It is often used in baking, or to complement fruits or other sweet foods.

[d04p000] Sopaipilla
[d04s000] A sopaipilla, sopapilla, sopaipa, or cachanga is a kind of fried pastry and a type of quick bread served in several regions with Spanish heritage in the Americas.
[d04s001] The word sopaipilla is the diminutive of sopaipa, a word that entered Spanish from the Mozarabic language of Al-Andalus.
[d04s002] The original Mozarabic word "Xopaipa" was used to mean bread soaked in oil, and derived in turn from the Germanic word "suppa" which meant bread soaked in liquid.

[d07p000] Churro
[d07s000] A churro (] , ] ) is a fried-dough pastry—predominantly choux—based snack.
[d07s001] Churros are traditional in Spain and Portugal - from where they originate - as well as the Philippines and Ibero-America.
[d07s002] They are also consumed in the Southwestern United States, France and other areas that have received immigration from Spanish and Portuguese-speaking countries.

[d08p000] Cinnamon leaf oil
[d08s000] Cinnamon leaf oil is obtained by steam distillation of cinnamon leaves and the oil yield ranges between 0.5% and 1.8%.
[d08s001] More than 47 compounds have been identified from the leaf oil, the most significant being eugenol, which constitutes 65–92% .
[d08s002] Cinnamon leaf oil is cheaper than bark oil and is used in the flavor industry, to a lesser extent, to flavor confectionary.

[d06p003] Cinnamon roll
[d06s003] Its main ingredients are flour, cinnamon, sugar, and butter, which provide a robust and sweet flavor.
[d06s004] In some places, it is eaten as a breakfast food and is served with cream cheese or icing.

[d03p000] Cruller
[d03s000] A traditional cruller (or twister) is a fried pastry often made from a rectangle of dough, with a cut made in the middle that allows it to be pulled over and through itself producing twists in the sides of the pastry.
[d03s001] Crullers have been described as resembling "a small, braided torpedo" and having been "a staple of the New England diet since the Pilgrims' day".
[d03s002] Some other cruller styles are made of a denser dough somewhat like that of a cake doughnut formed in a small loaf or stick shape, but not always twisted.

[d05p000] Nuegados
[d05s000] Nuegados is a traditional plate from many different countries in Latin America.
[d05s001] However, it is only in "El Salvador that they are called 'nuégados'" (Latinaish, Salvadoran Nuegados) Nuegados are "nothing more than fried dumplings coated with a sweet sugar cane sauce".
[d05s002] To prepare nuegados, one deep fries a dough made of corn flour, baking powder, butter, salt, and water in oil.

[d08p003] Cinnamon leaf oil
[d08s003] It is also used as a source of eugenol for the preparation of synthetic vanillin.
[d08s004] Cinnamon oleoresin obtained by solvent extraction is a dark brown extremely concentrated and viscous liquid, closely approximating the total spice flavour and containing 50% or more volatile oil.
[d08s005] It is used mainly for flavouring food products such as cakes and confectionary.

[d03p003] Cruller
[d03s003] Crullers may be topped with plain powdered sugar; powdered sugar mixed with cinnamon; or icing.
[d03s004] However, a "French cruller" is a fluted, ring-shaped doughnut made from choux pastry with a light airy texture.
[d03s005] The French cruller in German is called a Spritzkuchen.

context:
[d00p003] Vladimir Menshov
[d00s003] Although his output as an actor outnumbers his output as a director, he is best known for the five films he directed, the most famous of which is the 1979 melodrama "Moscow Does Not Believe in Tears", which won the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.
[d00s004] Actress Vera Alentova, who starred in the film, is the mother of Vladimir Menshov's daughter Yuliya Menshova.

[d09s002] In 2012, Aronowitz was awarded the Center for Study of Working Class Life's Lifetime Achievement Award at Stony Brook University.

[d05s002] Pure blue, in the middle, has a wavelength of 470 nanometres.

question: Thomas Fitch defended John Henry Holliday when he was accused of killing men during the gunfight at the o.k. corral, when was that?
context:
[d01p000] Thomas Fitch (politician)
[d01s000] Thomas Fitch (January 27, 1838 – November 12, 1923) was an American lawyer and politician.
[d01s001] He defended President Brigham Young of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and other church leaders when Young and his denomination were prosecuted for polygamy in 1871 and 1872.
[d01s002] He also successfully defended Virgil, Morgan, and Wyatt Earp along with Doc Holliday when they were accused of murdering Billy Clanton, and Tom and Frank McLaury during the October 25, 1881 Gunfight at the O.K. Corral.

[d08p000] Gunfight at the O.K. Corral
[d08s000] The Gunfight at the O.K. Corral was a 30-second shootout between lawmen and members of a loosely organized group of outlaws called the Cowboys that took place at about 3:00 p.m. on Wednesday, October 26, 1881 in Tombstone, Arizona Territory.
[d08s001] It is generally regarded as the most famous shootout in the history of the American Wild West.
[d08s002] The gunfight was the result of a long-simmering feud, with Cowboys Billy Claiborne, Ike and Billy Clanton, and Tom and Frank McLaury on one side and town Marshal Virgil Earp, Special Policeman Morgan Earp, Special Policeman Wyatt Earp, and temporary policeman Doc Holliday on the other side.

[d00p000] O.K. Corral hearing and aftermath
[d00s000] The O.K. Corral hearing and aftermath was the direct result of the 30-second Gunfight at the O.K. Corral in Tombstone, Arizona Territory on October 26, 1881.
[d00s001] During that confrontation, Deputy U.S. Marshal and Tombstone Town Marshal Virgil Earp, Assistant Town Marshal Morgan Earp, and temporary deputy marshals Wyatt Earp and Doc Holliday shot and killed Billy Clanton, and Tom and Frank McLaury.
[d00s002] Billy's brother Ike, who had repeatedly threatened to kill the Earps for some time, had been present at the gunfight but was unarmed and fled.

[d03p000] Doc Holliday
[d03s000] John Henry "Doc" Holliday (August 14, 1851 – November 8, 1887) was an American gambler, gunfighter, and dentist, and a good friend of Wyatt Earp.
[d03s001] He is best known for his role as a temporary deputy marshal in the events leading up to and following the Gunfight at the O.K. Corral.

[d07p000] Virgil Earp
[d07s000] Virgil Walter Earp (July 18, 1843 – October 19, 1905) was both deputy U.S. marshal and Tombstone, Arizona City Marshal when he led his brothers Morgan and Wyatt and Doc Holliday in a confrontation with outlaw Cowboys at the Gunfight at the O.K. Corral on October 26, 1881.
[d07s001] They killed brothers Tom and Frank McLaury and Billy Clanton.
[d07s002] All three Earp brothers had been the target of repeated death threats made by the Cowboys who were upset by the Earps' interference in their illegal activities.

[d05p000] Morgan Earp
[d05s000] Morgan Seth Earp (April 24, 1851 – March 18, 1882) was a Tombstone, Arizona Special Policeman when he helped his brothers Virgil and Wyatt and Doc Holliday confront outlaw Cowboys in the Gunfight at the O.K. Corral on October 26, 1881.
[d05s001] All three Earp brothers had been the target of repeated death threats made by the Cowboys who were upset by the Earps' interference in their illegal activities.
[d05s002] The lawmen killed Cowboys Tom and Frank McLaury and Billy Clanton.

[d02p000] Hour of the Gun
[d02s000] Hour of the Gun is a 1967 Western film depicting Wyatt Earp and Doc Holliday during their 1881 battles against Ike Clanton and his brothers in the Gunfight at the O.K. Corral, and the gunfight's aftermath in and around Tombstone, Arizona, starring James Garner as Earp, Jason Robards as Holliday, and Robert Ryan as Clanton.
[d02s001] The movie was directed by John Sturges.

[d08p006] Gunfight at the O.K. Corral
[d08s006] Virgil, Morgan, and Doc Holliday were wounded, but Wyatt Earp was unharmed.
[d08s007] The shootout has come to represent a period of the American Old West when the frontier was virtually an open range for outlaws, largely unopposed by law enforcement officers who were spread thin over vast territories.

[d00p003] O.K. Corral hearing and aftermath
[d00s003] He filed murder charges against the Earps and Doc Holliday on October 30.

[d08p003] Gunfight at the O.K. Corral
[d08s003] All three Earp brothers had been the target of repeated death threats made by the Cowboys, who objected to the Earps' interference in their illegal activities.
[d08s004] Billy Clanton and both McLaury brothers were killed.
[d08s005] Ike Clanton claimed that he was unarmed and ran from the fight, along with Billy Claiborne.

question: Which breed of dog was first recognized by their country's official kennel club, the American Hairless Terrier or the Saint-Usuge Spaniel?
context:
[d06p000] Saint-Usuge Spaniel
[d06s000] The Saint-Usuge Spaniel (or Épagneul de Saint-Usuge) is a breed of Spaniel originating in the Bresse region of France.
[d06s001] The breed has origins dating back to at least the 16th century, but was nearly extinct by the end of World War II.
[d06s002] Through the efforts of Father Robert Billard, the breed was resurrected during the second half of the 20th century; its national breed club was founded in 1990.

[d01p000] American Russell Terrier Club
[d01s000] The American Russell Terrier Club (formerly named the English Jack Russell Terrier Club), founded by JoAnn Stoll in 1995, was the first registry in the United States to maintain the Russell Terrier as a separate breed from the Parson Russell Terrier.
[d01s001] The American Jack Russell Terrier Club is affiliated with both the United Kennel Club and the American Kennel Club.
[d01s002] The purpose of the early founders was to establish a registry for the perpetuation and development of the Russell Terrier as a pure strain of working Jack Russell Terrier keeping their blood and type pure within the registry to works towards Kennel Club recognition as an official breed in the US.

[d00p000] American Hairless Terrier
[d00s000] The American Hairless Terrier is a rare breed of dog that was derived as a variant of Rat Terrier.
[d00s001] As of January 1, 2004, the United Kennel Club deemed the AHT a separate terrier breed, granting it full UKC recognition.
[d00s002] An intelligent, social and energetic working breed, the American Hairless Terrier is often listed as a potential good breed choice for allergy sufferers.

[d06p003] Saint-Usuge Spaniel
[d06s003] The breed was recognised by the Société Centrale Canine (French Kennel Club) in 2003.

question: Who was an important leader of the Democratic-Republican Party?
context:
[d03p000] Albert Gallatin
[d03s000] Abraham Alfonse Albert Gallatin (January 29, 1761 – August 12, 1849) was a Swiss-American politician, diplomat, ethnologist and linguist.
[d03s001] He was an important leader of the Democratic-Republican Party, serving in various federal elective and appointed positions across four decades.
[d03s002] He represented Pennsylvania in the Senate and the House of Representatives before becoming the longest-tenured United States Secretary of the Treasury and serving as a high-ranking diplomat.

[d01p000] Democratic-Republican Party
[d01s000] The Democratic-Republican Party was an American political party formed by Thomas Jefferson and James Madison in 1791–93 to oppose the centralizing policies of the new Federalist Party run by Alexander Hamilton (1755/57-1804), who was secretary of the treasury and chief architect of George Washington's administration.
[d01s001] The new party controlled the presidency and Congress, as well as most states, from 1801 to 1825, during the First Party System.
[d01s002] It began in 1791 as one faction in Congress, and included many politicians who had been opposed to the new constitution.

[d02p009] Whig Party (United States)
[d02s009] Party founders chose the "Whig" name to echo the American Whigs of the 18th century who fought for independence.
[d02s010] The underlying political philosophy of the American Whig Party was not directly related to the British Whig party.
[d02s011] Historian Frank Towers has specified a deep ideological divide:

[d00p003] Presidency of Thomas Jefferson
[d00s003] After two terms, Jefferson was succeeded by Secretary of State James Madison, also of the Democratic-Republican Party.

[d09p000] Jeremiah Morrow
[d09s000] Jeremiah Morrow (October 6, 1771March 22, 1852) was a Democratic-Republican Party politician from Ohio.
[d09s001] He served as the ninth Governor of Ohio, and the last Democratic-Republican to do so.

[d07p000] The Probability Broach
[d07s000] The Probability Broach is the 1979 first novel by American science fiction writer L. Neil Smith.
[d07s001] It is set in an alternate history, the so-called Gallatin Universe, where a libertarian society has formed on the North American continent, styled the North American Confederacy ("NAC").
[d07s002] This history was created when the Declaration of Independence has the word "unanimous" added to the preamble, to read that governments "derive their just power from the "unanimous" consent of the governed".

[d05p003] United States presidential election, 1800
[d05s003] The election was a realigning election that ushered in a generation of Democratic-Republican Party rule and the eventual demise of the Federalist Party in the First Party System.
[d05s004] It was a long, bitter re-match of the 1796 election between the pro-French and pro-decentralization Democratic-Republicans under Jefferson and Aaron Burr and the incumbent Adams and Charles Pinckney's pro-British and pro-centralization Federalists.
[d05s005] The chief political issues revolved around the fallout from the French Revolution, including opposition to the tax imposed by Congress to pay for the mobilization of the new army and the navy in the Quasi-War against France in 1798.

[d02p000] Whig Party (United States)
[d02s000] The Whig Party was a political party active in the middle of the 19th century in the United States.
[d02s001] Four US presidents belonged to the party while in office.
[d02s002] It emerged in the 1830s as the leading opponent of Jacksonians, pulling together former members of the National Republican (one of the successors of the Democratic-Republican Party) and Anti-Masonic Parties.

[d00p000] Presidency of Thomas Jefferson
[d00s000] The presidency of Thomas Jefferson began on March 4, 1801, when he was inaugurated as the third President of the United States, and ended on March 4, 1809.
[d00s001] Jefferson assumed the office after defeating incumbent President John Adams in the 1800 presidential election.
[d00s002] The election was a realigning election in which the Democratic-Republican Party swept the Federalist Party out of power, ushering in a generation of Democratic-Republican dominance in American politics.

[d02p003] Whig Party (United States)
[d02s003] It had distant links to the upscale traditions of the Federalist Party.
[d02s004] Along with the rival Democratic Party, it was central to the Second Party System from the early 1840s to the mid-1860s.
[d02s005] It originally formed in opposition to the policies of President Andrew Jackson (in office 1829–37) and his Democratic Party.

[d05p000] No. 1455 Flight RAF
[d05s000] No. 1455 (Fighter) Flight was formed at RAF Tangmere, West Sussex on 7 July 1941, equipped with Turbinlite Douglas Boston and Douglas Havoc aircraft.
[d05s001] On operations they co-operated with the Hawker Hurricanes of 1 Squadron and 3 Squadron.
[d05s002] The flight was replaced with 534 Squadron on 2 September 1942.

[d04p000] No. 1300 Flight RAF
[d04s000] No. 1300 (Meteorological) Flight was formed on 31 July 1943 at RAF Alipore, West Bengal, British India, by re-designating No. 1 Meteorological Flight RAF.
[d04s001] The flight, strength of which had been reduced to three Hawker Hurricane Mk.IIs by this time, was disbanded on 30 May 1946 at RAF Kallang, Malaya, as No. 1300 (Meteorological THUM) Flight, THUM standing for Temperature and Humidity.

[d09p000] Battle of Britain Memorial Flight
[d09s000] The Battle of Britain Memorial Flight (BBMF) is a Royal Air Force flight which provides an aerial display group usually comprising an Avro Lancaster, a Supermarine Spitfire and a Hawker Hurricane.
[d09s001] The aircraft are regularly seen at events commemorating the Second World War and upon British State occasions, notably Trooping the Colour, celebrating Queen Elizabeth II's 80th birthday in 2006, as well as the wedding of Prince William, Duke of Cambridge and Catherine Middleton in 2011 and at air displays throughout the United Kingdom and Europe.

[d08p000] Hawker Hurricane
[d08s000] The Hawker Hurricane is a British single-seat fighter aircraft of the 1930s–1940s that was designed and predominantly built by Hawker Aircraft Ltd for the Royal Air Force (RAF).
[d08s001] Although overshadowed by the Supermarine Spitfire, the aircraft became renowned during the Battle of Britain, accounting for 60 percent of the RAF air victories in the battle, and served in all the major theatres of the Second World War.

[d01p000] Flying Legend Hawker Hurricane Replica
[d01s000] The Flying Legend Hawker Hurricane Replica is an Italian light-sport aircraft, designed and produced by Flying Legend of Caltagirone and introduced at the AERO Friedrichshafen show in 2011.
[d01s001] The aircraft, a 72% scale replica of the British Hawker Hurricane Second World War fighter, is supplied as a kit for amateur construction or as a complete ready-to-fly-aircraft.

[d03p000] Hawker Hurricane in Yugoslav service
[d03s000] The Royal Yugoslav Air Force (VVKJ) operated the British Hawker Hurricane Mk I fighter aircraft from 1938 to 1941.
[d03s001] Between 1938 and 1940, the VVKJ obtained 24 Hurricane Mk I's from early production batches, marking the first foreign sale of the aircraft.
[d03s002] Twenty additional aircraft were built by Zmaj under licence in Yugoslavia.

[d07p000] Sindlinger Hawker Hurricane
[d07s000] The Sindlinger HH-1 Hawker Hurricane is a ⅝ scale homebuilt design based on the Hawker Hurricane.
[d07s001] Designed by Fred Sindlinger for amateur construction, the prototype was built between 1969 and 1972.

[d00p000] Supermarine Seafire
[d00s000] The Supermarine Seafire was a naval version of the Supermarine Spitfire adapted for operation from aircraft carriers.
[d00s001] In concept, it is relatively comparable to the Hawker Sea Hurricane, a navalised version of the Spitfire's stablemate, the Hawker Hurricane.
[d00s002] The name Seafire had been derived from the abbreviation of the longer name Sea Spitfire.

[d02p000] Hawker Typhoon
[d02s000] The Hawker Typhoon (Tiffy in RAF slang), is a British single-seat fighter-bomber, produced by Hawker Aircraft.
[d02s001] It was intended to be a medium–high altitude interceptor, as a replacement for the Hawker Hurricane but several design problems were encountered and it never completely satisfied this requirement.

[d03p003] Hawker Hurricane in Yugoslav service
[d03s003] When the country was drawn into World War II by the German-led Axis invasion of April 1941, a total of 41 Hurricane Mk I's were in service as fighters.
[d03s004] They achieved some successes against "Luftwaffe" aircraft, but all Yugoslav Hurricanes were destroyed or captured during the 11-day invasion.

context:
[d05p000] Cartoon Network Too
[d05s000] Cartoon Network Too was a British TV network created by Turner Broadcasting.
[d05s001] CN Too is the sister station of Cartoon Network, and it often aired programmes a while after they are shown on the main Cartoon Network.
[d05s002] During the daytime, it usually aired some action-adventure programming such as "" and "".

[d03p000] Nick Jr. Too
[d03s000] Nick Jr.
[d03s001] Too (formerly Nick Jr. 2) is the British second channel of Nick Jr. available in the United Kingdom and in the Republic of Ireland, generally presenting popular Nick Jr. programming at other times of the day.
[d03s002] It launched 24 April 2006, the same day as rival channel Cartoon Network Too.

[d08p000] Cartoon Network (South Korea)
[d08s000] Cartoon Network South Korea is the South Korean version of the original American Cartoon Network television channel in the United States and is a cable and satellite television channel created by Turner Broadcasting, a unit of Time Warner which primarily shows animated programming.
[d08s001] It was launched on November 11, 2006.

[d00p000] Cartoon Network (Middle East and Africa)
[d00s000] Cartoon Network refers to two digital children's TV channels broadcasting animated programs: Cartoon Network MENA, which serves the Middle East and North Africa region (excluding Israel, Iran and Turkey) along with Cyprus; and Cartoon Network Africa (formerly known as Cartoon Network HQ), which serves Sub-Saharan Africa.
[d00s001] Cartoon Network was created by Turner Broadcasting System, a unit of Time Warner.
[d00s002] Cartoon Network UK/Europe (the direct precursor to Cartoon Network feeds in the EMEA region, including Cartoon Network HQ) was launched on September 17, 1993.

[d03p003] Nick Jr. Too
[d03s003] Nick Jr.
[d03s004] Too carries a schedule separate from the main Nick Jr. channel.
[d03s005] The channel was renamed to Nick Jr.

[d01p000] Cartoon Network (Portugal)
[d01s000] Cartoon Network, commonly abbreviated as CN, is a Portuguese digital cable and satellite television channel launched on December 3, 2013 and owned by Turner Broadcasting System Europe (a semi-autonomous unit of Time Warner).
[d01s001] Currently, Cartoon Network is the second most-watched kids and teens' channel in Portugal, recently surpassing Canal Panda and is now only behind Disney Channel.

context:
[d03p000] INXS
[d03s000] INXS ( ) were an Australian rock band, formed as The Farriss Brothers in 1977 in Sydney, New South Wales.
[d03s001] They began playing covers in Western Australian pubs and clubs, occasionally playing some of their original music.
[d03s002] Mainstays were main composer and keyboardist Andrew Farriss, drummer Jon Farriss, guitarists Tim Farriss and Kirk Pengilly, bassist Garry Gary Beers and main lyricist and vocalist Michael Hutchence.

[d02p000] Tappi Tíkarrass
[d02s000] Tappi Tíkarrass was an Icelandic punk band which added elements of funk, rock and jazz to their music, marking a difference from other traditional bands at that time.
[d02s001] The band is also considered the first serious music project of now renowned singer Björk Guðmundsdóttir.

[d00p000] Bitið fast í vitið
[d00s000] Bitið fast í vitið (roughly "Bite Hard In Your Mind" in Icelandic) is the début EP of Icelander punk/pop group Tappi Tíkarrass .
[d00s001] It was released in late-1982 on the Spor label, within a year of the band's formation in September 1981 – led by vocalists Björk and Eyþór Arnalds .
[d00s002] This was the band's most punk-oriented release and contains five tracks, featuring one in English, "London".

[d09p000] Miranda (album)
[d09s000] Miranda is the only studio album by Icelandic punk band Tappi Tíkarrass.
[d09s001] It was released on December 23, 1983 through Gramm.

[d08p000] Folk rock
[d08s000] Folk rock is a music genre combining elements of folk music and rock music.
[d08s001] In its earliest and narrowest sense, the term referred to a genre that arose in the United States and the United Kingdom around the mid-1960s.
[d08s002] The genre emerged from bands such as the Beatles, the Searchers, and the Animals in the UK, and Bob Dylan and the Byrds in the US, who played traditional folk music and songs with rock instrumentation.

[d01p003] Steeltown (band)
[d01s003] The group members were Andy Richmond vocals, Peter Howard keyboards, Terry Gidman drums and Kate Richmond vocals and percussion and Reece Speceis Lead Guitar.
[d01s004] The band were formed from the remnant members of a Scottish group called the Technicians who migrated to Australia in the 80s and who also attained top 40 status with their music releases, Hot for Love, Clockwork Clown and Sodier of Fortune through record companies Powderworks, EMI and BMG, and were published by MMA which was owned by legendary rock outfit INXS.

[d04p000] Nýtt líf
[d04s000] Nýtt Líf (   , English: "New Life") is an Icelandic film directed by Þráinn Bertelsson and released in 1983.
[d04s001] The film is a comedy shot in the Westman Islands and stars Eggert Þorleifsson and Karl Ágúst Úlfsson, among others.
[d04s002] The music features several musicians including the band Tappi Tíkarrass (of which Björk was a member), which contributed the songs "Sperglar" and "Kukl" (a.k.a. "Seiður").

[d07p000] Rave music
[d07s000] Rave music may either refer to the late 1980s/early 1990s genres of house, breakbeat, acid house, techno and hardcore techno, which were the first genres of music to be played at rave parties, or to any other genre of electronic dance music (EDM) that may be played at a rave.
[d07s001] The genre "rave", also known as hardcore by early ravers, first appeared amongst the UK "acid" movement during the late 1980s at warehouse parties and other underground venues, as well as on UK pirate radio stations.
[d07s002] The genre would develop into oldschool hardcore, which lead onto newer forms of rave music such as drum and bass and 2-step, as well as other hardcore techno genres, such as gabber, hardstyle and happy hardcore.

[d05p000] Disco polo
[d05s000] Disco polo is a musical genre of popular music that is dance music, created in Poland in the late 1980s, initially known as "sidewalks music" ("muzyka chodnikowa").
[d05s001] This trend, also known as city folklore music, was popular in the mid-late 1990s, with its peak taking place around 1995–1997.
[d05s002] Later observed a gradual decline in the popularity led to the temporary collapse in the early twenty-first century.

[d03p003] INXS
[d03s003] For twenty years, INXS was fronted by Hutchence, whose "sultry good looks" and magnetic stage presence made him the focal point of the band.
[d03s004] Initially known for their new wave/pop style, the band later developed a harder pub rock style that included funk and dance elements.
