[d00p003] European Masters Games
[d00s003] The European Masters Games are held once every four year, while the last games were held in 2015 in Nice, France, the next games will be celebrated in Torino, Italy, in 2019.
[d00s004] The International Masters Games Association (IMGA), which is based in Lausanne, Switzerland, is the body responsible for the bidding and placing of the games.

[d04p000] Winter Olympic Games
[d04s000] The Olympic Winter Games (official name) (French: "Jeux olympiques d'hiver" ) is a major international sporting event held once every four years, for sports practised on snow and ice.
[d04s001] The first Winter Olympics, the 1924 Winter Olympics, was held in Chamonix, France.
[d04s002] The original five sports (broken into nine disciplines) were bobsleigh, curling, ice hockey, Nordic skiing (consisting of the disciplines military patrol, cross-country skiing, Nordic combined, and ski jumping), and skating (consisting of the disciplines figure skating and speed skating).

[d06p000] Women's Rugby World Cup
[d06s000] The Women's Rugby World Cup is the premier international competition in rugby union for women.
[d06s001] The tournament is organised by the sport's governing body, World Rugby.
[d06s002] The championships are currently held every four years; the event was most recently held in France in August 2014.

[d04p003] Winter Olympic Games
[d04s003] The Games were held every four years from 1924 to 1936, interrupted in 1940 and 1944 by World War II, and resumed in 1948.
[d04s004] Until 1992 the Winter and Summer Olympic Games were held in the same years, but in accordance with a 1986 decision by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) to place the Summer and Winter Games on separate four-year cycles in alternating even-numbered years, the next Winter Olympics after 1992 was in 1994.

[d04p000] Florida black bear
[d04s000] The Florida black bear ("Ursus americanus floridanus") is a subspecies of the American black bear that has historically ranged throughout most of Florida and southern portions of Alabama, Georgia, and Mississippi.
[d04s001] The large black-furred bears live mainly in forested areas and have seen recent habitat reduction throughout the state.

[d02p000] Ursus americanus carlottae
[d02s000] The Haida Gwaii black bear ("Ursus americanus carlottae") is a morphologically distinct subspecies of the American black bear.
[d02s001] The most significant morphological differences are its large size, massive cranium, and large molars.
[d02s002] This subspecies is endemic to the Haida Gwaii (Queen Charlotte Islands) and is considered a "keystone species" because of the bears transportation of salmon remains into surrounding forests of Haida Gwaii.

[d08p000] Newfoundland black bear
[d08s000] The Newfoundland black bear ("Ursus americanus hamiltoni") is a morphologically distinct subspecies of the American black bear which is endemic to the island of Newfoundland in Atlantic Canada.
[d08s001] The Newfoundland black bear is generally larger than its mainland relatives, ranging in size from 90 to and averaging 135 kg .
[d08s002] It also has one of the longest hibernation periods of any bear in North America.

[d06p000] American black bear
[d06s000] The American black bear ("Ursus americanus") is a medium-sized bear native to North America.

[d01p000] Cinnamon bear
[d01s000] The cinnamon bear ("Ursus americanus cinnamomum") is both a color phase and subspecies of the American black bear, native to central and western areas of the United States and Canada.
[d01s001] Established populations are found in Colorado, New Mexico, Utah, Idaho, Montana, Washington, Manitoba Minnesota, Wisconsin, Wyoming, California, Alberta, and British Columbia.
[d01s002] They also have been seen in Pennsylvania and New York.

[d05p000] Japanese black bear
[d05s000] The Japanese black bear ("Ursus thibetanus japonicus") is a subspecies of the Asian black bear that lives on three main islands of Japan: Honshu, Shikoku and Kyushu.
[d05s001] There are said to be 10,000 black bears on Japan.
[d05s002] The population of black bears on Shikoku and Kyushu may be endangered or extinct.

[d09p000] Kermode bear
[d09s000] The Kermode bear ("Ursus americanus kermodei"), also known as the "spirit bear" (particularly in British Columbia), is a rare subspecies of the American black bear living in the Central and North Coast regions of British Columbia, Canada.
[d09s001] It is the official provincial mammal of British Columbia.
[d09s002] It is noted for about one-tenth of its population having white or cream-coloured coats like polar bears.

[d07p000] Baluchistan bear
[d07s000] The Baluchistan bear, also called the Pakistan black bear ("Ursus thibetanus gedrosianus") is a subspecies of the Asian black bear found in the Baluchistan Mountains of southern Pakistan and Iran.
[d07s001] It has an unusually thin coat for an Asian black bear, but this is because it is found in a warmer climate than most of the other subspecies, which are found in the much colder Himalayan Mountains.
[d07s002] It is also more frugivorous than the other subspecies, and it loves to eat figs and bananas.

[d03p000] Ussuri black bear
[d03s000] The Ussuri black bear ("Ursus thibetanus ussuricus"), also known as the Manchurian black bear, is a large subspecies of the Asian black bear native to the Far East, including the Korean Peninsula.

[d09s004] They are not albinos and not any more related to polar bears or the "blonde" brown bears of Alaska's "ABC Islands" than other members of their species.

question: What company was Luca Cordero di Montezemolo the chairman of that merged into a new Netherlands-based holding company Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV?
context:
[d05p000] Fiat S.p.A.
[d05s000] Fiat S.p.A., or "Fabbrica Italiana Automobili Torino" (Italian Automobile Factory of Turin), was an Italian holding company whose original and core activities were in the automotive industry, and that was succeeded by Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV (FCA).
[d05s001] The Fiat Group contained many brands such as Ferrari, Maserati, Fiat, Alfa Romeo, the Chrysler Group, and many more.
[d05s002] On 29 January 2014, it was announced that Fiat S.p.A. (the former owner of Fiat Group) was to be merged into a new Netherlands-based holding company Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV (FCA), took place before the end of 2014.

[d01p000] Fiat Chrysler Automobiles
[d01s000] Fiat Chrysler Automobiles N.V. (abbreviated as FCA) is an Italian-controlled multinational corporation incorporated in the Netherlands, and currently the world’s seventh-largest auto maker.
[d01s001] The group was established in late 2014 by merging Fiat S.p.A. into a new holding company, FCA (with headquarters in London) for tax purposes.
[d01s002] The holding company is listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Borsa Italiana in Milan.

[d02p000] Fiat Industrial
[d02s000] Fiat Industrial S.p.A. was an Italian company into which Fiat S.p.A. (parent company of Fiat Group) demerged most of its activities not directly related to automobiles at the start of 2011.
[d02s001] Fiat Industrial served as a holding company for the activities of truck manufacturer Iveco; an 89.3% stake in the agricultural and construction equipment producer CNH Global; and FPT Industrial, which consists of the industrial and marine activities formerly part of Fiat Powertrain Technologies.
[d02s002] The company's Chairman was Sergio Marchionne, who also served as CEO of Fiat S.p.A. and Chairman/CEO of Chrysler Group LLC, now merged as Fiat Chrysler Automobiles.

[d07p000] Luca Cordero di Montezemolo
[d07s000] Luca Cordero di Montezemolo (] ; born 31 August 1947) is an Italian businessman, former Chairman of Ferrari, and formerly Chairman of Fiat S.p.A. and President of Confindustria and FIEG.
[d07s001] He comes from an aristocratic family from the region of Piedmont in Italy.
[d07s002] He graduated with a degree in law from La Sapienza University in 1971.

[d06p000] Future Italy
[d06s000] Future Italy ("Italia Futura", IF) is an Italian liberal-centrist think tank, formed in 2009 by Luca Cordero di Montezemolo, chairman of Alitalia (since 2014) and former chairman of Ferrari (1991–2014), FIAT (2004–2010) and Confindustria (2004–2008).

[d08p000] Ferrari Ascari
[d08s000] The Ferrari Ascari is a Ferrari concept car that won the "Ferrari: New Concepts for the Myth" car design competition in 2005.
[d08s001] The car was designed by Manuele Amprimo, Werner Gruber, and Yu Jae-Cheul from Istituto Europeo di Design (IED; English: "European Institute of Design"), Turin, Italy.
[d08s002] The judges of the competition included Luca Cordero di Montezemolo, the second and only living son of Enzo Ferrari, Piero Ferrari, Jean Todt, Amedeo Felisa, Massimo Fumarola, Pininfarina, and more than 22,000 users of FerrariWorld's online website.

[d03p000] 2009 24 Hours of Le Mans
[d03s000] The 2009 24 Hours of Le Mans (French: "24 Heures du Mans 2009" ) was the 77th Grand Prix of Endurance, an endurance auto race run over 24 hours.
[d03s001] It took place at the Circuit de la Sarthe, Le Mans, France, and was organised by the Automobile Club de l'Ouest (ACO) over 13–14 June 2009 and was started by Fiat and Ferrari chairman Luca Cordero di Montezemolo at 15:00 local time (13:00 UTC).
[d03s002] A test day was initially scheduled for 31 May that year, but was canceled by the ACO due to economic concerns.

[d07s003] Afterward, he studied for a masters degree in international commercial law at Columbia University.
[d07s004] He is one of the founders and former president of NTV, an Italian company which is Europe's first private open access operator of 300 km/h (186 mph) high-speed trains.

[d04p000] GAC Fiat
[d04s000] GAC Fiat Chrysler Automobiles Co., Ltd. is an automobile manufacturing company headquartered in Changsha, China and a 50:50 joint-venture between GAC Group and Fiat Chrysler Automobiles.
[d04s001] The company was founded on 9 March 2010.
[d04s002] Fiat has agreed to invest an initial US$559 million in the venture.

question: Which breed of dog was first recognized by their country's official kennel club, the American Hairless Terrier or the Saint-Usuge Spaniel?
context:
[d06p000] Saint-Usuge Spaniel
[d06s000] The Saint-Usuge Spaniel (or Épagneul de Saint-Usuge) is a breed of Spaniel originating in the Bresse region of France.
[d06s001] The breed has origins dating back to at least the 16th century, but was nearly extinct by the end of World War II.
[d06s002] Through the efforts of Father Robert Billard, the breed was resurrected during the second half of the 20th century; its national breed club was founded in 1990.

[d01p000] American Russell Terrier Club
[d01s000] The American Russell Terrier Club (formerly named the English Jack Russell Terrier Club), founded by JoAnn Stoll in 1995, was the first registry in the United States to maintain the Russell Terrier as a separate breed from the Parson Russell Terrier.
[d01s001] The American Jack Russell Terrier Club is affiliated with both the United Kennel Club and the American Kennel Club.
[d01s002] The purpose of the early founders was to establish a registry for the perpetuation and development of the Russell Terrier as a pure strain of working Jack Russell Terrier keeping their blood and type pure within the registry to works towards Kennel Club recognition as an official breed in the US.

[d06p003] Saint-Usuge Spaniel
[d06s003] The breed was recognised by the Société Centrale Canine (French Kennel Club) in 2003.

[d00p000] American Hairless Terrier
[d00s000] The American Hairless Terrier is a rare breed of dog that was derived as a variant of Rat Terrier.
[d00s001] As of January 1, 2004, the United Kennel Club deemed the AHT a separate terrier breed, granting it full UKC recognition.
[d00s002] An intelligent, social and energetic working breed, the American Hairless Terrier is often listed as a potential good breed choice for allergy sufferers.

question: Which astronaut, Jean-François Clervoy or Ulrich Walter, was born first?
context:
[d03p000] Jean-François Clervoy
[d03s000] Jean-François André Clervoy (born 19 November 1958) is a French engineer and a CNES and ESA astronaut.
[d03s001] He is a veteran of three NASA Space Shuttle missions.

[d04p000] Ulrich Walter
[d04s000] Prof. Dr. Ulrich Hans Walter (born February 9, 1954) is a German physicist/engineer and a former DFVLR astronaut.

[d07p000] Walter Cunningham
[d07s000] Ronnie Walter Cunningham (born March 16, 1932), (Col, USMCR, Ret.)
[d07s001] , better known as Walter Cunningham, is a retired American astronaut.
[d07s002] In 1968, he was a Lunar Module Pilot on the Apollo 7 mission.

[d01p000] Andrew Benjamin
[d01s000] Andrew Benjamin (born 1952, Australia) is an Australian philosopher.
[d01s001] Currently he holds two academic posts: Distinguished Professor of Philosophy and the Humanities at Kingston University, London and Professor of Philosophy and Jewish Thought in the Department of Philosophy and the Australian Centre for Jewish Civilization at Monash University, Melbourne, Australia.
[d01s002] Benjamin first came to critical attention with his writings in continental philosophy, writing articles and editing books on the thinking of Martin Heidegger, Theodor Adorno, Walter Benjamin, Julia Kristeva and Jean-François Lyotard.

[d00p000] Claude Nicollier

question: What where both Hawker Hurricane and No. 1455 Flight apart of?
context:
[d05p000] No. 1455 Flight RAF
[d05s000] No. 1455 (Fighter) Flight was formed at RAF Tangmere, West Sussex on 7 July 1941, equipped with Turbinlite Douglas Boston and Douglas Havoc aircraft.
[d05s001] On operations they co-operated with the Hawker Hurricanes of 1 Squadron and 3 Squadron.
[d05s002] The flight was replaced with 534 Squadron on 2 September 1942.

[d08p000] Hawker Hurricane
[d08s000] The Hawker Hurricane is a British single-seat fighter aircraft of the 1930s–1940s that was designed and predominantly built by Hawker Aircraft Ltd for the Royal Air Force (RAF).
[d08s001] Although overshadowed by the Supermarine Spitfire, the aircraft became renowned during the Battle of Britain, accounting for 60 percent of the RAF air victories in the battle, and served in all the major theatres of the Second World War.

[d02p000] Hawker Typhoon
[d02s000] The Hawker Typhoon (Tiffy in RAF slang), is a British single-seat fighter-bomber, produced by Hawker Aircraft.
[d02s001] It was intended to be a medium–high altitude interceptor, as a replacement for the Hawker Hurricane but several design problems were encountered and it never completely satisfied this requirement.

[d06p000] Hawker Tornado
[d06s000] The Hawker Tornado was a British single-seat fighter aircraft design of World War II for the Royal Air Force as a replacement for the Hawker Hurricane.
[d06s001] The planned production of Tornados was cancelled after the engine it was designed to use—the Rolls-Royce Vulture—proved unreliable in service.
[d06s002] A parallel airframe with the Napier Sabre continued into production as the Hawker Typhoon.

[d04p000] No. 1300 Flight RAF
[d04s000] No. 1300 (Meteorological) Flight was formed on 31 July 1943 at RAF Alipore, West Bengal, British India, by re-designating No. 1 Meteorological Flight RAF.
[d04s001] The flight, strength of which had been reduced to three Hawker Hurricane Mk.IIs by this time, was disbanded on 30 May 1946 at RAF Kallang, Malaya, as No. 1300 (Meteorological THUM) Flight, THUM standing for Temperature and Humidity.

[d01p000] Flying Legend Hawker Hurricane Replica
[d01s000] The Flying Legend Hawker Hurricane Replica is an Italian light-sport aircraft, designed and produced by Flying Legend of Caltagirone and introduced at the AERO Friedrichshafen show in 2011.
[d01s001] The aircraft, a 72% scale replica of the British Hawker Hurricane Second World War fighter, is supplied as a kit for amateur construction or as a complete ready-to-fly-aircraft.

[d07p000] Sindlinger Hawker Hurricane
[d07s000] The Sindlinger HH-1 Hawker Hurricane is a ⅝ scale homebuilt design based on the Hawker Hurricane.
[d07s001] Designed by Fred Sindlinger for amateur construction, the prototype was built between 1969 and 1972.

[d09p000] Battle of Britain Memorial Flight
[d09s000] The Battle of Britain Memorial Flight (BBMF) is a Royal Air Force flight which provides an aerial display group usually comprising an Avro Lancaster, a Supermarine Spitfire and a Hawker Hurricane.
[d09s001] The aircraft are regularly seen at events commemorating the Second World War and upon British State occasions, notably Trooping the Colour, celebrating Queen Elizabeth II's 80th birthday in 2006, as well as the wedding of Prince William, Duke of Cambridge and Catherine Middleton in 2011 and at air displays throughout the United Kingdom and Europe.

[d03p003] Hawker Hurricane in Yugoslav service
[d03s003] When the country was drawn into World War II by the German-led Axis invasion of April 1941, a total of 41 Hurricane Mk I's were in service as fighters.
[d03s004] They achieved some successes against "Luftwaffe" aircraft, but all Yugoslav Hurricanes were destroyed or captured during the 11-day invasion.

[d03p000] Hawker Hurricane in Yugoslav service
[d03s000] The Royal Yugoslav Air Force (VVKJ) operated the British Hawker Hurricane Mk I fighter aircraft from 1938 to 1941.
[d03s001] Between 1938 and 1940, the VVKJ obtained 24 Hurricane Mk I's from early production batches, marking the first foreign sale of the aircraft.
[d03s002] Twenty additional aircraft were built by Zmaj under licence in Yugoslavia.

question: Who has won more awards, Dan Schneider or Helen Hunt?
context:
[d01p000] Helen Hunt
[d01s000] Helen Elizabeth Hunt (born June 15, 1963) is an American actress, director, and screenwriter.
[d01s001] She starred in the sitcom "Mad About You" for seven years, and played single mother Carol Connelly in the 1997 romantic comedy film "As Good as It Gets", for which she won the Academy Award for Best Actress.
[d01s002] Some of her other notable films include "Twister" (1996), "Cast Away" (2000), "What Women Want" (2000), "Pay It Forward" (2000), and "The Sessions" (2012), the latter garnered her a second Academy Award nomination.

[d01p003] Helen Hunt
[d01s003] She made her directorial debut in 2007 with "Then She Found Me" (2007).
[d01s004] Hunt has also won four Emmy Awards, four Golden Globe Awards, and two Screen Actors Guild Awards.

[d04p000] Dan Schneider (TV producer)
[d04s000] Dan Schneider (born January 14, 1966) is an American actor, television and film writer, and producer.
[d04s001] After appearing in mostly supporting roles in a number of 1980s and 1990s films and TV shows, Schneider devoted himself to behind-the-scenes work in production.
[d04s002] He is the co-president of television production company Schneider's Bakery.

[d04p003] Dan Schneider (TV producer)
[d04s003] He created/co-created "All That", "The Amanda Show", "What I Like About You", "Drake & Josh", "Zoey 101", "iCarly", "Victorious", "Sam & Cat", "Henry Danger", "Game Shakers", and "The Adventures of Kid Danger and Captain Man".

[d02p000] Helen Hunt Falls
[d02s000] Helen Hunt Falls is a waterfall located on Cheyenne Creek in the North Cheyenne Cañon Park of Colorado Springs, Colorado.
[d02s001] The falls are named in honor of Helen Maria Hunt Jackson (October 15, 1830 – August 12, 1885), a United States poet and writer who became an activist on behalf of improved treatment of Native Americans by the U.S. government.
[d02s002] She died in San Francisco, California in 1885 and was later buried in Colorado Springs.

[d09p000] Ride (2014 film)
[d09s000] Ride is an 2014 American drama film written and directed by Helen Hunt.
[d09s001] The film stars Helen Hunt, Luke Wilson, Brenton Thwaites and Leonor Varela.
[d09s002] The film had a limited release in theaters and was released on video on demand beginning on May 1, 2015 by Screen Media Films.

[d03p000] Schneider's Bakery
[d03s000] Schneider's Bakery, DANWARP Inc. is a television production company founded by Dan Schneider.

[d06p000] Jamie Snow
[d06s000] Jamie Linda Snow (born September 22, 1985) is an American actress and casting director.
[d06s001] Best known for her collaborations with television producer Dan Schneider, as an actress she played Tammy (the exchange student from Tennessee) on "The Girls' Room" sketches of Schneider's series "The Amanda Show".

[d02p003] Helen Hunt Falls
[d02s003] The falls are located on North Cheyenne Creek immediately off of North Cheyenne Canyon Road in the North Cheyenne Canyon Park.
[d02s004] There is parking for about 30 vehicles at the falls and it becomes crowded early during summer months when visits to the canyon are popular among locals and tourists.
[d02s005] The Columbine Trail, which starts at the entrance of the Park by the Starsmore Visitor and Nature Center, terminates at Helen Hunt Falls.

[d02p006] Helen Hunt Falls
[d02s006] Visitors can hike a short distance of about 2/3 of a mile up a moderately steep trail above Helen Hunt Falls to reach Silver Cascade Falls.

context:
[d01p006] Cell fate determination
[d01s006] This is one of the reasons that model systems such as the fly ("Drosophila melanogaster"), the mouse (Muridae), and the leech ("Helobdella"), can all be used to study embryogenesis and developmental biology relevant to other animals, including humans.
[d01s007] What continues to be discovered and investigated is how the basic set of proteins (and mRNAs) are expressed differentially between cells types, temporally and spatially; and whether this is responsible for the vast diversity of organisms produced.
[d01s008] This leads to one of the key questions of developmental biology of how is cell fate determined.

[d01p000] Cell fate determination
[d01s000] Within the field of developmental biology one goal is to understand how a particular cell (or embryo) develops into the final cell type (or organism), essentially how a cell's fate is determined.
[d01s001] Within an embryo, 4 processes play out at the cellular and tissue level to essentially create the final organism.
[d01s002] These processes are cell proliferation, cell specialization, cell interaction and cell movement.

[d01p003] Cell fate determination
[d01s003] Each cell in the embryo receives and gives cues to its neighboring cells and retains a cell memory of its own cell proliferation history.
[d01s004] Almost all animals undergo a similar sequence of events during embryogenesis and have, at least at this developmental stage, the three germ layers and undergo gastrulation.
[d01s005] While embryogenesis has been studied for more than a century, it was only recently (the past 15 years or so) that scientists discovered that a basic set of the same proteins and mRNAs are involved in all of embryogenesis.

question: Which breed of dog was first recognized by their country's official kennel club, the American Hairless Terrier or the Saint-Usuge Spaniel?
context:
[d06p000] Saint-Usuge Spaniel
[d06s000] The Saint-Usuge Spaniel (or Épagneul de Saint-Usuge) is a breed of Spaniel originating in the Bresse region of France.
[d06s001] The breed has origins dating back to at least the 16th century, but was nearly extinct by the end of World War II.
[d06s002] Through the efforts of Father Robert Billard, the breed was resurrected during the second half of the 20th century; its national breed club was founded in 1990.

[d01p000] American Russell Terrier Club
[d01s000] The American Russell Terrier Club (formerly named the English Jack Russell Terrier Club), founded by JoAnn Stoll in 1995, was the first registry in the United States to maintain the Russell Terrier as a separate breed from the Parson Russell Terrier.
[d01s001] The American Jack Russell Terrier Club is affiliated with both the United Kennel Club and the American Kennel Club.
[d01s002] The purpose of the early founders was to establish a registry for the perpetuation and development of the Russell Terrier as a pure strain of working Jack Russell Terrier keeping their blood and type pure within the registry to works towards Kennel Club recognition as an official breed in the US.

[d00p000] American Hairless Terrier
[d00s000] The American Hairless Terrier is a rare breed of dog that was derived as a variant of Rat Terrier.
[d00s001] As of January 1, 2004, the United Kennel Club deemed the AHT a separate terrier breed, granting it full UKC recognition.
[d00s002] An intelligent, social and energetic working breed, the American Hairless Terrier is often listed as a potential good breed choice for allergy sufferers.

[d04p000] Terrier Group
[d04s000] Terrier Group is the name of a breed Group of dogs, used by kennel clubs to classify a defined collection of dog breeds.
[d04s001] In general, a "Terrier Group" includes one particular type of dog, the Terrier, although other types may be included in a kennel club's "Terrier Group".
[d04s002] Most major English-language kennel clubs include a "Terrier Group" although different kennel clubs may not include the same breeds in their "Terrier Group".

[d03p000] Shikoku (dog)
[d03s000] The Shikoku (四国犬 , Shikoku-ken , alternative names: Kochi-ken, Mikawa Inu, Japanese Wolfdog) is a native, primitive Japanese breed of dog from Shikoku island that is similar to a Shiba Inu.
[d03s001] The Shikoku was recently added as recognized breed of the American Kennel Club as an AKC FSS standard [ Foundation Stock Service ], it is recognized by the Japan Kennel Club, an organization recognized by AKC as an official foreign registry (AKC recognizes the Shiba Inu, however).
[d03s002] The Shikoku is also in the Canadian Kennel Club Hound group and the United Kennel Club, awaiting full recognition.

[d02p000] Rare breed (dog)
[d02s000] Rare breed (dog) is any breed of dog that is small in number and is used to refer to both old established breeds such as the Stabyhoun and Glen of Imaal Terrier or newer creations.
[d02s001] Since dogs have greater genetic variability than other domesticated animals the number of possible breeds is vast with new crosses constantly occurring, from these both selected and random crosses may come new breeds should offspring reliably breed true to type.
[d02s002] New breeds from the wild such as the Carolina Dog are quite rare compared to attempts at breed creation from man as found in the American Hairless Terrier which sought to exploit a mutation.

[d07p000] Toy Manchester Terrier
[d07s000] The Toy Manchester Terrier is a breed of dog, categorized as a terrier.
[d07s001] The breed was bred down in size in North America from the Manchester Terrier, and is placed in the Toy Group by the American Kennel Club and the Canadian Kennel Club (the Manchester Terrier is placed in the Terrier Group.)
[d07s002] Neither the Fédération Cynologique Internationale nor The Kennel Club recognize a Toy variety of the Manchester Terrier.

[d09p006] English Springer Spaniel
[d09s006] The smaller "cockers" hunted woodcock while the larger littermates were used to flush, or "spring," game.
[d09s007] In 1902, The Kennel Club recognized the English Springer Spaniel as a distinct breed.
[d09s008] They are used as sniffer dogs on a widespread basis.

[d06p003] Saint-Usuge Spaniel
[d06s003] The breed was recognised by the Société Centrale Canine (French Kennel Club) in 2003.

[d01p003] American Russell Terrier Club
[d01s003] On January 1, 2001, the United Kennel Club recognized the Russell Terrier as an official breed, designating only the stock from the American Russell Terrier Club as Foundation stock for the UKC Russell Terrier.
[d01s004] In 2004 the American Russell Terrier Club submitted an official request to include the American Russell Terrier Club stock into the AKC FSS Program to work towards becoming an official breed under the perimeters.
[d01s005] On December 8, 2004, the AKC officially accepted the Russell Terrier.

context:
[d03p000] INXS
[d03s000] INXS ( ) were an Australian rock band, formed as The Farriss Brothers in 1977 in Sydney, New South Wales.
[d03s001] They began playing covers in Western Australian pubs and clubs, occasionally playing some of their original music.
[d03s002] Mainstays were main composer and keyboardist Andrew Farriss, drummer Jon Farriss, guitarists Tim Farriss and Kirk Pengilly, bassist Garry Gary Beers and main lyricist and vocalist Michael Hutchence.

[d03p003] INXS
[d03s003] For twenty years, INXS was fronted by Hutchence, whose "sultry good looks" and magnetic stage presence made him the focal point of the band.
[d03s004] Initially known for their new wave/pop style, the band later developed a harder pub rock style that included funk and dance elements.

[d02p000] Tappi Tíkarrass
[d02s000] Tappi Tíkarrass was an Icelandic punk band which added elements of funk, rock and jazz to their music, marking a difference from other traditional bands at that time.
[d02s001] The band is also considered the first serious music project of now renowned singer Björk Guðmundsdóttir.

[d00p000] Bitið fast í vitið
[d00s000] Bitið fast í vitið (roughly "Bite Hard In Your Mind" in Icelandic) is the début EP of Icelander punk/pop group Tappi Tíkarrass .
[d00s001] It was released in late-1982 on the Spor label, within a year of the band's formation in September 1981 – led by vocalists Björk and Eyþór Arnalds .
[d00s002] This was the band's most punk-oriented release and contains five tracks, featuring one in English, "London".

The genre would develop into oldschool hardcore, which lead onto newer forms of rave music such as drum and bass and 2-step, as well as other hardcore techno genres, such as gabber, hardstyle and happy hardcore.

question: What position does Kyle York hold at the internet performance management company Dyn?
context:
[d01p000] Kyle York (entrepreneur)
[d01s000] Kyle York (born November 26, 1982) is an Internet entrepreneur, startup advisor, angel investor, cloud and Infrastructure-as-a-Service expert and sought-after global public speaker on cloud migration, internet security and hybrid cloud strategy.
[d01s001] York is an executive at Dyn, currently serving as Chief Strategy Officer.
[d01s002] Dyn was acquired by Oracle on November 21, 2016.

[d01p003] Kyle York (entrepreneur)
[d01s003] York also sits on the boards of Datanyze, CloudApp and 3rd Generation family business, YORK Athletics MFG.
[d01s004] where he is a co-founder.
[d01s005] York is also an active angel investor and advisor in dozens of fast growth Internet companies.

[d07p000] Dyn (company)
[d07s000] Dyn, Inc. ( ) is an Internet performance management company, offering products to monitor, control, and optimize online infrastructure, and also domain registration services and email products.
[d07s001] The company was acquired by Oracle Corporation in 2016.

[d01p006] Kyle York (entrepreneur)
[d01s006] He has been part of eight successful exits as an investor and employee.
[d01s007] Companies he has invested in and worked as a go-to-market (GTM) leader have been acquired by Cisco, Cognizant, New Relic, Oracle and Sophos.

[d05p000] Verelo
[d05s000] Verelo, originally based in Toronto, Canada and acquired by infrastructure as a service company Dyn in January 2013, was a website monitoring service that tracks a website's uptime, downtime, and performance.
[d05s001] Verelo monitored websites from multiple locations globally so that it could distinguish actual downtime from routing and access problems.
[d05s002] Verelo argued that downtime can be costly and even take lives, and is now based in Manchester, New Hampshire.

[d04p000] Dynatrace
[d04s000] Dynatrace is an American application performance management (APM) software company with products aimed at the information technology departments and digital business owners of medium and large businesses.
[d04s001] The company's services include performance management software for programs running on-premises and in the cloud.
[d04s002] This software manages the availability and performance of software applications and the impact on user experience in the form of deep transaction tracing, synthetic monitoring, real user monitoring, and network monitoring.

[d08p000] IBM Application Performance Management
[d08s000] IBM Application Performance Management is an offering that enables IT operations and DevOps and personnel to detect, isolate and diagnose problems in their hybrid cloud development and production environments.
[d08s001] The solution is part of the IBM IT Service Management portfolio, which is a key component of IBM Cloud solutions.
[d08s002] The offering provides capabilities such as End User Management (EUM), Application Discovery, Application Diagnostics, Transaction profiling and IT Operations Analytics.

[d06p000] Cognos
[d06s000] Cognos (Cognos Incorporated) was an Ottawa, Ontario-based company making business intelligence (BI) and performance management (PM) software.
[d06s001] Founded in 1969, at its peak Cognos employed almost 3,500 people and served more than 23,000 customers in over 135 countries until being acquired by IBM on January 31, 2008.
[d06s002] While no longer an independent company, the Cognos name continues to be applied to IBM's line of business intelligence and performance management products.

[d08p003] IBM Application Performance Management
[d08s003] IBM Application Performance Management solutions are available in both SaaS (software-as-a-service), hybrid and on-premises delivery models.
[d08s004] IBM Application Performance Management was a part of IBM Tivoli brand until 2013.

[d00p000] Business performance management
[d00s000] Business performance management is a set of performance management and analytic processes that enables the management of an organization's performance to achieve one or more pre-selected goals.
[d00s001] Synonyms for "business performance management" include "corporate performance management (CPM)" and "enterprise performance management".

[d06s002] The museum is situated on Çankaya St. within the Çankaya Campus.

[d08s000] The Atatürk Museum in Mersin (Turkish: "Mersin Atatürk Evi Müzesi" ) is a two-storey house in Mersin, which hosted the founder of modern Turkey, Mustafa Kemal Atatürk and his wife in 1925.

[d03p000] Atatürk Museum, Şişli

[d00s001] Founded by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, a Turkish army officer, revolutionary, and the first President of Turkey, the Izmir Atatürk Museum opened to the public on 11 September 1941, on the 19th anniversary of Atatürk’s arrival in Izmir.
[d00s002] On 13 May 1988 it was officially named the Izmir Atatürk Museum, which it is called today.

[d07p003] Seyfi Arkan
[d07s003] He was first in his class under Vedat Tek in 1928, and later worked with Hans Poelzig in Germany.
[d07s004] In 193 he designed the Glass Villa of Çankaya Köşkü, the President of Turkey's official residence, as well as Florya Atatürk Marine Mansion, a Bauhaus-style former residence of Atatürk and now a museum, in 1935.

[d01s001] It was unveiled by the Atatürk Society of America (ASA) in November 2013.
[d01s002] It is one of two statues in Washington, D.C. depicting Kemal Atatürk; the other is installed in front of the Embassy of Turkey, which is also located in Embassy Row.

question: What where both Hawker Hurricane and No. 1455 Flight apart of?
context:
[d05p000] No. 1455 Flight RAF
[d05s000] No. 1455 (Fighter) Flight was formed at RAF Tangmere, West Sussex on 7 July 1941, equipped with Turbinlite Douglas Boston and Douglas Havoc aircraft.
[d05s001] On operations they co-operated with the Hawker Hurricanes of 1 Squadron and 3 Squadron.
[d05s002] The flight was replaced with 534 Squadron on 2 September 1942.

[d04p000] No. 1300 Flight RAF
[d04s000] No. 1300 (Meteorological) Flight was formed on 31 July 1943 at RAF Alipore, West Bengal, British India, by re-designating No. 1 Meteorological Flight RAF.
[d04s001] The flight, strength of which had been reduced to three Hawker Hurricane Mk.IIs by this time, was disbanded on 30 May 1946 at RAF Kallang, Malaya, as No. 1300 (Meteorological THUM) Flight, THUM standing for Temperature and Humidity.

[d09p000] Battle of Britain Memorial Flight
[d09s000] The Battle of Britain Memorial Flight (BBMF) is a Royal Air Force flight which provides an aerial display group usually comprising an Avro Lancaster, a Supermarine Spitfire and a Hawker Hurricane.
[d09s001] The aircraft are regularly seen at events commemorating the Second World War and upon British State occasions, notably Trooping the Colour, celebrating Queen Elizabeth II's 80th birthday in 2006, as well as the wedding of Prince William, Duke of Cambridge and Catherine Middleton in 2011 and at air displays throughout the United Kingdom and Europe.

[d08p000] Hawker Hurricane
[d08s000] The Hawker Hurricane is a British single-seat fighter aircraft of the 1930s–1940s that was designed and predominantly built by Hawker Aircraft Ltd for the Royal Air Force (RAF).
[d08s001] Although overshadowed by the Supermarine Spitfire, the aircraft became renowned during the Battle of Britain, accounting for 60 percent of the RAF air victories in the battle, and served in all the major theatres of the Second World War.

[d01p000] Flying Legend Hawker Hurricane Replica
[d01s000] The Flying Legend Hawker Hurricane Replica is an Italian light-sport aircraft, designed and produced by Flying Legend of Caltagirone and introduced at the AERO Friedrichshafen show in 2011.
[d01s001] The aircraft, a 72% scale replica of the British Hawker Hurricane Second World War fighter, is supplied as a kit for amateur construction or as a complete ready-to-fly-aircraft.

[d03p000] Hawker Hurricane in Yugoslav service
[d03s000] The Royal Yugoslav Air Force (VVKJ) operated the British Hawker Hurricane Mk I fighter aircraft from 1938 to 1941.
[d03s001] Between 1938 and 1940, the VVKJ obtained 24 Hurricane Mk I's from early production batches, marking the first foreign sale of the aircraft.
[d03s002] Twenty additional aircraft were built by Zmaj under licence in Yugoslavia.

[d07p000] Sindlinger Hawker Hurricane
[d07s000] The Sindlinger HH-1 Hawker Hurricane is a ⅝ scale homebuilt design based on the Hawker Hurricane.
[d07s001] Designed by Fred Sindlinger for amateur construction, the prototype was built between 1969 and 1972.

[d00p000] Supermarine Seafire
[d00s000] The Supermarine Seafire was a naval version of the Supermarine Spitfire adapted for operation from aircraft carriers.
[d00s001] In concept, it is relatively comparable to the Hawker Sea Hurricane, a navalised version of the Spitfire's stablemate, the Hawker Hurricane.
[d00s002] The name Seafire had been derived from the abbreviation of the longer name Sea Spitfire.

[d02p000] Hawker Typhoon
[d02s000] The Hawker Typhoon (Tiffy in RAF slang), is a British single-seat fighter-bomber, produced by Hawker Aircraft.
[d02s001] It was intended to be a medium–high altitude interceptor, as a replacement for the Hawker Hurricane but several design problems were encountered and it never completely satisfied this requirement.

[d03p003] Hawker Hurricane in Yugoslav service
[d03s003] When the country was drawn into World War II by the German-led Axis invasion of April 1941, a total of 41 Hurricane Mk I's were in service as fighters.
[d03s004] They achieved some successes against "Luftwaffe" aircraft, but all Yugoslav Hurricanes were destroyed or captured during the 11-day invasion.

Winter Olympic Games
The Olympic Winter Games (official name) (French: "Jeux olympiques d'hiver" ) is a major international sporting event held once every four years, for sports practised on snow and ice. The first Winter Olympics, the 1924 Winter Olympics, was held in Chamonix, France. The original five sports (broken into nine disciplines) were bobsleigh, curling, ice hockey, Nordic skiing (consisting of the disciplines military patrol, cross-country skiing, Nordic combined, and ski jumping), and skating (consisting of the disciplines figure skating and speed skating).

[d04s001] The large black-furred bears live mainly in forested areas and have seen recent habitat reduction throughout the state.

[d02p000] Ursus americanus carlottae
[d02s000] The Haida Gwaii black bear ("Ursus americanus carlottae") is a morphologically distinct subspecies of the American black bear.
[d02s001] The most significant morphological differences are its large size, massive cranium, and large molars.
[d02s002] This subspecies is endemic to the Haida Gwaii (Queen Charlotte Islands) and is considered a "keystone species" because of the bears transportation of salmon remains into surrounding forests of Haida Gwaii.

[d08p000] Newfoundland black bear
[d08s000] The Newfoundland black bear ("Ursus americanus hamiltoni") is a morphologically distinct subspecies of the American black bear which is endemic to the island of Newfoundland in Atlantic Canada.
[d08s001] The Newfoundland black bear is generally larger than its mainland relatives, ranging in size from 90 to and averaging 135 kg .
[d08s002] It also has one of the longest hibernation periods of any bear in North America.

[d03p000] Ussuri black bear

question: Which American film director hosted the 18th Independent Spirit Awards in 2002?
context:
[d06p000] 18th Independent Spirit Awards
[d06s000] The 2002 Independent Spirit Awards, honoring the best in independent filmmaking for 2002, were announced on March 22, 2003.
[d06s001] It was hosted by John Waters.

[d05p000] John Waters
[d05s000] John Samuel Waters Jr. (born April 22, 1946) is an American film director, screenwriter, author, actor, stand-up comedian, journalist, visual artist, and art collector, who rose to fame in the early 1970s for his transgressive cult films.

[d03p000] 32nd Independent Spirit Awards
[d03s000] The 32nd Independent Spirit Awards (2017) nominees were announced by Film Independent, the nonprofit arts organization that produces them, on November 22, 2016.
[d03s001] The ceremony, hosted by Nick Kroll and John Mulaney, took place on Saturday, February 25, 2017, and was broadcast live on IFC at 2:00 pm PT.

[d06s002] In North America, its common use is as breakfast or dessert.

[d04s002] The original Mozarabic word "Xopaipa" was used to mean bread soaked in oil, and derived in turn from the Germanic word "suppa" which meant bread soaked in liquid.

[d08s004] Cinnamon oleoresin obtained by solvent extraction is a dark brown extremely concentrated and viscous liquid, closely approximating the total spice flavour and containing 50% or more volatile oil.

[d03p000] Cruller
[d03s000] A traditional cruller (or twister) is a fried pastry often made from a rectangle of dough, with a cut made in the middle that allows it to be pulled over and through itself producing twists in the sides of the pastry.

[d05s002] To prepare nuegados, one deep fries a dough made of corn flour, baking powder, butter, salt, and water in oil.

question: Pedro Duque and Mark Shuttleworth both went where in their life times?
context:
[d07p000] Pedro Duque
[d07s000] Pedro Duque Duque (born 14 March 1963) is a Spanish astronaut and a veteran of two space missions.

[d02p000] Pedro Duque y Cornejo
[d02s000] Pedro Duque y Cornejo (1677–1757) was a Spanish Baroque painter and sculptor of the Sevillian school of sculpture, a disciple of his grandfather Pedro Roldán.

[d05p000] Shuttleworth Foundation
[d05s000] The Shuttleworth Foundation was established in January 2001 by South African entrepreneur Mark Shuttleworth as an experiment with the purpose of providing funding for people engaged in social change.
[d05s001] While there have been various iterations of the foundation, its structure and how it invests in social innovation, the current model employs a fellowship model where fellows are given funding commensurate with their experience to match a year's salary, allowing them to spend that year developing a particular idea.

[d01p000] Impi Linux
[d01s000] Impi Linux was a South African Linux distribution which focused on the enterprise and government sector.
[d01s001] The project name originally referred to Impi meaning group of warriors in the Zulu language.
[d01s002] In September 2005, Mark Shuttleworth invested R10 million in return for 65% of Impi Linux.

[d08p000] Canonical (company)
[d08s000] Canonical Ltd. is a UK-based privately held computer software company founded and funded by South African entrepreneur Mark Shuttleworth to market commercial support and related services for Ubuntu and related projects.
[d08s001] Canonical employs staff in more than 30 countries and maintains offices in London, Austin, Boston, Shanghai, Beijing, Taipei and the Isle of Man.

[d00p000] Ravi Naidoo
[d00s000] Ravi Naidoo is the recipient of the 2015 Sir Misha Black Medal for innovation in design education.
[d00s001] He is the founder of Interactive Africa, a Cape Town based media and project management company responsible for the First African in Space mission with Mark Shuttleworth, and the marketing bid to host the 2010 Fifa World Cup.

[d03p000] Mark Shuttleworth
[d03s000] Mark Richard Shuttleworth (born 18 September 1973) is a South African entrepreneur who is the founder and CEO of Canonical Ltd., the company behind the development of the Linux-based Ubuntu operating system.
[d03s001] In 2002, he became the first citizen of an independent African country to travel to space as a space tourist.
[d03s002] He currently lives on the Isle of Man and holds dual citizenship from South Africa and the United Kingdom.

[d06p000] Thawte
[d06s000] Thawte Consulting (pronounced "thought") is a certificate authority (CA) for X.509 certificates.
[d06s001] Thawte was founded in 1995 by Mark Shuttleworth in South Africa.
[d06s002] As of December 30, 2016, its parent company, Symantec Group is collectively the third largest public CA on the Internet with 17.2% market share.

[d04p000] Inktank Storage
[d04s000] Inktank Storage is the lead development contributor and financial sponsor company behind the open source Ceph distributed file system.
[d04s001] Inktank was founded by Sage Weil and initially funded by DreamHost and Mark Shuttleworth.

[d09p000] Beijing GNU/Linux User Group
[d09s000] The Beijing GNU/Linux User Group (BLUG) was founded in Beijing on November 19, 2002 and has since met at least monthly without exception.
[d09s001] Awarded Best SFD 2007 event (1 of 3), Golden Bull 2008 by CSDN as a technology driving group and Best LUG of the Month by Linux Format early 2008.
[d09s002] The Beijing GNU/Linux User Group has also been the host of many famous actors of our movement such as RMS, Ulrich Drepper, Mark Shuttleworth or Louis Suarez to name just a few.

question: Glaramara is a fell in the English Lake District in Cumbria that stretches from Stonethwaite which is a part of a valley and civil parrish in what Borough?
context:
[d06p000] Glaramara
[d06s000] Glaramara is a fell in the English Lake District in Cumbria.
[d06s001] It is a substantial fell that is part of a long ridge that stretches for over six kilometres from Stonethwaite in Borrowdale up to the important mountain pass of Esk Hause.
[d06s002] The summit of Glaramara at 783 m (2,569 ft) is the central point of this ridge, which separates the valleys of Langstrath and Grains Gill.

[d01p000] Borrowdale
[d01s000] Borrowdale is a valley and civil parish in the English Lake District in the Borough of Allerdale in Cumbria, England.

[d04p000] Stonethwaite
[d04s000] Stonethwaite is a small village in the Lake District in the English county of Cumbria.
[d04s001] Historically part of Cumberland, it is situated in the valley of the Stonethwaite Beck, a side valley of Borrowdale, and within the Lake District National Park.

question: Who was an important leader of the Democratic-Republican Party?
context:
[d01p000] Democratic-Republican Party
[d01s000] The Democratic-Republican Party was an American political party formed by Thomas Jefferson and James Madison in 1791–93 to oppose the centralizing policies of the new Federalist Party run by Alexander Hamilton (1755/57-1804), who was secretary of the treasury and chief architect of George Washington's administration.
[d01s001] The new party controlled the presidency and Congress, as well as most states, from 1801 to 1825, during the First Party System.
[d01s002] It began in 1791 as one faction in Congress, and included many politicians who had been opposed to the new constitution.

[d03p000] Albert Gallatin
[d03s000] Abraham Alfonse Albert Gallatin (January 29, 1761 – August 12, 1849) was a Swiss-American politician, diplomat, ethnologist and linguist.
[d03s001] He was an important leader of the Democratic-Republican Party, serving in various federal elective and appointed positions across four decades.
[d03s002] He represented Pennsylvania in the Senate and the House of Representatives before becoming the longest-tenured United States Secretary of the Treasury and serving as a high-ranking diplomat.

[d02p000] Whig Party (United States)
[d02s000] The Whig Party was a political party active in the middle of the 19th century in the United States.
[d02s001] Four US presidents belonged to the party while in office.
[d02s002] It emerged in the 1830s as the leading opponent of Jacksonians, pulling together former members of the National Republican (one of the successors of the Democratic-Republican Party) and Anti-Masonic Parties.

[d04p003] United States elections, 1812
[d04s003] However, the Democratic-Republican Party continued its control of the Presidency and both houses of Congress.

[d06p000] United States elections, 1828
[d06s000] The 1828 United States elections elected the members of the 21st United States Congress.
[d06s001] It marked the beginning of the Second Party System, and the definitive split of the Democratic-Republican Party into the Democratic Party (organized around Andrew Jackson) and the National Republican Party (organized around John Quincy Adams and opponents of Jackson).
[d06s002] While the Democrats cultivated strong local organizations, the National Republicans relied on a clear national platform of high tariffs and internal improvements.

[d00p000] Presidency of Thomas Jefferson
[d00s000] The presidency of Thomas Jefferson began on March 4, 1801, when he was inaugurated as the third President of the United States, and ended on March 4, 1809.
[d00s001] Jefferson assumed the office after defeating incumbent President John Adams in the 1800 presidential election.
[d00s002] The election was a realigning election in which the Democratic-Republican Party swept the Federalist Party out of power, ushering in a generation of Democratic-Republican dominance in American politics.

[d05p003] United States presidential election, 1800
[d05s003] The election was a realigning election that ushered in a generation of Democratic-Republican Party rule and the eventual demise of the Federalist Party in the First Party System.
[d05s004] It was a long, bitter re-match of the 1796 election between the pro-French and pro-decentralization Democratic-Republicans under Jefferson and Aaron Burr and the incumbent Adams and Charles Pinckney's pro-British and pro-centralization Federalists.
[d05s005] The chief political issues revolved around the fallout from the French Revolution, including opposition to the tax imposed by Congress to pay for the mobilization of the new army and the navy in the Quasi-War against France in 1798.

[d01p003] Democratic-Republican Party
[d01s003] They called themselves "Republicans" after their ideology, Republicanism.
[d01s004] They distrusted the Federalist commitment to republicanism.
[d01s005] The party splintered in 1824 into the Jacksonian movement (which became the Democratic Party in 1828) and the short-lived National Republican Party (later succeeded by the Whig Party).

[d02p003] Whig Party (United States)
[d02s003] It had distant links to the upscale traditions of the Federalist Party.
[d02s004] Along with the rival Democratic Party, it was central to the Second Party System from the early 1840s to the mid-1860s.
[d02s005] It originally formed in opposition to the policies of President Andrew Jackson (in office 1829–37) and his Democratic Party.

[d00p003] Presidency of Thomas Jefferson
[d00s003] After two terms, Jefferson was succeeded by Secretary of State James Madison, also of the Democratic-Republican Party.

question: What Electoral Division in Victoria contained a suburb of Melbourne with a population of 25,147 at the 2016 Census?
context:
[d09p000] South Yarra, Victoria
[d09s000] South Yarra is an inner suburb of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, 4 km south-east of Melbourne's Central Business District, located within the Cities of Melbourne and Stonnington local government areas. South Yarra recorded a population of 25,147 at the 2016 Census.

[d03p000] Fitzroy, Victoria
[d03s000] Fitzroy is an inner-city suburb of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, 3 km north-east of Melbourne's Central Business District in the local government area of the City of Yarra.
[d03s001] At the 2016 Census, Fitzroy had a population of 10,445.
[d03s002] Planned as Melbourne's first suburb, it was later also one of the city's first areas to gain municipal status.

[d06p003] Division of Maribyrnong
[d06s003] Due to redistributions, the division has been slowly moving west.
[d06s004] It originally covered the suburbs of Footscray and North Melbourne.
[d06s005] According to the 2011 census, Maribyrnong has the highest proportion of Catholics in any Commonwealth Electoral Division in Australia with 41.6% of the population.

[d00p000] Division of Balaclava
[d00s000] The Division of Balaclava was an Australian Electoral Division in Victoria.
[d00s001] The division was created in 1900 and was one of the original 75 divisions contested at the first federal election.
[d00s002] It was named for the suburb of Balaclava, which in turn was named for a battlefield of the Crimean War.

[d04p000] District electoral division
[d04s000] A district electoral division (DED; Irish: "Toghroinn ceantair" ) is a former name given to a low-level territorial division in Ireland.
[d04s001] In 1994, both district electoral divisions and wards (the equivalent of district electoral divisions within the five county boroughs) were renamed as electoral divisions (the boundaries and names of the DEDs and wards themselves remained unchanged).
[d04s002] In the Republic of Ireland, DEDs are the smallest legally defined administrative areas in the state for which small area population statistics (SAPS) are published from the Census.

[d07p000] Division of McMillan
[d07s000] The Division of McMillan is an Australian Electoral Division in the state of Victoria.
[d07s001] It is located in the western part of the Gippsland region, which extends for the length of Victoria's eastern Bass Strait coastline.
[d07s002] It includes the outer south-eastern Melbourne suburb of Pakenham, and also includes the towns of Warragul, Moe, Wonthaggi, Leongatha and Foster.

[d01p000] Division of Kooyong
[d01s000] The Division of Kooyong is an Australian Electoral Division in the state of Victoria.
[d01s001] The Division was proclaimed in 1900, and was one of the original 75 divisions to be contested at the first Federal election.
[d01s002] It covers an area of approximately 52 km2 in the inner-east suburbs of Melbourne.

[d08p000] Division of Fawkner
[d08s000] The Division of Fawkner was an Australian Electoral Division in Victoria.
[d08s001] The division was created in 1906 as a replacement for Southern Melbourne, and was abolished itself in 1969.
[d08s002] It was named for John Pascoe Fawkner, one of the founders of Melbourne.

[d05p000] Penparcau
[d05s000] Penparcau is a village and an electoral division in Aberystwyth, Ceredigion, Wales, constituting the south side of Aberystwyth.
[d05s001] Aberystwyth-Penparcau is the largest electoral division in Ceredigion and elects two county councillors.
[d05s002] It is also the 3rd most populated division in Ceredigion (3,122 Census 2011) after Aberystwyth and Cardigan.

[d08p003] Division of Fawkner
[d08s003] It was located in the inner southern suburbs of Melbourne, including at various times Prahran, South Yarra, St Kilda and Toorak.
[d08s004] It was usually a safe conservative seat, but was occasionally won by the Australian Labor Party.

[d04s001] He has worked as a producer, music arranger, songwriter, television host, and solo artist; been inducted into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame, the Georgia Music Hall of Fame, and the Christian Music Hall of Fame; and received Gold Albums for his music sales.

[d01s000] Montel Brian Anthony Williams (born July 3, 1956) is an American television personality, radio talk show host, and actor.
[d01s001] He is best known as host of the long-running "The Montel Williams Show", and more recently as a spokesman for the Partnership for Prescription Assistance (PPA), Williams is also active with the nonprofit MS Foundation, which he founded after being diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 1999.

[d09s001] Primarily a doubles specialist, he was known for his quick racket and tactical astuteness.
[d09s002] He was ranked first in the U.S. men's doubles for twelve consecutive seasons (1965–1976); all but the last of these in a partnership with fellow left-hander Jim Poole that was consistently competitive at the world class level.

[d02s000] Vampirovibrio chorellavorus is a 0.6 µm pleomorphic cocci with a gram negative cell wall, and is one of the few known predatory bacteria.
[d02s001] Unlike many bacteria, "Vampirovibrio chlorellavorus" is an obligate parasite, attaching to the cell wall of green algae of the genus "Chlorella".
[d02s002] "Vampirovibrio" originates from the Hungarian words "vampir" meaning vampire (due to the nature of sucking out cellular contents of its prey) and "vibrio" referring to the bacterial genus of curved rod bacterium.

[d08s000] Fremont High School is an urban public high school located in the Fruitvale District of East Oakland, California, United States.
[d08s001] It was formerly a group of smaller high schools located on the same campus and known as Fremont Federation of High Schools.
[d08s002] The school's present configuration is that of the "wall to wall" career academies model, consisting of a 9th Grade House which feeds into one of three California Partnership Academies (CPA), specifically the Architecture Academy, Mandela Law & Public Service Academy, and Media Academy.

[d05s000] Salomon Brothers was a Wall Street investment bank, known as a bulge bracket company.

question: What year was Playford B Power Station permanently closed in by its Australian operator?
context:
[d07p003] Playford B Power Station
[d07s003] Commissioned in 1963, it was co-located with the larger, newer Northern Power Station.
[d07s004] Playford B was mothballed in 2012 and its permanent closure was announced by operator Alinta Energy in October 2015.
[d07s005] Prior to being mothballed it primarily operated in the summer, when electricity demand peaks.

[d01p000] Playford A Power Station
[d01s000] Playford A power station was the first power station built by the Electricity Trust of South Australia at Port Paterson, South Australia near Port Augusta in South Australia.
[d01s001] It was built in the early 1950s to generate electricity from coal mined from the Telford Cut at Leigh Creek and transported 250 km by rail.
[d01s002] It was joined by the Playford B Power Station soon after, and the Northern Power Station in 1980.

[d07p000] Playford B Power Station
[d07s000] Playford B Power Station was located at Port Paterson in the Australian state of South Australia about 5.5 km south of the city centre of Port Augusta.
[d07s001] It was coal powered with four 60 MW steam turbines that generate a total of 240 MW of electricity.
[d07s002] Playford B received coal by rail from the Leigh Creek Coal Mine, 280 km to the north and draws cooling water from Spencer Gulf, returning it to the sea at an elevated temperature.

[d09p006] Dunston Power Station
[d09s006] From the A Station's opening in 1910 until the B Station's demolition in 1986, they collectively operated from the early days of electricity generation in the United Kingdom, through the industry's nationalisation, and until a decade before its privatisation.

[d08p000] Curlew Island (South Australia)
[d08s000] Curlew Island is a low mangrove-dominated island located near the head of Spencer Gulf, South Australia.
[d08s001] It lies between Port Augusta and Point Lowly and is adjacent to the Playford B Power Station.
[d08s002] Several ships ran aground in the shallow waters surrounding the island during the late 1800s and early 1900s.

[d04p000] Rugeley power stations
[d04s000] The Rugeley power stations were a series of two coal-fired power stations located on the River Trent at Rugeley in Staffordshire.
[d04s001] The first power station on the site, Rugeley A power station was opened in 1961, but has since been closed and demolished.
[d04s002] Rugeley B power station was commissioned in 1970 and closed on 8 June 2016.

[d03p003] Ironbridge power stations
[d03s003] Originally powered by coal, they were converted to use 100% biomass fuel.
[d03s004] Ironbridge B Power Station stopped generating electricity on 20 November 2015, with the decommissioning process expected to continue into 2017.

[d02p000] Pembroke Power Station
[d02s000] Pembroke B Power Station is a 2,000 MWe natural gas-fired power station near Pembroke in Wales.
[d02s001] The power station was officially opened on 19 September 2012 and is the largest gas-fired power station in Europe.
[d02s002] It is also the largest power station to be built in the UK since Drax power station came online in 1986.

[d00p000] Alinta Energy
[d00s000] Alinta Energy is an Australian generation, electricity and gas retailing private company that is owned by Hong Kong-based Chow Tai Fook Enterprises.
[d00s001] Alinta Energy has an owned and contracted generation portfolio of up to 1,957 MW, approximately 800,000 combined electricity and gas retail customers and around 450 employees across Australia and New Zealand.

[d05p000] Blyth Power Station
[d05s000] Blyth Power Station (also known as Cambois Power Station) refers to a pair of now demolished coal-fired power stations, which were located on the Northumberland coast in North East England.
[d05s001] The two stations were built alongside each other on a site near Cambois in Northumberland, on the northern bank of the River Blyth, between its tidal estuary and the North Sea.
[d05s002] The stations took their name from the town of Blyth on the opposite bank of the estuary.

[d02s000] Carl Grimes is a fictional character from the comic book series "The Walking Dead" and is portrayed by Chandler Riggs in the American television series of the same name, which airs on AMC in the United States.
[d02s001] The character was created by writer Robert Kirkman and artist Tony Moore, and debuted in "The Walking Dead" #2 in 2003.
[d02s002] In both forms of media, Carl is the son of primary protagonist Rick Grimes, and his wife Lori Grimes, and is one of the longest-surviving characters and one of the few original Atlanta survivors still alive.

[d04p000] Hershel Greene

[d04s001] He is the widowed owner of a farm in Georgia and has previous experience in the veterinary fields.
[d04s002] A devout Christian, with uncompromising morals and a stubborn attitude, Hershel remains fiercely protective of his large family, despite his many losses.

[d01p000] Sophia Peletier

[d01s001] She is the daughter of Carol Peletier, who is fiercely protective of her, as is Carl Grimes, with whom she becomes close friends during the zombie outbreak.
[d01s002] She becomes a major focal point in both media, despite her limited involvement in many of the central conflicts faced by the other characters.

[d06p000] Lori Grimes

[d01s000] Lepidozamia is a genus of two species of cycad, both endemic to Australia.

[d00s002] There are seven species, two in South America and five in Australia, and several named hybrids.

[d00s003] They are mostly evergreen though one species ("E. glutinosa") is usually deciduous.

[d01s003] They have a chromosome number of 2n = 18.

question: Where did the Discovery Channel show franchise that Ben Bailey is an executive producer on originate from?
context:
[d06p000] Ben Bailey
[d06s000] Benjamin Ray Bailey (born October 30, 1970 in Bowling Green, Kentucky) is an American comedian, licensed taxi cab driver, and Emmy Award winning former game show host and executive producer for Discovery Channel's "Cash Cab" in New York City.

[d07p000] Cash Cab (U.S. game show)
[d07s000] Cash Cab (stylized as CA$H CAB) is an American game show that aired new episodes on the Discovery Channel from 2005 to 2012.
[d07s001] It began airing on December 5, 2005, hosted by stand-up comedian Ben Bailey.
[d07s002] It is part of the global "Cash Cab" franchise that originated in the United Kingdom.

[d04p000] Discovery Channel
[d04s000] Discovery Channel (formerly The Discovery Channel from 1985 to 1995, and often referred to as simply Discovery) is an American basic cable and satellite television channel (which is also delivered via IPTV, terrestrial television and internet television in other parts of the world) that is the flagship television property of Discovery Communications, a publicly traded company run by CEO David Zaslav.
[d04s001] s of 2012 , Discovery Channel is the third most widely distributed cable channel in the United States, behind TBS and The Weather Channel; it is available in 409 million households worldwide, through its U.S. flagship channel and its various owned or licensed television channels internationally.

[d00p000] Discovery (UK and Ireland)
[d00s000] Discovery (formerly Discovery Channel) is an English speaking channel which targets the United Kingdom and Ireland, operated by Discovery Networks Western Europe.
[d00s001] The channel's programming is based on programming produced by Discovery Networks Europe, Discovery Channel Canada and Discovery Channel from the United States.

[d08p000] The FBI Files
[d08s000] The FBI Files is an American television docudrama series that originally ran from 1998 to 2006.
[d08s001] It was carried by the Discovery Channel cable network and produced by New Dominion Pictures of Suffolk, Virginia.
[d08s002] The show was cancelled by the Discovery Channel in 2006; however, Escape (TV network), Discovery Channel and its sister network, Investigation Discovery, air re-runs, although until October 2012, Investigation Discovery only showed episodes from seasons 5,6, and 7.

[d09p003] You Spoof Discovery
[d09s003] The makers of parodies that made it on the air were given $500 from the Discovery Channel.
[d09s004] According to Jane Root, then the president of Discovery Channel, the series was intended to be the beginning of a new wave of viewer-generated content.

[d05p006] Mick Kaczorowski
[d05s006] He edited Discovery Channel’s first original production Ivory Wars.
[d05s007] Kaczorowski joined Discovery Communications in 1994 holding many positions and titles across different Discovery networks.
[d05s008] Over the next 20 years, he developed, supervised and managed everything from documentary specials and long running series, IMAX movies “”, Discovery’s first feature film “”, Animal Planet’s first feature film “” and Animal Planet’s first scripted drama “The Whale”.

[d03p003] Billy Derian
[d03s003] Billy D currently is executive producer/creator of several network/cable shows.

[d09p000] You Spoof Discovery

[d01p000] The Wolf Man (1924 film)
[d01s000] The Wolf Man is a 1924 American silent drama film that starred John Gilbert and Norma Shearer, before they signed with the newly formed MGM.
[d01s001] Directed by Edmund Mortimer, the film's story was written by Reed Heustis, and written by Fanny and Frederic Hatton.

[d07p003] Edmund Mortimer (actor)
[d07s003] He was born in New York, New York and died in Los Angeles, California.

[d02p000] Edmund Mortimer, 5th Earl of March
[d02s000] Edmund de Mortimer, 5th Earl of March and 7th Earl of Ulster (6 November 1391 – 18 January 1425) was an English nobleman.
[d02s001] A great-great-grandson of King Edward III of England, he was heir presumptive to King Richard II of England, his first cousin twice removed, when Richard II was deposed in favour of Henry IV.
[d02s002] Edmund Mortimer's claim to the throne was the basis of rebellions and plots against Henry IV and his son Henry V, and was later taken up by the House of York in the Wars of the Roses, though Mortimer himself was an important and loyal vassal of Henry V and Henry VI.

[d05p000] Against All Odds (1924 film)
[d05s000] Against All Odds is a lost 1924 silent film western directed by Edmund Mortimer and starring Buck Jones.
[d05s001] It was produced and distributed by Fox Film Corporation.

[d08p000] Tripartite Indenture
[d08s000] The Tripartite Indenture was an agreement made in February 1405 between Owain Glyndŵr, Edmund Mortimer, and Henry Percy, 1st Earl of Northumberland, agreeing to divide England and Wales up between them at the expense of Henry IV.
[d08s001] Glyndŵr was to be given Wales, and a substantial part of the west of England, including the English portions of the Welsh Marches.
[d08s002] Northumberland was to have received the north, as well as Northamptonshire, Norfolk, Warwickshire, and Leicestershire.

[d02p003] Edmund Mortimer, 5th Earl of March
[d02s003] Edmund Mortimer was the last Earl of March of the Mortimer family.

[d06p000] Edmund Mortimer (1302–1331)
[d06s000] Sir Edmund Mortimer (1302/1303 – 16 December 1331) was the eldest son of Roger Mortimer, 1st Earl of March and Joan de Geneville, 2nd Baroness Geneville.
[d06s001] By his wife Elizabeth de Badlesmere he was the father of Roger Mortimer, 2nd Earl of March.
[d06s002] Though Edmund survived his father by one year, he did not inherit his father's lands and titles as they were forfeited to the Crown and his son only reacquired them gradually.

[d09p000] Lady Elizabeth Percy
[d09s000] Lady Elizabeth Percy (c. 1395 – 26 October 1436) was the daughter of Sir Henry Percy, known to history as 'Hotspur', and Elizabeth Mortimer.
[d09s001] Her mother was the eldest daughter of Edmund Mortimer, 3rd Earl of March and his wife, Philippa, the only child of Lionel, 1st Duke of Clarence, and Elizabeth de Burgh, Countess of Ulster.

[d03p000] 32nd Independent Spirit Awards
[d03s000] The 32nd Independent Spirit Awards (2017) nominees were announced by Film Independent, the nonprofit arts organization that produces them, on November 22, 2016.

[d03s002] Online streaming service Sundance Now live-streamed the Spirit Awards concurrently with the telecast, with an on-demand version available on Sundance Now.

[d04s000] The 2012 Independent Spirit Awards was the 28th annual occasion of the Film Independent Spirit Awards.

[d04s002] The winners were announced on February 23, 2013 during an awards ceremony hosted by Andy Samberg.

[d00p000] Independent Spirit Awards
[d00s000] The Film Independent Spirit Awards (abbreviated "Spirit Awards" and originally known as the FINDIE or Friends of Independents Awards), founded in 1984, are awards dedicated to independent filmmakers.
[d00s001] Winners were typically presented with acrylic glass pyramids containing suspended shoestrings representing the paltry budgets of independent films.
[d00s002] Since 2006, winners have received a trophy depicting a bird with its wings spread sitting atop of a pole with the shoestrings from the previous design wrapped around the pole.

[d01p006] Cell fate determination
[d01s006] This is one of the reasons that model systems such as the fly ("Drosophila melanogaster"), the mouse (Muridae), and the leech ("Helobdella"), can all be used to study embryogenesis and developmental biology relevant to other animals, including humans.
[d01s007] What continues to be discovered and investigated is how the basic set of proteins (and mRNAs) are expressed differentially between cells types, temporally and spatially; and whether this is responsible for the vast diversity of organisms produced.
[d01s008] This leads to one of the key questions of developmental biology of how is cell fate determined.

[d01p000] Cell fate determination
[d01s000] Within the field of developmental biology one goal is to understand how a particular cell (or embryo) develops into the final cell type (or organism), essentially how a cell's fate is determined.
[d01s001] Within an embryo, 4 processes play out at the cellular and tissue level to essentially create the final organism.
[d01s002] These processes are cell proliferation, cell specialization, cell interaction and cell movement.

[d01p003] Cell fate determination
[d01s003] Each cell in the embryo receives and gives cues to its neighboring cells and retains a cell memory of its own cell proliferation history.
[d01s004] Almost all animals undergo a similar sequence of events during embryogenesis and have, at least at this developmental stage, the three germ layers and undergo gastrulation.
[d01s005] While embryogenesis has been studied for more than a century, it was only recently (the past 15 years or so) that scientists discovered that a basic set of the same proteins and mRNAs are involved in all of embryogenesis.

[d06p000] Retinoblastoma protein
[d06s000] The retinoblastoma protein (protein name abbreviated pRb; gene name abbreviated RB or RB1) is a tumor suppressor protein that is dysfunctional in several major cancers.
[d06s001] One function of pRb is to prevent excessive cell growth by inhibiting cell cycle progression until a cell is ready to divide.
[d06s002] When the cell is ready to divide, pRb is phosphorylated, becomes inactive and allows cell cycle progression.

[d02p000] The Ready Set
[d02s000] Jordan Mark Witzigreuter (born November 14, 1989), known professionally as The Ready Set, is an American singer-songwriter from Fort Wayne, Indiana.
[d02s001] He is the lead vocalist and sole member of the act, using a backup band while on tour.
[d02s002] Witzigreuter created The Ready Set in the basement of his childhood home in Fort Wayne, Indiana.

[d05p000] Ready Set Roll
[d05s000] "Ready Set Roll" is a song recorded by American country music artist Chase Rice.
[d05s001] It was released in November 2013 as his first single from his EP album, "Ready Set Roll", and later appeared on his first major-label studio album, "Ignite the Night".
[d05s002] Rice wrote the song with Chris DeStefano, who also produced it, and Rhett Akins.

[d04p012] IBM 2997
[d04s012] His work led to the development of the NCI Blood Cell Separator and later to the IBM 2990 Blood Cell Separator which could harvest white blood cells from blood donors, to support leukemia patients to keep them alive.
[d04s013] The subsequent development of the machine as the IBM 2997, essentially a continuous centrifuge which separated the blood into red blood cells, white blood cells, and blood plasma (used in plasmapheresis), was picked up by IBM's Systems Supplies Division (SSD) which was already ready marketing the IBM 2991 Blood cell Processor.
[d04s014] The (disposable) supplies element represented a large part of the revenue stream.

[d08p000] Ready Ready Set Go
[d08s000] Ready Ready Set Go is the first compilation album (third overall) by Canadian musical duo Prozzäk, released under the name Simon and Milo, by Hollywood Records on April 30, 2002.
[d08s001] This was a limited edition CD and also enhanced with three bonus videos.
[d08s002] The album's name is taken from the opening line from "Pretty Girls (Make Me Nervous)", the first track on the album.

[d03p003] Ready Set Go! (album)
[d03s003] A hip hop album with influences of pop and contemporary R&B, "Ready Set Go" features hook-driven content sung by Dash's high-pitched, nasal voice.

[d02p003] The Ready Set
[d02s003] He has released four studio albums "Tantrum Castle", "I'm Alive, I'm Dreaming," "The Bad & The Better", and "I Will Be Nothing Without Your Love," four extended plays and seven singles.
[d02s004] Fall Out Boy bassist Pete Wentz signed The Ready Set to his label Decaydance Records, in 2009.
[d02s005] He is currently with Hopeless Records.

question: What year was Playford B Power Station permanently closed in by its Australian operator?
context:
[d07p003] Playford B Power Station
[d07s003] Commissioned in 1963, it was co-located with the larger, newer Northern Power Station.
[d07s004] Playford B was mothballed in 2012 and its permanent closure was announced by operator Alinta Energy in October 2015.
[d07s005] Prior to being mothballed it primarily operated in the summer, when electricity demand peaks.

[d01p000] Playford A Power Station
[d01s000] Playford A power station was the first power station built by the Electricity Trust of South Australia at Port Paterson, South Australia near Port Augusta in South Australia.
[d01s001] It was built in the early 1950s to generate electricity from coal mined from the Telford Cut at Leigh Creek and transported 250 km by rail.
[d01s002] It was joined by the Playford B Power Station soon after, and the Northern Power Station in 1980.

[d04p000] Rugeley power stations
[d04s000] The Rugeley power stations were a series of two coal-fired power stations located on the River Trent at Rugeley in Staffordshire.
[d04s001] The first power station on the site, Rugeley A power station was opened in 1961, but has since been closed and demolished.
[d04s002] Rugeley B power station was commissioned in 1970 and closed on 8 June 2016.

[d06p000] Kosovo A Power Station
[d06s000] Kosovo A Power Station is a lignite power station with five units at Obilić, Kosovo.
[d06s001] It is the second largest power station in Kosovo with capacity of 650 MW after Kosovo B Power Station.
[d06s002] It is described as the worst single-point source of pollution in Europe and it is expected to be closed by 2017.

Walter Osborne
Walter Frederick Osborne (17 June 1859 – 24 April 1903) was an Irish impressionist and Post-Impressionism landscape and portrait painter, best known for his documentary depictions of late 19th century working class life. Most of his paintings are figurative and focus on women, children, the elderly, the poor, and the day-to-day life of ordinary people on Dublin streets, as well as series of rural scenes. He also produced city-scapes, which he painted from both sketches and photographs.

[d04s000] Prof. Dr. Ulrich Hans Walter (born February 9, 1954) is a German physicist/engineer and a former DFVLR astronaut.
