[d08p000] David J. Thouless
[d08s000] David James Thouless {'1': ", '2': ", '3': ", '4': "} ( , born 21 September 1934) is a British condensed-matter physicist.
[d08s001] He is a winner of the Wolf Prize and laureate of the 2016 Nobel Prize for physics along with F. Duncan M. Haldane and J. Michael Kosterlitz for theoretical discoveries of topological phase transitions and topological phases of matter.
[d08s002] In 2016, Thouless was reported to be suffering from dementia.

[d03p000] François Englert
[d03s000] François Baron Englert (] ; born 6 November 1932) is a Belgian theoretical physicist and 2013 Nobel prize laureate (shared with Peter Higgs).
[d03s001] He is Professor emeritus at the Université libre de Bruxelles (ULB) where he is member of the Service de Physique Théorique.
[d03s002] He is also a Sackler Professor by Special Appointment in the School of Physics and Astronomy at Tel Aviv University and a member of the Institute for Quantum Studies at Chapman University in California.

[d05p000] Stockholm Memorandum
[d05s000] The Stockholm Memorandum is a document signed in May 2011 by many Nobel Laureates based on the verdict from the trial of humanity, which opened the 3rd Nobel Laureate Symposium.
[d05s001] The jury of Nobel laureates concluded that Earth has entered a new geological age, which it calls the Anthropocene, in which humans are the most significant driver of global climate change, and in which human collective actions could have abrupt and irreversible consequences for human communities and ecological systems.
[d05s002] The memorandum was signed by 20 winner of the Nobel Prize winners or the Sveriges Riksbank Prize for Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel (six in Chemistry, five in Physics, three in Physiology or Medicine, one in Literature, one Peace Prize winner and four in Economic Sciences) was submitted to the United Nations High Level Panel on global sustainability.

[d02p000] Wolf Prize in Mathematics

[d05s000] Fiat S.p.A., or "Fabbrica Italiana Automobili Torino" (Italian Automobile Factory of Turin), was an Italian holding company whose original and core activities were in the automotive industry, and that was succeeded by Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV (FCA).
[d05s001] The Fiat Group contained many brands such as Ferrari, Maserati, Fiat, Alfa Romeo, the Chrysler Group, and many more.
[d05s002] On 29 January 2014, it was announced that Fiat S.p.A. (the former owner of Fiat Group) was to be merged into a new Netherlands-based holding company Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV (FCA), took place before the end of 2014.

[d01p000] Fiat Chrysler Automobiles
[d01s000] Fiat Chrysler Automobiles N.V. (abbreviated as FCA) is an Italian-controlled multinational corporation incorporated in the Netherlands, and currently the world’s seventh-largest auto maker.
[d01s001] The group was established in late 2014 by merging Fiat S.p.A. into a new holding company, FCA (with headquarters in London) for tax purposes.
[d01s002] The holding company is listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Borsa Italiana in Milan.

[d02p000] Fiat Industrial
[d02s000] Fiat Industrial S.p.A. was an Italian company into which Fiat S.p.A. (parent company of Fiat Group) demerged most of its activities not directly related to automobiles at the start of 2011.
[d02s001] Fiat Industrial served as a holding company for the activities of truck manufacturer Iveco; an 89.3% stake in the agricultural and construction equipment producer CNH Global; and FPT Industrial, which consists of the industrial and marine activities formerly part of Fiat Powertrain Technologies.
[d02s002] The company's Chairman was Sergio Marchionne, who also served as CEO of Fiat S.p.A. and Chairman/CEO of Chrysler Group LLC, now merged as Fiat Chrysler Automobiles.

question: What genre of music was played by both Tappi Tíkarrass and INXS?
context:
[d03p000] INXS
[d03s000] INXS ( ) were an Australian rock band, formed as The Farriss Brothers in 1977 in Sydney, New South Wales.
[d03s001] They began playing covers in Western Australian pubs and clubs, occasionally playing some of their original music.
[d03s002] Mainstays were main composer and keyboardist Andrew Farriss, drummer Jon Farriss, guitarists Tim Farriss and Kirk Pengilly, bassist Garry Gary Beers and main lyricist and vocalist Michael Hutchence.

[d03p003] INXS
[d03s003] For twenty years, INXS was fronted by Hutchence, whose "sultry good looks" and magnetic stage presence made him the focal point of the band.
[d03s004] Initially known for their new wave/pop style, the band later developed a harder pub rock style that included funk and dance elements.

[d02p000] Tappi Tíkarrass
[d02s000] Tappi Tíkarrass was an Icelandic punk band which added elements of funk, rock and jazz to their music, marking a difference from other traditional bands at that time.
[d02s001] The band is also considered the first serious music project of now renowned singer Björk Guðmundsdóttir.

[d00p000] Bitið fast í vitið
[d00s000] Bitið fast í vitið (roughly "Bite Hard In Your Mind" in Icelandic) is the début EP of Icelander punk/pop group Tappi Tíkarrass .
[d00s001] It was released in late-1982 on the Spor label, within a year of the band's formation in September 1981 – led by vocalists Björk and Eyþór Arnalds .
[d00s002] This was the band's most punk-oriented release and contains five tracks, featuring one in English, "London".

[d09p000] Miranda (album)
[d09s000] Miranda is the only studio album by Icelandic punk band Tappi Tíkarrass.
[d09s001] It was released on December 23, 1983 through Gramm.

[d08p000] Folk rock
[d08s000] Folk rock is a music genre combining elements of folk music and rock music.
[d08s001] In its earliest and narrowest sense, the term referred to a genre that arose in the United States and the United Kingdom around the mid-1960s.
[d08s002] The genre emerged from bands such as the Beatles, the Searchers, and the Animals in the UK, and Bob Dylan and the Byrds in the US, who played traditional folk music and songs with rock instrumentation.

[d01p003] Steeltown (band)
[d01s003] The group members were Andy Richmond vocals, Peter Howard keyboards, Terry Gidman drums and Kate Richmond vocals and percussion and Reece Speceis Lead Guitar.
[d01s004] The band were formed from the remnant members of a Scottish group called the Technicians who migrated to Australia in the 80s and who also attained top 40 status with their music releases, Hot for Love, Clockwork Clown and Sodier of Fortune through record companies Powderworks, EMI and BMG, and were published by MMA which was owned by legendary rock outfit INXS.

[d04p000] Nýtt líf
[d04s000] Nýtt Líf (   , English: "New Life") is an Icelandic film directed by Þráinn Bertelsson and released in 1983.
[d04s001] The film is a comedy shot in the Westman Islands and stars Eggert Þorleifsson and Karl Ágúst Úlfsson, among others.
[d04s002] The music features several musicians including the band Tappi Tíkarrass (of which Björk was a member), which contributed the songs "Sperglar" and "Kukl" (a.k.a. "Seiður").

[d07p000] Rave music
[d07s000] Rave music may either refer to the late 1980s/early 1990s genres of house, breakbeat, acid house, techno and hardcore techno, which were the first genres of music to be played at rave parties, or to any other genre of electronic dance music (EDM) that may be played at a rave.
[d07s001] The genre "rave", also known as hardcore by early ravers, first appeared amongst the UK "acid" movement during the late 1980s at warehouse parties and other underground venues, as well as on UK pirate radio stations.
[d07s002] The genre would develop into oldschool hardcore, which lead onto newer forms of rave music such as drum and bass and 2-step, as well as other hardcore techno genres, such as gabber, hardstyle and happy hardcore.

[d05p000] Disco polo
[d05s000] Disco polo is a musical genre of popular music that is dance music, created in Poland in the late 1980s, initially known as "sidewalks music" ("muzyka chodnikowa").
[d05s001] This trend, also known as city folklore music, was popular in the mid-late 1990s, with its peak taking place around 1995–1997.
[d05s002] Later observed a gradual decline in the popularity led to the temporary collapse in the early twenty-first century.

[d06p000] Ben Bailey
[d06s000] Benjamin Ray Bailey (born October 30, 1970 in Bowling Green, Kentucky) is an American comedian, licensed taxi cab driver, and Emmy Award winning former game show host and executive producer for Discovery Channel's "Cash Cab" in New York City.

[d07p000] Cash Cab (U.S. game show)
[d07s000] Cash Cab (stylized as CA$H CAB) is an American game show that aired new episodes on the Discovery Channel from 2005 to 2012.
[d07s001] It began airing on December 5, 2005, hosted by stand-up comedian Ben Bailey.
[d07s002] It is part of the global "Cash Cab" franchise that originated in the United Kingdom.

[d04p000] Discovery Channel
[d04s000] Discovery Channel (formerly The Discovery Channel from 1985 to 1995, and often referred to as simply Discovery) is an American basic cable and satellite television channel (which is also delivered via IPTV, terrestrial television and internet television in other parts of the world) that is the flagship television property of Discovery Communications, a publicly traded company run by CEO David Zaslav.
[d04s001] s of 2012 , Discovery Channel is the third most widely distributed cable channel in the United States, behind TBS and The Weather Channel; it is available in 409 million households worldwide, through its U.S. flagship channel and its various owned or licensed television channels internationally.

[d00p000] Discovery (UK and Ireland)
[d00s000] Discovery (formerly Discovery Channel) is an English speaking channel which targets the United Kingdom and Ireland, operated by Discovery Networks Western Europe.
[d00s001] The channel's programming is based on programming produced by Discovery Networks Europe, Discovery Channel Canada and Discovery Channel from the United States.

[d08p000] The FBI Files
[d08s000] The FBI Files is an American television docudrama series that originally ran from 1998 to 2006.
[d08s001] It was carried by the Discovery Channel cable network and produced by New Dominion Pictures of Suffolk, Virginia.
[d08s002] The show was cancelled by the Discovery Channel in 2006; however, Escape (TV network), Discovery Channel and its sister network, Investigation Discovery, air re-runs, although until October 2012, Investigation Discovery only showed episodes from seasons 5,6, and 7.

[d09p003] You Spoof Discovery
[d09s003] The makers of parodies that made it on the air were given $500 from the Discovery Channel.
[d09s004] According to Jane Root, then the president of Discovery Channel, the series was intended to be the beginning of a new wave of viewer-generated content.

[d05p006] Mick Kaczorowski
[d05s006] He edited Discovery Channel’s first original production Ivory Wars.
[d05s007] Kaczorowski joined Discovery Communications in 1994 holding many positions and titles across different Discovery networks.
[d05s008] Over the next 20 years, he developed, supervised and managed everything from documentary specials and long running series, IMAX movies “”, Discovery’s first feature film “”, Animal Planet’s first feature film “” and Animal Planet’s first scripted drama “The Whale”.

[d09p000] You Spoof Discovery
[d09s000] You Spoof Discovery: The ultimate viewer-submitted low-cost high-quality extremely entertaining Discovery parody special hosted by Mike Rowe of Dirty Jobs, who also narrates the series American Chopper, American Hot Rod and Deadliest Catch, commonly shortened to You Spoof Discovery, was a one-hour special on the Discovery Channel which showed viewer-submitted parodies of Discovery Channel shows.
[d09s001] The special premiered on February 25, 2007 and was hosted by Mike Rowe.
[d09s002] Over 600 entries were submitted.

[d05p000] Mick Kaczorowski
[d05s000] Michael "Mick" Kaczorowski (born January 4, 1960) is the Creative Director and Producer of Bangkok Swagger is a nine time nominated and three time Emmy Award winning Producer and Executive Producer.
[d05s001] As Executive Producer, he is responsible for some of Animal Planet and Discovery’s biggest and most iconic hits including , Raising the Mammoth, and Walking with Prehistoric Beasts.
[d05s002] Kaczorowski is also responsible for many of Discovery Channel and Animal Planet long running hit series including Meerkat Manor, North Woods Law, River Monsters, Alaskan Bush Family, Wild West Alaska, Buggin with Rude, and American Stuffers.

question: What year was Playford B Power Station permanently closed in by its Australian operator?
context:
[d07p003] Playford B Power Station
[d07s003] Commissioned in 1963, it was co-located with the larger, newer Northern Power Station.
[d07s004] Playford B was mothballed in 2012 and its permanent closure was announced by operator Alinta Energy in October 2015.
[d07s005] Prior to being mothballed it primarily operated in the summer, when electricity demand peaks.

[d01p000] Playford A Power Station
[d01s000] Playford A power station was the first power station built by the Electricity Trust of South Australia at Port Paterson, South Australia near Port Augusta in South Australia.
[d01s001] It was built in the early 1950s to generate electricity from coal mined from the Telford Cut at Leigh Creek and transported 250 km by rail.
[d01s002] It was joined by the Playford B Power Station soon after, and the Northern Power Station in 1980.

[d09p006] Dunston Power Station
[d09s006] From the A Station's opening in 1910 until the B Station's demolition in 1986, they collectively operated from the early days of electricity generation in the United Kingdom, through the industry's nationalisation, and until a decade before its privatisation.

[d08p000] Curlew Island (South Australia)
[d08s000] Curlew Island is a low mangrove-dominated island located near the head of Spencer Gulf, South Australia.
[d08s001] It lies between Port Augusta and Point Lowly and is adjacent to the Playford B Power Station.
[d08s002] Several ships ran aground in the shallow waters surrounding the island during the late 1800s and early 1900s.

[d04p000] Rugeley power stations
[d04s000] The Rugeley power stations were a series of two coal-fired power stations located on the River Trent at Rugeley in Staffordshire.
[d04s001] The first power station on the site, Rugeley A power station was opened in 1961, but has since been closed and demolished.
[d04s002] Rugeley B power station was commissioned in 1970 and closed on 8 June 2016.

[d03p003] Ironbridge power stations
[d03s003] Originally powered by coal, they were converted to use 100% biomass fuel.
[d03s004] Ironbridge B Power Station stopped generating electricity on 20 November 2015, with the decommissioning process expected to continue into 2017.

[d02p000] Pembroke Power Station
[d02s000] Pembroke B Power Station is a 2,000 MWe natural gas-fired power station near Pembroke in Wales.
[d02s001] The power station was officially opened on 19 September 2012 and is the largest gas-fired power station in Europe.
[d02s002] It is also the largest power station to be built in the UK since Drax power station came online in 1986.

[d00p000] Alinta Energy
[d00s000] Alinta Energy is an Australian generation, electricity and gas retailing private company that is owned by Hong Kong-based Chow Tai Fook Enterprises.
[d00s001] Alinta Energy has an owned and contracted generation portfolio of up to 1,957 MW, approximately 800,000 combined electricity and gas retail customers and around 450 employees across Australia and New Zealand.

[d05p000] Blyth Power Station
[d05s000] Blyth Power Station (also known as Cambois Power Station) refers to a pair of now demolished coal-fired power stations, which were located on the Northumberland coast in North East England.
[d05s001] The two stations were built alongside each other on a site near Cambois in Northumberland, on the northern bank of the River Blyth, between its tidal estuary and the North Sea.
[d05s002] The stations took their name from the town of Blyth on the opposite bank of the estuary.

[d07p000] Playford B Power Station
[d07s000] Playford B Power Station was located at Port Paterson in the Australian state of South Australia about 5.5 km south of the city centre of Port Augusta.
[d07s001] It was coal powered with four 60 MW steam turbines that generate a total of 240 MW of electricity.
[d07s002] Playford B received coal by rail from the Leigh Creek Coal Mine, 280 km to the north and draws cooling water from Spencer Gulf, returning it to the sea at an elevated temperature.

[d05p000] Verelo
[d05s000] Verelo, originally based in Toronto, Canada and acquired by infrastructure as a service company Dyn in January 2013, was a website monitoring service that tracks a website's uptime, downtime, and performance.
[d05s001] Verelo monitored websites from multiple locations globally so that it could distinguish actual downtime from routing and access problems.
[d05s002] Verelo argued that downtime can be costly and even take lives, and is now based in Manchester, New Hampshire.

[d04p000] Dynatrace
[d04s000] Dynatrace is an American application performance management (APM) software company with products aimed at the information technology departments and digital business owners of medium and large businesses.
[d04s001] The company's services include performance management software for programs running on-premises and in the cloud.
[d04s002] This software manages the availability and performance of software applications and the impact on user experience in the form of deep transaction tracing, synthetic monitoring, real user monitoring, and network monitoring.

question: Which breed of dog was first recognized by their country's official kennel club, the American Hairless Terrier or the Saint-Usuge Spaniel?
context:
[d06p000] Saint-Usuge Spaniel
[d06s000] The Saint-Usuge Spaniel (or Épagneul de Saint-Usuge) is a breed of Spaniel originating in the Bresse region of France.
[d06s001] The breed has origins dating back to at least the 16th century, but was nearly extinct by the end of World War II.
[d06s002] Through the efforts of Father Robert Billard, the breed was resurrected during the second half of the 20th century; its national breed club was founded in 1990.

[d00p000] American Hairless Terrier
[d00s000] The American Hairless Terrier is a rare breed of dog that was derived as a variant of Rat Terrier.
[d00s001] As of January 1, 2004, the United Kennel Club deemed the AHT a separate terrier breed, granting it full UKC recognition.
[d00s002] An intelligent, social and energetic working breed, the American Hairless Terrier is often listed as a potential good breed choice for allergy sufferers.

[d01p000] American Russell Terrier Club
[d01s000] The American Russell Terrier Club (formerly named the English Jack Russell Terrier Club), founded by JoAnn Stoll in 1995, was the first registry in the United States to maintain the Russell Terrier as a separate breed from the Parson Russell Terrier.
[d01s001] The American Jack Russell Terrier Club is affiliated with both the United Kennel Club and the American Kennel Club.
[d01s002] The purpose of the early founders was to establish a registry for the perpetuation and development of the Russell Terrier as a pure strain of working Jack Russell Terrier keeping their blood and type pure within the registry to works towards Kennel Club recognition as an official breed in the US.

[d06p003] Saint-Usuge Spaniel
[d06s003] The breed was recognised by the Société Centrale Canine (French Kennel Club) in 2003.

question: In the muti-sport games usually held every four years between nations around the Mediterranean Sea, Fatma Lanouar is best known for winning gold in which event?
context:
[d05p000] Fatma Lanouar
[d05s000] Fatma Lanouar (Arabic: فاطمة لأنور; born March 14, 1978) is a former female middle distance runner from Tunisia.
[d05s001] She is best known for twice (2001 and 2005) winning the gold medal at the Mediterranean Games in the women's 1500 metres.
[d05s002] Lanouar set her personal best (4:06.91) in the 1,500 metres in 2000.

[d09p000] Mediterranean Games
[d09s000] The Mediterranean Games are a multi-sport games held usually every four years, between nations around or very close to the Mediterranean Sea, where Europe, Africa, and Asia meet.
[d09s001] The games are under the auspices of the International Committee of Mediterranean Games (CIJM).

[d00p000] European Masters Games
[d00s000] The European Masters Games (EMG) is a multi-sport event, consisting of summer sports, that is held every four years.
[d00s001] The age categories vary depending on the sport but the competition is generally for people 30–35 years or older.
[d00s002] The first games were held in 2008 in Malmö, Sweden.

[d06p000] Women's Rugby World Cup
[d06s000] The Women's Rugby World Cup is the premier international competition in rugby union for women.
[d06s001] The tournament is organised by the sport's governing body, World Rugby.
[d06s002] The championships are currently held every four years; the event was most recently held in France in August 2014.

[d02p000] Olympic Games
[d02s000] The modern Olympic Games or Olympics (French: "Jeux olympiques" ) are leading international sporting events featuring summer and winter sports competitions in which thousands of athletes from around the world participate in a variety of competitions.
[d02s001] The Olympic Games are considered the world's foremost sports competition with more than 200 nations participating.
[d02s002] The Olympic Games are held every four years, with the Summer and Winter Games alternating by occurring every four years but two years apart.

question: What Electoral Division in Victoria contained a suburb of Melbourne with a population of 25,147 at the 2016 Census?
context:
[d09p000] South Yarra, Victoria
[d09s000] South Yarra is an inner suburb of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, 4 km south-east of Melbourne's Central Business District, located within the Cities of Melbourne and Stonnington local government areas. South Yarra recorded a population of 25,147 at the 2016 Census.

[d03p000] Fitzroy, Victoria
[d03s000] Fitzroy is an inner-city suburb of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, 3 km north-east of Melbourne's Central Business District in the local government area of the City of Yarra.
[d03s001] At the 2016 Census, Fitzroy had a population of 10,445.
[d03s002] Planned as Melbourne's first suburb, it was later also one of the city's first areas to gain municipal status.

[d06p000] Division of Maribyrnong
[d06s000] The Division of Maribyrnong is an Australian Electoral Division in the state of Victoria.
[d06s001] It is located in the inner north-western suburbs of Melbourne.
[d06s002] It covers the suburbs of Aberfeldie, Airport West, Avondale Heights, Braybrook, Essendon, Kealba, Keilor East, Maribyrnong, Moonee Ponds, Niddrie, St. Albans and Sunshine North.

[d07p000] Division of McMillan
[d07s000] The Division of McMillan is an Australian Electoral Division in the state of Victoria.
[d07s001] It is located in the western part of the Gippsland region, which extends for the length of Victoria's eastern Bass Strait coastline.
[d07s002] It includes the outer south-eastern Melbourne suburb of Pakenham, and also includes the towns of Warragul, Moe, Wonthaggi, Leongatha and Foster.

[d02p000] Division of Hotham
[d02s000] The Division of Hotham is an Australian Electoral Division in Victoria.
[d02s001] The division was created in 1969 and is named for Sir Charles Hotham, Governor of Victoria 1854–55.
[d02s002] It is located in the south-eastern suburbs of Melbourne.

[d01p000] Division of Kooyong
[d01s000] The Division of Kooyong is an Australian Electoral Division in the state of Victoria.
[d01s001] The Division was proclaimed in 1900, and was one of the original 75 divisions to be contested at the first Federal election.
[d01s002] It covers an area of approximately 52 km2 in the inner-east suburbs of Melbourne.

[d08p003] Division of Fawkner
[d08s003] It was located in the inner southern suburbs of Melbourne, including at various times Prahran, South Yarra, St Kilda and Toorak.
[d08s004] It was usually a safe conservative seat, but was occasionally won by the Australian Labor Party.

[d03p003] Fitzroy, Victoria
[d03s003] It occupies Melbourne's smallest and most densely populated suburban area, just 100 ha.

[d06p003] Division of Maribyrnong
[d06s003] Due to redistributions, the division has been slowly moving west.
[d06s004] It originally covered the suburbs of Footscray and North Melbourne.
[d06s005] According to the 2011 census, Maribyrnong has the highest proportion of Catholics in any Commonwealth Electoral Division in Australia with 41.6% of the population.

[d02p003] Division of Hotham
[d02s003] Hotham covers an area of approximately 72 square kilometres from Oakleigh in the north to Dingley Village in the south.
[d02s004] The division includes the suburbs of Bentleigh East, Clarinda, Dingley Village, Heatherton and Moorabbin in their entirety, and parts of Clayton, Cheltenham, Hughesdale, Murrumbeena, Noble Park, Oakleigh, and Springvale.
[d02s005] Hotham is the only electorate in Victoria which does not have either a waterway or a body of water forming any part of its boundary.

context:
[d06p000] Atatürk Museum Mansion
[d06s000] Atatürk Museum Mansion (Turkish: "Atatürk Müze Köşkü" ) is a historic house museum in Ankara, Turkey.
[d06s001] It was the residence of President Mustafa Kemal Atatürk between 1921 and 1932, during the early years of the Republic.
[d06s002] The museum is situated on Çankaya St. within the Çankaya Campus.

[d02s000] Silifke Atatürk Museum (Turkish: "Silifke Atatürk Evi Müzesi" ) is a two-storey house in Silifke which hosted the founder of modern Turkey, Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, and his wife in 1925.

[d08p000] Mersin Atatürk Museum
[d08s000] The Atatürk Museum in Mersin (Turkish: "Mersin Atatürk Evi Müzesi" ) is a two-storey house in Mersin, which hosted the founder of modern Turkey, Mustafa Kemal Atatürk and his wife in 1925.

[d03p000] Atatürk Museum, Şişli
[d03s000] Atatürk Museum (Turkish: "Atatürk Müzesi" ) is a historic house museum dedicated to the life of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, the first president of the Republic of Turkey.
[d03s001] It is located in the district of Şişli, on the European side of Istanbul, Turkey.

[d06p003] Atatürk Museum Mansion
[d06s003] It is situated right beside the Çankaya Mansion.

question: What Dutch painter specialized in domestic interior scenes of middle class life and has a painting of a young woman dressed in a yellow shawl in the Louvre, Paris?
context:
[d01p000] The Lacemaker (Vermeer)
[d01s000] The Lacemaker is a painting by the Dutch artist Johannes Vermeer (1632–1675), completed around 1669–1670 and held in the Louvre, Paris.
[d01s001] The work shows a young woman dressed in a yellow shawl, holding up a pair of bobbins in her left hand as she carefully places a pin in the pillow on which she is making her bobbin lace.
[d01s002] At 24.5 cm x 21 cm (9.6 in x 8.3 in), the work is the smallest of Vermeer's paintings, but in many ways one of his most abstract and unusual.

[d06p000] Johannes Vermeer
[d06s000] Johannes, Jan or Johan Vermeer ( ; ] ; October 1632 – December 1675) was a Dutch painter who specialized in domestic interior scenes of middle-class life.
[d06s001] Vermeer was a moderately successful provincial genre painter in his lifetime.
[d06s002] He evidently was not wealthy, leaving his wife and children in debt at his death, perhaps because he produced relatively few paintings.

[d05p000] Young Woman in a Pearl Necklace (New York City)
[d05s000] Young Woman in a Pearl Necklace (after 1655) is an oil on canvas painting by an unknown painter, after a painting by the Dutch painter Willem Drost.
[d05s001] It is an example of Dutch Golden Age painting and is part of the collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

[d09p000] A Young Woman Reading (Vermeer imitator)
[d09s000] A Young Woman Reading (after 1670s) is an oil on canvas painting by an unknown painter in the manner of the Dutch painter Johannes Vermeer.
[d09s001] It is an example of Dutch Golden Age painting and is part of the collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

[d02p000] Pieter Janssens Elinga
[d02s000] Pieter Janssens Elinga (1623–1682) was a Dutch Golden Age painter, mainly of domestic interior scenes with a strong emphasis on the rectangular geometrical elements of windows, floor tiling paintings, and other elements, and a few genre figures.
[d02s001] He also painted still lifes.

[d01p003] The Lacemaker (Vermeer)
[d01s003] The canvas used was cut from the same bolt as that used for "A Young Woman Seated at the Virginals", and both paintings seem to have had identical dimensions originally.

[d07p000] Annunciation (Memling)
[d07s000] The Annunciation is an oil-on-oak panel painting attributed to the Early Netherlandish master Hans Memling.
[d07s001] Completed c. 1482, it was partially transferred to canvas in the 1920s and is today held in the Robert Lehman collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
[d07s002] It shows the Virgin in a domestic interior, two attendant angels, the archangel Gabriel dressed in rich ecclesiastical robes, and a hovering dove.

[d00p000] Co Breman
[d00s000] Ahazueros Jacobus Breman, known as Co (7 December 1865, Zwolle - 18 November 1938, Laren) was a Dutch painter.
[d00s001] He specialized in landscapes, farms and interior scenes, with figures, and was one of the first Pointillist painters in the Netherlands.

[d03p003] Alexis Leon Louis Valbrun
[d03s003] Some of his paintings are displayed at the Fondation Calvet in Avignon, the Palace of Versailles (Philip V of Spain) and the Chateau de Chantilly (Sophie Dawes, Baronne de Feucheres).
[d03s004] His historic painting "La mort de Saphire" (Fine Art Museum in Saint Lo) was exhibited at the Salon in 1843.
[d03s005] In 1846 he decorated the church Saint-Paul-Saint-Louis in Paris.

[d03p000] Alexis Leon Louis Valbrun
[d03s000] Alexis Leon Louis Valbrun (Paris, January 3, 1803 – Paris, 1852) was a prominent French painter specialized in portraits of the European aristocracy.
[d03s001] He studied under Nicolas Gosse and was a pupil of Antoine-Jean Gros.
[d03s002] He entered the École nationale supérieure des Beaux-Arts in Paris in 1817 and exhibited his work at the Salon (Paris) between 1831 and 1843.

[d07s000] The Man from Snowy River II is a 1988 Australian drama film, the sequel to the 1982 film "The Man from Snowy River".

[d08p000] Bruce Rowland
[d08s000] Bruce Rowland (born May 9, 1942 in Melbourne) is a well-known Australian composer.
[d08s001] He composed the soundtrack for the 1982 movie "The Man from Snowy River", as well as the soundtrack for its 1988 sequel "The Man from Snowy River II" (which has the United States title of "Return to Snowy River", and the United Kingdom title of "The Untamed").
[d08s002] Both films were based on Banjo Paterson's poem The Man from Snowy River.

[d03p000] The Man from Snowy River and Other Verses
[d03s000] The Man from Snowy River and Other Verses (1895) is the first collection of poems by Australian poet Banjo Paterson.
[d03s001] It was released in hardback by Angus and Robertson in 1895, and features the poet's widely anthologised poems "The Man from Snowy River", "Clancy of the Overflow", "Saltbush Bill" and "The Man from Ironbark".
[d03s002] It also contains the poet's first two poems that featured in The Bulletin Debate, a famous dispute in "The Bulletin" magazine from 1892-93 between Paterson and Henry Lawson.

[d06p000] The Man from Snowy River (TV series)
[d06s000] The Man from Snowy River is an Australian adventure drama television series based on Banjo Paterson's poem "The Man from Snowy River".
[d06s001] Released in Australia as "Banjo Paterson's The Man from Snowy River", the series was subsequently released in both the United States and the United Kingdom as "Snowy River: The McGregor Saga".

[d00p000] Return to Snowy River
[d00s000] Return to Snowy River is the original motion picture soundtrack from the 1988 film "The Man from Snowy River II".
[d00s001] The soundtrack album is named after the American title for the film.

[d04p000] The Man from Snowy River (poem)
[d04s000] "The Man from Snowy River" is a poem by Australian bush poet Banjo Paterson.
[d04s001] It was first published in "The Bulletin", an Australian news magazine, on 26 April 1890, and was published by Angus & Robertson in October 1895, with other poems by Paterson, in "The Man from Snowy River and Other Verses".

[d09p000] Snowy River
[d09s000] The Snowy River is a major river in south-eastern Australia.
[d09s001] It originates on the slopes of Mount Kosciuszko, Australia's highest mainland peak, draining the eastern slopes of the Snowy Mountains in New South Wales, before flowing through the Alpine National Park and the Snowy River National Park in Victoria and emptying into Bass Strait.

question: Were both the Battle of Stones River and the Battle of the Ch'ongch'on River fought in the 19th century?
context:
[d06p000] Battle of the Ch'ongch'on River
[d06s000] The Battle of the Ch'ongch'on River, also known as the Battle of the Ch'ongch'on () or the Second Phase Campaign Western Sector (), was a decisive battle in the Korean War, and it took place from November 25 to December 2, 1950, along the Ch'ongch'on River Valley in the northwestern part of North Korea.
[d06s001] In response to the successful Chinese First Phase Campaign against the United Nations forces, General Douglas MacArthur launched the Home-by-Christmas Offensive to evict the Chinese forces from Korea and to end the war.
[d06s002] Anticipating this reaction, the Chinese People's Volunteer Army Commander Peng Dehuai planned a counteroffensive, dubbed the "Second Phase Campaign", against the advancing UN forces.

[d04p000] Battle of Stones River
[d04s000] The Battle of Stones River or Second Battle of Murfreesboro, was fought from December 31, 1862, to January 2, 1863, in Middle Tennessee, as the culmination of the Stones River Campaign in the Western Theater of the American Civil War.
[d04s001] Of the major battles of the Civil War, Stones River had the highest percentage of casualties on both sides.
[d04s002] Although the battle itself was inconclusive, the Union Army's repulse of two Confederate attacks and the subsequent Confederate withdrawal were a much-needed boost to Union morale after the defeat at the Battle of Fredericksburg, and it dashed Confederate aspirations for control of Middle Tennessee.

[d03p003] Umba River (Tanzania)
[d03s003] Just before the Umba flows into the Indian Ocean, it crosses the border to Kenya.
[d03s004] The mouth itself marks the most eastern point on the border between Tanzania and Kenya, which was largely made in a straight line to the northwest towards Lake Victoria in the 19th Century.
[d03s005] On the upper reaches of the river in the mid-1960s rich deposits of precious stones, including sapphires and Spessartine, were discovered.
